name: Cookie Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
Get Ready for the Cookie Run! 🍪✨

Join us for the Cookie Run It's not just a race, it's an adventure filled with delicious cookies for those who run with a sweet reward in mind!
You’ll love the shirt we send you. Set a goal, bring a friend, and join this super fun 5K/10K/13.1 Half-Marathon! 

Forget the massive, impersonal race-day crowds. We keep things small, personal, and local, so every run feels less like a number and more like a memory. Whether it's a 5K, 10K, half-marathon, or virtual run, you'll get the warmth of a hometown event.
 

Overview:
Spots sell out FAST! We close each wave the moment it fills. Once a wave sells out, you can grab the virtual run option or join the waitlist.

This is a smaller, private group run with a capped field per wave so it never feels crowded and you're never just a bib number.
All paces and ages welcome (under 18 with a guardian) - run it, walk it, however you like!
There's no gear, no setup, no fuss - just you, the course, and our coordinators cheering you on in a relaxed, stress-free setting.
When you sign up, you're not just registering for a race - you're getting real support toward your fitness goals, plus an invite to join one of our local run clubs to keep the momentum going.
 
Timing:
Optional! Track your own time via Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, or similar, then submit it through our easy online form to get posted.  Or just ask a coordinator to help time you.
No timing chips - this is about progress, not pressure.
 
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-shirt (shipped to your address - U.S. only)
- Finisher's medal
- Virtual Training Run (emailed to you a month before your run)
- Online results & certificate of completion
- Invitation to join a local running club
- NEW: Upgrade to a lightweight, moisture-wicking technical shirt for just $5 more
 
Packet Pickup?
Skip It. No lines, no hassle - your swag ships straight to your door. (Double check your full U.S. mailing address, including apartment number, when you register as your shirt is sent to this address!) Race bibs are simply handed out on race day.
 
When Will My Swag Arrive?
Your shirt will arrive at your mailing address the week of your race.
 
Signing Up Last Minute? (Within 2 Weeks of the Race)
No problem - just note that shipping may not catch up in time, so your shirt could arrive after race day. No worries, though: wear whatever you like and come run with us anyway!
 
When Will I Receive the Course Map and Details?
We'll send final participant info by the Wednesday before race day with all the details and course maps.
 
Wave Times  (Once you've registered, use your confirmation number to reserve a wave here)
Wave A: 7:30 AM
Wave B: 8:00 AM
Wave C: 8:30 AM
 
Running Late?
Jump in when you arrive - our coordinators stay on-site for 3 hours after the first wave. Times may be subject to change depending on seasons, please check your participant info email!
Got more questions? Check our FAQ.
 
Virtual Run Option
Prefer to run on your own time? Our Virtual Run includes a digital training pack to keep you on track. Run it whenever, wherever, with any tracking device you like (optional) — then send your results to info@thebestraces.com to claim your medal.
 
Race Bundle
Sign up for multiple races and save with a bundle discount.
 
Sponsorships & Promoting Your Business
Want to put your business in front of our community? We'd love to feature you as a sponsor. Learn more.
 
Team Glo Volunteers
Love helping people cross finish lines? Join our volunteer team and help bring these community runs to life. Sign up here.
 
Be Part of the Journey
Discover our charity initiatives at https://www.thebestraces.com/runforothers/.
Got a mission that helps people around the world? Let us help you fundraise at no cost to you.
 

Your Race | Your Journey | Your Story

name: Cougar Mountain Trail Run Series (October)
description:
Welcome to the 2025 edition of the Cougar Mountain Trail Run Series, put on by Seattle Running Club and Northwest Trail Runs. Our events support King County Parks, with a portion of every entry going to KC Parks. 

 

OCTOBER'S RACE ONLY - COSTUME CONTEST/CHALLENGE: The October Cougar Mountain races fall a few days before Halloween so let's see who can get into the spirit and run some trails in costume.  UPDATE - there will be an award for best costume (any distance) and best group costume (any distance).  Winners will receive a gift certificate and a unique trophy from Otter Pawz Lazer.  

 

October 7.6-Mile Cross Country // Cougar Cup - The 7.6-Mile Race is a team race - individuals are still eligible to run the 7.6 mile race for podium awards but not the Cougar Cup. The Cougar Cup is open to any team, group or club. In order to participate in the event, teams must sign-up the morning of the race and declare who is on the team. All team members must sign a waiver and list an emergency contact who is not racing. All teams must pay the entry fee of $180. This is a mixed team event and 2 women must score for each team. Teams can consist of 4-6 people with 4 people scoring and 2 displacing. There will be a cup handed out to the winning team. Team captains need to fill out this survey, and communicate information to other team members.

 

Events

May 10: 5.1 Miles & 10.8 Miles 
9 AM start for all races, 12:00 PM cut-off (~16:40 pace for 10.8 miles)

June 14: 5K, 8.2 Miles & 14.5 Miles
9 AM start for all races, 1:00 PM cut-off (~16:35 pace for 14.5 miles)

July 12: 5K, 10.8 Miles & 19.5 Miles
9 AM start for all race, 2:30 PM cut-off (~16:55 pace for 19.5 miles)

August 9: 5K, 14.5 Miles & 26.2 Miles
8:30 AM start for the 14.5 and 26.2, 9 AM start for the 5K, 4 PM cut-off (~17:10 pace for the marathon)

October 31: 5K, 7.6 Mile Cross Country, 19.5 Miles & 50K
8 AM start for the 19.5 and 50K (7 AM early start will be available), 9 AM start for 7.6 Miles and Cross Country event, 9:30 AM start for 5K, 5 PM Cut-off (~17:25 pace for 50K, ~19:30 pace for early start)

Event-day registration is available starting at 7:00AM

 

Series:
Short Series: May 5.1 Miles, June 8.2 Miles, July 10.8 Miles & August 14.5 Miles
Long Series: May 10.8 Miles, June 14.5 Miles, July 19.5 Miles, August 26.2 Miles
Top overall Man, Woman, and Nonbinary runners based on cumulative time will receive an award and free entry into next year's series.

If you are a Seattle Running Club member and want to use your membership discount on the short or long series, please signup for the series using the short pass or long pass and then send the race director (races@seattlerunningclub.org) an email with your SRC member number. You will receive a partial refund within 5 business days. For all other races, please use the coupon code given to Seattle Running Club members--if you do not know the member code, please email the race director with your member number to get the code). 

Online registration closes at 11:59 PM PDT the Wednesday before each event. We will have day-of registration if you did not register in time.

 

Reasons to Sign Up:
1) Well-marked trails with distances that are perfect for all experience levels
2) Community: Surround yourself with members of the trail-running community
3) Post-race food and libations, including beer provided by one of our Club's partner stores, Flying Lion Brewery
4) Raise money for King County Parks: $15/runner donated to the parks

 

DID YOU KNOW

That the August Cougar Mountain Trail Run Series 14.5-Mile Race will serve as the USATF PNTF Open and Masters Trail Championships? There is prize money for this event! Additionally, the 5k race serves as the first ever  USATF PNTF Youth Trail Championship!  This was put together by the PNW Youth Trail Project and is the final race of the inaugural PNW YTP Race Series. Both championship races require participants to be members of the USATF organization - you'll need your USATF member number when registering for a championship race. For more information about how to become a USATF member, click here. Please note - the championship races are optional. Anyone can run the 5k or 14.5mi races without being in the USATF PNTF championship. However, if you want that extra shot of competition, prize money (14.5 mile only), and possible bragging rights, become a USATF member today!

 

Safety Guidelines
If you have had COVID-19 symptoms in the last 10 days or have known exposure to someone with COVID-19, please skip this race.

 

We Run on Native Land
We acknowledge that our running opportunities are built on the purposeful removal of Native peoples, who have been the stewards of Seattle-area lands for thousands of years. Thus, we accept our ethical responsibility for the ongoing stewardship of the land and purposeful support of Native neighbors, colleagues, businesses, and tribes. The Muckleshoot, Duwamish, Stillaguamish, Snoqualmie, and Coast Salish are the Natives of the lands we run on.

 

Photo Consent
I understand and accept that photos/videos/illustrations may be taken of me and/or my personal property while attending/participating in Seattle Running Club (SRC) events/functions. I acknowledge and agree that such photographs or other illustrations may be used by SRC and its related entities for advertising and promotional purposes in any medium, without compensation to me. If you would prefer not to have a particular photo used, let us know and we’ll do our best to remove it right away.


A Greener Event: Cup Free

Again, this year the series is continuing to reduce the amount of trash created during the event. We ask that runners bring a refillable water container with them on the trail to use at aid stations along the way and post-race. Our friends at Seven Hills Running, Fleet Feet Sports Seattle (Capitol Hill and Ballard), and Snoqualmie Running have a variety of hydration products.

 

Race Information

Thanks to runners like you, the Cougar Mountain Trail Run Series has raised over $250,000 for King County Parks and contributed hundreds of hours of trail work. Join Seattle Running Club and Northwest Trail Runs in carrying this legacy forward and making this 21st annual event bigger and better than ever!

Just 15 minutes from Seattle, King County's Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park is one of the most popular training grounds for area trail runners and the Seattle Running Club. The course builds on itself throughout the series and brings runners through a lush forest of fern-lined single-track trails, over hills and along marshes and wetland habitats. This is a great series to supplement the training regime for a fall marathon or ultra. Cougar Mountain features rolling hills, a few moderate climbs, and a few steep but short inclines.

 

The summer Short Series and Long Series races are held on the 2nd Saturday of May, June, July, and August. The Fall races are held on the last Sunday in October. Series standings are updated after each month's races and everyone competing in each successive distance is eligible for Series awards. There is a participant cap and the races tend to sell out, so register early! There are NO REFUNDS!

 

Seattle Running Club Discount
If you are a member of Seattle Running Club, you should have received a discount code for 20% in the newsletter. You will need to provide your member number if you use this discount code. There are also many other discounts and benefits for being a member of the Seattle Running Club. 

 

No Dogs
As much as we love our four-legged friends and family members, we are not allowed to have dogs at our event.

Very important announcement: Dogs are not allowed on the course due to USATF Sanctioning and Insurance Requirements. Despite the park's policy on dogs on leashes being acceptable, USATF has determined dogs on course cause a potentially unsafe environment for participants and spectators. We love our dogs and remember Scott's dog Jack attending Cougar races for years and years. But we want to continue hosting races for years to come and need to abide by the USATF rules.

 

Awards
The top 3 Men, Women, and Nonbinary Runners in each event will receive a podium prize. 
Our August 14.5-Mile Race will serve as the USATF PNTF championships. There will be prize money for this event. Prize money will be announced as we get closer to this event.

If you would prefer not to have a particular photo used, let us know and we’ll do our best to remove it right away.


A Greener Event: Cup Free

Again, this year the series is continuing to reduce the amount of trash created during the event. We ask that runners bring a refillable water container with them on the trail to use at aid stations along the way and post-race. Our friends at Seven Hills Running, Fleet Feet Sports Seattle (Capitol Hill and Ballard), and Snoqualmie Running have a variety of hydration products.

 

Race Information

Thanks to runners like you, the Cougar Mountain Trail Run Series has raised over $250,000 for King County Parks and contributed hundreds of hours of trail work. Join Seattle Running Club and Northwest Trail Runs in carrying this legacy forward and making this 21st annual event bigger and better than ever!

Just 15 minutes from Seattle, King County's Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park is one of the most popular training grounds for area trail runners and the Seattle Running Club. The course builds on itself throughout the series and brings runners through a lush forest of fern-lined single-track trails, over hills and along marshes and wetland habitats. This is a great series to supplement the training regime for a fall marathon or ultra. Cougar Mountain features rolling hills, a few moderate climbs, and a few steep but short inclines.

 

The summer Short Series and Long Series races are held on the 2nd Saturday of May, June, July, and August. The Fall races are held on the last Sunday in October. Series standings are updated after each month's races and everyone competing in each successive distance is eligible for Series awards. There is a participant cap and the races tend to sell out, so register early! There are NO REFUNDS!

 

Seattle Running Club Discount
If you are a member of Seattle Running Club, you should have received a discount code for 20% in the newsletter. You will need to provide your member number if you use this discount code. There are also many other discounts and benefits for being a member of the Seattle Running Club. 

 

No Dogs
As much as we love our four-legged friends and family members, we are not allowed to have dogs at our event.

Very important announcement: Dogs are not allowed on the course due to USATF Sanctioning and Insurance Requirements. Despite the park's policy on dogs on leashes being acceptable, USATF has determined dogs on course cause a potentially unsafe environment for participants and spectators. We love our dogs and remember Scott's dog Jack attending Cougar races for years and years. But we want to continue hosting races for years to come and need to abide by the USATF rules.

 

Awards
The top 3 Men, Women, and Nonbinary Runners in each event will receive a podium prize. 
Our August 14.5-Mile Race will serve as the USATF PNTF championships. There will be prize money for this event. Prize money will be announced as we get closer to this event.

name: Couve Clover Run
description:
FLASH SALE PRICING GOOD THROUGH APRIL 12th.

RUN, GIVE BACK & PARTY on Vancouver’s Waterfront!
Join us for the 13th Annual Couve Clover Run and celebrate in your festive green while running or walking 1- miler, 3, 7 or 10 miles along an extremely fast and scenic course to support local charities! We will make you earn your post-event party, but it will be off the charts hosted by Why Racing Events and other downtown Vancouver Pubs & Breweries.

We believe this is one of the prettiest courses in the Northwest! We’ve designed the 1-miler, 3 miles, Lucky 7 miles and 10-mile courses to take you through some of the most scenic areas of Vancouver and it really highlights our wonderful community including historic Officer’s Row, Fort Vancouver, the Columbian Riverfront, and more. The course is mostly flat with a couple of short hills.

name: Defiance 50K / 30K / 15K
description:
The Defiance 50K, 30K, 15K & 3-Person 50K Relay is a scenic race that takes runners through the beautiful trails of Point Defiance, with over 700 acres of old growth forests and panoramic views of the Puget Sound. 

The course is approximately a 9.75 mi / 15.7 km loop through old growth forest. Runners of the 15K and each team member of the 3-Person 50K Relay will complete this loop once, 30K runners will run the loop twice and 50K runners will run the loop three times. Each loop will take you through the Start/Finish area at Owen Beach.

On the course, you will see sweeping views of the Puget Sound, run on soft trails beneath 500-year-old giant cedars and firs in one of the top 20 urban parks in the United States.

The course is mostly single track and typically dry mid-October. Train for some hills but the course is 95% run-able.

name: Dia de los Muertos - Hockinson AAA Booster 5K Run/Walk & Kids Costume Mile #RunningTheRaceTogether
description:
Community Event

The Hockinson High School AAA Boosters and the Hockinson High School Cross Country Team invite you to join Us for the Hockinson Community 5K Run/Walk! Looking for a fun way to stay active and spend time with family? Join us on November 2nd at Hockinson Meadows Community Park for the 5K Run/Walk! The event will start and finish at the picnic shelter/playground area, making it easy to relax and enjoy the park after the race. Bring the whole family and make it a day to remember. We hope to see you there!

Schedule of Events:

9:00 - 10:00 AM - Pre-Race pickup - Please arrive a minimum of 30-45 minutes before your race time for race Bib and any pre ordered T-shirts or Medals.

10:00 AM - Start of the Kids Mile - Arrive early for Pre-Race pickup and have your kiddo ready for their 1-mile run/walk. The High School Cross Country Runners will be on site to run with the kids and make this a fun event.

10:30 AM - Start of the 5K run/walk - Arrive early for Pre-Race pickup and get ready for your event.

Take photos with your T-shirt, medal and/or costume and Share your Race with Us!

We would love to hear about your experience!  Share your photos to Facebook and Instagram #RunningTheRaceTogether

name: Emerald City Open
description:
If you are a NCAA college coach you need to register your team on Direct Athletics so we can get the TFFRS number: https://www.directathletics.com/meets/xc/28770.html Non-NCAA colleges please use Run Sign Up. 

If you are registering individually and not with a team, use the unattached team option in the teams drop down box.

Emerald City Open was started by the UW in 1989. In the mid-1990s, with the advent of the Sundodger Classic, Seattle University was given the meet to host. Club Northwest started helping SU in 1997, and took over in 2017. Since then, we’re proud to continue providing a competitive early-season cross country meet in Seattle, for both collegiate and post collegiate teams!

The course is located at Upper Woodland Park in Seattle, WA. There is one 2000m loop run three times for the 6k and four for the 8k. The start line is in the grassy clearing, approximately here.

The meet is free to Club Northwest members. You can enter as a team or as an individual; we will publish all individual results with team affiliations. Open individuals will be charged $20 and teams will be charged $200. A team is considered a single-gendered group of 5-12 participants; teams larger than 12 will be charged an extra $20 per participant. The Community 2k is $5, and open to kids and adults.

Packet pickup will be available at the tent at the start/finish lines. At pickup time, we will ask you to declare your team and scratch any non-competing runners. Race day registration is available as well.

name: F Cancer 5k Run & Walk
description: A family friendly 5k run or walk through Point Defiance where everyone who’s been affected in any way by cancer can come together and feel less alone. The net proceeds after event expenses will be donated 50/50 to Fred Hutch Cancer Center and Tacoma Multicare Home and Hospice. Our goal is to keep event expenses at a minimum so we can maximize the donations towards these 2 organizations who have helped our amazing mom, Sweet Caroline, through her 2nd and final battle with breast cancer.

name: Fall - Mud Mountain Dam Marathon & Half Marathon
description:
Start Planning Now for Your Next Boston Qualifier!

Take on a beautiful, fully paved downhill course with no tunnel, no dirt, and no BQ downhill penalty.

Full Marathon
The Marathon starts at Mud Mountain Dam, high above the Carbon River at an elevation of approximately 1,400 feet.

From there, runners will follow a fully paved downhill route through picturesque farmland and forest, tracing the scenic Carbon River before finishing at the McMillin Farm Collective at approximately 128 feet.

That's a net elevation loss of about 1,200 feet—a fast, scenic course built for a memorable Boston Qualifier!

Half Marathon
The Half Marathon starts in the scenic town of South Prairie at approximately 467 feet and follows a gradual downhill route along the paved Foothills Rail Trail.

Runners will wind through farmland and forest alongside the Carbon River before finishing at the McMillin Farm Collective, at approximately 128 feet.

The course features a net elevation loss of 339 feet.

A Finish Line Worth Celebrating!
We've got a brand-new finish line just down the road from the McMillin Bridge, and we're making it a destination!

After crossing the finish line, stick around and celebrate with:

Brewhouse
Food trucks
Hot & Cold plunge pools

It's going to be a finish line to remember!

Beautiful course. Fast downhill miles. Fully paved. No tunnel. No dirt. No BQ penalty.

There’s no excuse not to do the dam thing!

name: FORGE
description:
FORGE Backyard Ultra

  • Run a 4.167-mile loop every hour on the hour for 12 hours
  • Complete all 12 loops and you'll have run 50 miles
  • Miss the start or don’t finish in time? Your FORGE is over.

Everyone is celebrated but we will have winners:

Top Male and Female awards:
1. fastest total time- Trophy and $500.

2. final loop winner- trophy and free registration for next years FORGE  

Space is limited. Secure your spot today.

Date: June 6, 2026

Location: Trails and dirt roads south of Swinomish Casino, Skagit County, WA

Start Time: 7:00 AM

All Runners will receive:

  • FORGE running hat
  • FORGE hoodie
  • FORGEd custom medal(finisher prize)
  • Day of race food and snacks, Tailwind Nutrition Endurance Fuel.
  •  
FORGE is a race built around a unique and growing format known as the "backyard ultra." Unlike traditional races where runners aim for a set distance or time, backyard ultras follow a simple but demanding structure: runners complete a 4.167-mile loop every hour, on the hour. Whatever time remains after finishing a lap becomes their rest period before starting again at the top of the next hour. This continues until the event reaches its predetermined duration—in FORGE’s case, 12 hours.
The format is gaining popularity worldwide because it removes the pressure of speed and replaces it with a test of endurance, pacing, and mental toughness. Fast runners and steady runners line up together every hour. Everyone starts at the same time, and the race unfolds differently for each participant. Some will aim for a personal-best distance, while others will push to complete all 12 laps.
One of the most unique aspects of this style of racing is the community it creates. The time between laps—when runners gather, recover, and prepare for the next start—becomes a shared experience. Conversations happen. Encouragement is exchanged. Whether you’re completing your first backyard-style event or chasing a new personal milestone, you’re not doing it alone.

 

At its core, FORGE is about stepping into a challenge and discovering what you’re capable of. There’s no finish line waiting for you at a set distance—just another lap, another opportunity to push forward. It’s an event designed to be hard, but also to be welcoming, rewarding, and deeply memorable.

name: Fowl Fun Run 5K & 10K
description:
Join us for the 48th Annual Fowl Fun Run!

Run the Valley with Skagit Runners

We offer two distances: a 5K run/walk and a 10K run. Both courses are run on flat, low-traffic farm roads in the Skagit Valley.

Stay for food, refreshments and for the opportunity to win a pumpkin pie!
 
Free Kids' Half-Mile Run
The half-mile kids' run for those 8 years and under starts promptly at 9:15 a.m. This fun run is free, but children must be registered in person by 9:00 a.m.

Race day schedule
8 am - 8:25 am: Volunteers set up


8:25 am - 9:30 am: Day of race registration (NOT GUARANTEED A FINISHERS MEDAL)


8:25 am - 9:30 am: Check in for pre-registered participants


9:15 am: 1/2 mile kids' run start


10 am: 5K & 10K start


10:05 am: Turkey begins the 10K


Noon: Both courses close


Packet Pick-Up: 1-5pm Friday, November 13th at Skagit Running Company (724 S 1st St, Mount Vernon, WA 98273)

 

Day of Race Registration: Please arrive early if you plan to register on the morning of the race.

Price increase $40 5k and $50 10k.

(NOT GUARANTEED A FINISHERS MEDAL)


Day of Race Packet Pick-up: Pre-registered participants may pick up their bib numbers starting at 8:25 a.m. on race morning.


Food and Refreshments: Traditional pumpkin pie available as a post-race treat!


Awards: Every participant will receive a finishers medal. Special awards will be given to the top 3 male and female finishers.


Beat the Turkey! Tom Turkey will be starting the 10K five minutes after the gun. Finish the 10K ahead of him and receive a special award at the finish line!

name: Frosty Moss Relay
description:
Welcome to the Green Season on the Olympic Peninsula of Washington State
Towering evergreens. Endless moss and ferns. Miles of waterfront. Snowcapped mountains. Need a cure for gray-season blues? Frosty Moss has you covered.

Pavement + Trail Runners Unite
From the Sol Duc River to Sequim Bay, the 80-mile Frosty Moss course follows the paved Olympic Discovery Trail and the singletrack Adventure Route. The 30-mile Mini Moss course begins at Ediz Hook in Port Angeles and end at Sequim Bay.

Celebrate After the Race
As if your day wasn’t epic enough, 7 Cedars Resort is ready to help you celebrate. They will host hot food, cold drinks, awards and fun after the race.

name: Girlfriends Run
description:
THE GIRLFRIENDS AND PINK BRIGADE HAVE RAISED OVER $900,000 OVER THE LAST 19 YEARS!
The 20th Annual Girlfriends Run offers a Half Marathon, 10K & 6K designed specifically for women to get together to do something good for themselves and to help support a very important women’s cause. GREAT NEWS! Girlfriends is honored to have a title sponsor and we are thrilled to announce our Title Sponsor for this event- Vancouver Clinic.  

We started this event to honor and support one of our BFFs, Joleen Skarberg, who was diagnosed with Breast Cancer and continues to run it every year with her daughters, sisters, nieces, cousins and girlfriends! Watch for her – she’ll be wearing #1!

About half the gals run, half walk and many do a combination of running and walking. It doesn’t matter how you get to the finish line, as long as you get there!

Are you a male who would like to support this race?  You CAN join two ways.  One – by becoming a Pink Brigade Guy and raise donations for Pink Lemonade Project.  Two – by being part of a corporate team.  We love to see everyone support this race.

GREAT NEWS! Girlfriends is honored to have a title sponsor and we are thrilled to announce our Title Sponsor for this event- Vancouver Clinic.  

We started this event to honor and support one of our BFFs, Joleen Skarberg, who was diagnosed with Breast Cancer and continues to run it every year with her daughters, sisters, nieces, cousins and girlfriends! Watch for her – she’ll be wearing #1!

About half the gals run, half walk and many do a combination of running and walking. It doesn’t matter how you get to the finish line, as long as you get there!

Are you a male who would like to support this race?  You CAN join two ways.  One – by becoming a Pink Brigade Guy and raise donations for Pink Lemonade Project.  Two – by being part of a corporate team.  We love to see everyone support this race.

name: Girlfriends Triathlon & Fitness Festival
description:
GIRLFRIEND, YES, YOU CAN CROSS THE FINISH LINE!

This 29th Annual Girlfriends All-Women’s Triathlon & Fitness Festival at a beautiful venue along the Columbia River offers something for everyone so rally your girlfriends, train together and then cross the finish line with your best girls!

It is one of the most scenic areas with views of the Columbia River, Mt. Hood, Mt. St. Helens and Vancouver Lake. The course is flat and fast with a down-current swim close to the shore so perfect for a 1st time Triathlon or Multisport event! Kids Triathlon and a Sunset 5K/10K are scheduled Friday night and Co-Ed events on Saturday so make a whole weekend of it for the whole family.

PARKING IS INCLUDED IN REGISTATION FEES.

name: Give NCW Turkey Trot
description:
The Give NCW Turkey Trot brings our community together on Thanksgiving morning to celebrate generosity in action.

Hosted by the Community Foundation of NCW, this annual tradition launches Give NCW, a community-wide giving movement that supports nearly 100 nonprofit organizations serving North Central Washington. Thanks to the generosity of our event sponsors, 100% of registration fees are donated to the Give to All Fund and shared among participating nonprofits.

Runners can choose from a timed 10K Run/Walk, timed 5K Run/Walk, or a free Kids Fun Run. The 5K and 10K courses follow the scenic Apple Capital Loop Trail along the Wenatchee riverfront, while the Kids Fun Run takes place near the grounds of Pybus Public Market.

Whether you're chasing a personal best, walking with family and friends, cheering on your kids, or showing up in your favorite Thanksgiving costume, the Turkey Trot is a fun and welcoming way to start the holiday. Together, we're kicking off a season of generosity that supports and strengthens our communities throughout North Central Washington.

Special thanks to our Presenting Sponsor, Wenatchee Valley Medical Group, and our Gold Sponsors, Cordell Neher & Company and Cashmere Valley Bank, whose generosity makes this event possible.

We are also grateful to the Pybus Market Charitable Foundation for hosting the event and opening Pybus Public Market on Thanksgiving Day to welcome participants, families, volunteers, and spectators. Crunch Pak and Mela Coffee will once again provide in-kind donations of delicious apple snacks, coffee, and hot chocolate.

Gather your friends, family, coworkers, teammates, or neighbors and come dressed to impress. Giving Cards will be awarded to our favorite group costumes and can be redeemed to support participating nonprofits through Give NCW.

Strollers and leashed dogs are welcome.

name: Gobble Gobble 5K & 10K
description:
Kick start your Thanksgiving morning with Puyallup’s own Gobble Gobble 5K & 10K! Gather your friends and family and run/walk this festive community tradition starting and finishing at Pierce College Puyallup.

Enjoy a fun and scenic chip-timed course while celebrating Thanksgiving with the local running and walking community. 

Registration Includes:
• Chip Timed Event
• Finisher Medal
• Commemorative Race Bib
• After-event Snacks
• Entry into Prize Giveaways

We will also be collecting donations for the Stahl Jr. High food pantry. Suggested donation items include single-serving microwavable mac & cheese cups, single-serving breakfast cereal, granola bars, protein bars, microwavable soups, and Pop-Tarts. Help us support local students and families this Thanksgiving season.

Whether you’re looking to burn a few calories before the big feast, create lasting memories with family and friends, or continue your holiday running tradition, the Gobble Gobble 5K & 10K is the perfect way to start your Thanksgiving Day.  The Gobble Gobble 5K & 10K is proudly becoming a Puyallup Thanksgiving tradition!

name: Gobbler 5K, 10K & 13.1M at Olympia, WA (46)
description:
US Road Running Races

US Road Running races are built for runners and walkers who like friendly, low-pressure race days with just enough competition to keep things exciting. Our events are local, welcoming, and easy to jump into, whether you are chasing a PR, collecting another themed medal, working toward series points, or just getting outside with good people.

Most races are small enough to feel personal but organized enough to feel official. You can expect a clear course, helpful race staff, finisher medals, results, and a relaxed community feel. Bring your fast shoes, your steady walking pace, your favorite running buddy, or your best “I signed up for this on purpose” smile. We will be glad to see you at the start line.

A quick race-day note: because many US Road Running events are small local races, we normally have one or two staff members at each race. EMS is not stationed on site, and water stations are limited to the finish area at the end of each lap and at the race finish. Please plan for the weather, bring anything you may want between laps, and check in with race staff if you need help.

View Race Course, Results, and Race Information on the US Road Running race page.

Our events are local, welcoming, and easy to jump into, whether you are chasing a PR, collecting another themed medal, working toward series points, or just getting outside with good people.

Most races are small enough to feel personal but organized enough to feel official. You can expect a clear course, helpful race staff, finisher medals, results, and a relaxed community feel. Bring your fast shoes, your steady walking pace, your favorite running buddy, or your best “I signed up for this on purpose” smile. We will be glad to see you at the start line.

A quick race-day note: because many US Road Running events are small local races, we normally have one or two staff members at each race. EMS is not stationed on site, and water stations are limited to the finish area at the end of each lap and at the race finish. Please plan for the weather, bring anything you may want between laps, and check in with race staff if you need help.

name: Green Lake Sole 5K Run
description:
Put on your running shoes and be ready to run your "sole" out at the Green Lake Sole 5K Run.  This 5k is partnered with YouthCare.  Proceeds will go towards buying shoes for Seattle youth experiencing homelessness.  As you put your heart and "sole" into this race, you are also putting soles on the feet of local Seattle youth experiencing homeless.  Join us on October 17th, 2026, to participate in a fun, active community event, while also helping local Seattle youth experiencing homelessness.  

 

Race Info: 5k race/walk on October 17th, 2026, starting at 10:00 am and cutting off at 11:00 am.  Check in will begin at 9:15 am and end at 9:58 am, awards will begin at 11:00 am.

 

Location: Basketball courts at East Green Lake Beach by the Green Lake Playfields (Google Map Link).  Parking is available at the East Green Lake Beach, and if that parking is full, there are plenty of places to park around the neighborhood. 

 

Route Info:  Route begins by the Green Lake basketball courts and loops around Green Lake before turning and going around the outside of the Green Lake playfields and finishing at the basketball courts (route map below). 

 

Race Categories: There will be male, female, and non-binary categories, and within each of those categories medals will be given to the top 3 finishers of the 1–14-year-old, 15–20-year-old, 20-40-year-old, and the 40 and older categories.  Medals will also be given to the top 3 finishers in the male, female, and non-binary categories.  Top 3 finishers only receive medal for overall placement, not age group placement.

 

Timing: Race is hand timed (no electronic/professional timing- online results will still be provided). 

 

About Fundraiser: This race is partnered with YouthCare. YouthCare serves homeless youth ages 12-24 through four different shelters in Seattle and through job training. All dollars raised will go to YouthCare to help support and empower youth experiencing homelessness.  Specifically, donations will enable youth to purchase shoes.  Youth Care's mission is to end youth homelessness and to ensure that young people are valued for who they are and empowered to achieve their potential.  Through entering and supporting this race, you are helping empower and support local Seattle youth experiencing homelessness. 

 

Weather: Given that it is October in Seattle expect cold weather and likely rain.  

 

FAQS:

Are Dogs Allowed?

Dogs will not be allowed due to event insurance.

Are Strollers Allowed?

Strollers will also not be allowed due to event insurance.

 

Other Info:

Route Map

 

Donations:  If you have the means, extra donations would be greatly appreciated and would provide YouthCare with more money to provide Seattle youth experiencing homelessness with shoes.   

 

Refund Policy:  Green Lake Sole 5K Run will not provide any refunds.

name: Halloween Trick or Trot Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
🎃 👻 Trick or Trot! 👻 🎃
Run in our annual Halloween Run, where healthy fitness meets frightful fun! We'll even give you some free Halloween candy after your run! Find a friend, set a goal, and join this unique 5K, 10K, or 13.1 Half-Marathon run!

Forget the massive, impersonal race-day crowds. We keep things small, personal, and local, so every run feels less like a number and more like a memory. Whether it's a 5K, 10K, half-marathon, or virtual run, you'll get the warmth of a hometown event.
 

Overview:
Spots sell out FAST! We close each wave the moment it fills. Once a wave sells out, you can grab the virtual run option or join the waitlist.

This is a smaller, private group run with a capped field per wave so it never feels crowded and you're never just a bib number.
All paces and ages welcome (under 18 with a guardian) - run it, walk it, however you like!
There's no gear, no setup, no fuss - just you, the course, and our coordinators cheering you on in a relaxed, stress-free setting.
When you sign up, you're not just registering for a race - you're getting real support toward your fitness goals, plus an invite to join one of our local run clubs to keep the momentum going.
 
Timing:
Optional! Track your own time via Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, or similar, then submit it through our easy online form to get posted.  Or just ask a coordinator to help time you.
No timing chips - this is about progress, not pressure.
 
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-shirt (shipped to your address - U.S. only)
- Finisher's medal
- Virtual Training Run (emailed to you a month before your run)
- Online results & certificate of completion
- Invitation to join a local running club
- NEW: Upgrade to a lightweight, moisture-wicking technical shirt for just $5 more
 
Packet Pickup?
Skip It. No lines, no hassle - your swag ships straight to your door. (Double check your full U.S. mailing address, including apartment number, when you register as your shirt is sent to this address!) Race bibs are simply handed out on race day.

name: Harvest Hustle 5k/10k
description:
CELEBRATING COMMUNITY, MOVEMENT, AND LOCAL ATHLETICS

The Harvest Hustle 5K / 10K is a community race through Othello created to bring runners, walkers, families, local businesses, and supporters together during the fall season in the Columbia Basin.

Hosted by Pillar Fitness and Les Schwab, this event supports the Othello High School Cross Country team while giving the community a fun and active way to celebrate local athletics, health, and hometown pride.

A RUN FOR EVERY PACE

Whether you are a serious runner looking to compete, a casual jogger challenging yourself, or a group of friends simply wanting to get outside and move, this event is built to be welcoming, energetic, and fun.

Both the 5K and 10K courses will take participants through unique routes around Othello, including portions that highlight our local city parks and community spaces. The start and finish area will include local vendors, supporters, and a community atmosphere for participants and spectators to enjoy.

ROOTED IN THE COLUMBIA BASIN

Othello sits in the heart of the Columbia Basin, surrounded by farm fields, irrigation canals, open skies, and the harvest season that helps define our region. Harvest Hustle was created with that identity in mind — a fall event that reflects the hardworking, family-centered, agriculture-rooted spirit of our community.

From the fields that surround us to the students we are supporting, this race is about showing up for something bigger than ourselves.

SUPPORTING OTHELLO CROSS COUNTRY

Proceeds from the event will help support the Othello High School Cross Country team, giving local student-athletes additional encouragement, resources, and community backing as they continue to train, compete, and represent Othello.

Every registration helps support young runners who are learning discipline, endurance, teamwork, and pride in representing their school and community.

name: Haunted 5K, 10K & 13.1M at Camas, WA (41)
description:
US Road Running Races

US Road Running races are built for runners and walkers who like friendly, low-pressure race days with just enough competition to keep things exciting. Our events are local, welcoming, and easy to jump into, whether you are chasing a PR, collecting another themed medal, working toward series points, or just getting outside with good people.

Most races are small enough to feel personal but organized enough to feel official. You can expect a clear course, helpful race staff, finisher medals, results, and a relaxed community feel. Bring your fast shoes, your steady walking pace, your favorite running buddy, or your best “I signed up for this on purpose” smile. We will be glad to see you at the start line.

A quick race-day note: because many US Road Running events are small local races, we normally have one or two staff members at each race. EMS is not stationed on site, and water stations are limited to the finish area at the end of each lap and at the race finish. Please plan for the weather, bring anything you may want between laps, and check in with race staff if you need help.

View Race Course, Results, and Race Information on the US Road Running race page.

name: Haunted Hustle 5K
description:
Ready to have a "spooky" good run?!  Come join us for our first ever Haunted Hustle 5K!  Run, Walk, or Skip a 5K (3.1mi) on Saturday, October 31st.  

Costumes... costumes... costumes!  Want to run in your costume?  Please do!! We will be giving out prizes for best costumes.

 

Support our local Oakesdale Nighthawk Track & Field Teams!  All race proceeds go to support these programs.

name: Haunted Hustle 5K & 10K
description:
Price Reduction!

We are sold out of 2026 medals so we are reducing the price to $35 for the 5K and $40 for the 10K.  You will be receiving our Haunted Hustle 2025 medal.

 

Costumes on. Spirits high. Let’s get haunted.
We’re back from the beyond! 👻

The Haunted Hustle 5K & 10K Run/Walk is back for another Halloween tradition in Puyallup — and this one is all about fun, costumes, friends, and a little spooky adventure.

This is a non-timed, family-friendly event, so whether you’re a serious runner, a casual walker, a costume enthusiast, or simply looking for a fun way to kick off Halloween, there’s a place for you at the Haunted Hustle.  And yes… costumes are highly encouraged. 🎃

CHOOSE YOUR HAUNT
Take your pick:

👻 5K Run/Walk
💀 10K Run/Walk

Both distances start at Clarks Creek South in Puyallup and take participants on a memorable journey through the cemetery, with a mix of sidewalks and off-the-beaten-path sections.

It’s not your typical neighborhood stroll. It’s a Haunted Hustle. 👻

name: Heroes Walk, 5K & 10k Fun Run
description:
CHECK IN BEGINS AT 9:00 AM 


Empowering Communities and Fortifying Families to End Veteran Suicide and Strengthen our Heroes to Lead their Communities.

HONOR HEROES - FORTIFY FAMILIES - CELEBRATE FREEDOM

Walk in support of veterans to choose LIFE. The enemy did not have victory in war, and will not win in the day to day battle for our veteran’s lives. Together we can end veteran suicide and fortify families after service. Live life abundantly with a community that hears, sees and recognizes the sacrifices of our HEROES. Family and supporters of our veterans are encouraged to join. Let’s gather in a big way to show the love and support of our veterans and the USA. 

The circle of return from military service to civilian life is a personal and community process. Join a community wide celebration and resources fair as we help veterans and families make the journey back home after service. 

Schedule: 

9 AM Registration Opens and Community Resource Fair

10 AM Opening Ceremonies 

11:00 AM Walk Commences on paths through Riverfront Park.

name: Holiday 5K, 10K, & 13.1M at Camas, WA (50)
description:
US Road Running Races

US Road Running races are built for runners and walkers who like friendly, low-pressure race days with just enough competition to keep things exciting. Our events are local, welcoming, and easy to jump into, whether you are chasing a PR, collecting another themed medal, working toward series points, or just getting outside with good people.

Most races are small enough to feel personal but organized enough to feel official. You can expect a clear course, helpful race staff, finisher medals, results, and a relaxed community feel. Bring your fast shoes, your steady walking pace, your favorite running buddy, or your best “I signed up for this on purpose” smile. We will be glad to see you at the start line.

A quick race-day note: because many US Road Running events are small local races, we normally have one or two staff members at each race. EMS is not stationed on site, and water stations are limited to the finish area at the end of each lap and at the race finish. Please plan for the weather, bring anything you may want between laps, and check in with race staff if you need help.

View Race Course, Results, and Race Information on the US Road Running race page.

name: Hope and Heroes Run
description:
🦸 CAPES ON. COSTUMES READY. IT'S TIME TO UNITE.
Join us at beautiful Marymoor Park in Redmond for a family-friendly, superhero-themed race day featuring a timed 5K and 10K and Kids Dash.

Run, walk, bring the family, and suit up for a fun October morning at Marymoor Park.

All ages. All paces. Superhero costumes encouraged.

⏰ START TIMES
8:00 AM — Check-In Opens
9:10 AM — Superhero Costume Contest
9:15 AM — Super Sidekick Dash
9:30 AM — The Unstoppable 10K
9:35 AM — The Fearless 5K

🏃 THE EVENTS
⚡ The Fearless 5K — 3.1 Miles
You don't have to be fast to be fearless. Run or walk the paths of Marymoor Park in this family-friendly, timed 5K. Strollers welcome. Finisher medals plus overall and age-group awards.

💪 The Unstoppable 10K — 6.2 Miles
Take on 6.2 miles through Marymoor Park in our timed 10K. Whether you're chasing a PR or taking on a new challenge, this one's for you. Strollers welcome. Finisher medals plus overall and age-group awards.

⭐ Super Sidekick Dash — 0.4 Miles · Ages 0–5
The littlest heroes take over the course for their very own 0.4-mile dash. Parents and guardians are welcome to run alongside, and every little hero earns a finisher medal.

👥 CREATE OR JOIN A TEAM
Racing is better together! Create or join a team with friends, family, coworkers, your running crew, or an organization. Choose Social Team or Company & Organization Team during registration.

🏆 SUPERHERO COSTUME CONTEST
Suit up and show us your superhero style!

🦸 Best Individual Costume
🦸‍♀️ Best Group Costume
⭐ Best Kids Costume

👕 EVENT T-SHIRT
Register for the 5K or 10K by September 25 to receive an official Hope & Heroes Run event T-shirt with your registration.

💚 WHY WE RUN
Held in recognition of PANS/PANDAS Awareness Day on October 9, this event shines a light on PANS (Pediatric Acute-onset Neuropsychiatric Syndrome) and PANDAS (Pediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated with Streptococcal infections) while raising awareness and support for the children and families affected by these conditions.

The superhero theme celebrates the courage and strength of children facing PANS/PANDAS and the families standing beside them.

Every registration helps spread awareness. Every superhero costume celebrates courage. Every step brings hope.

100% of donations benefit the Northwest PANDAS/PANS Network, helping provide education, advocacy, and support for families across our region.

For more information about PANS/PANDAS, please visit the Northwest PANDAS/PANS Network (NWPPN) website.

Come for the capes. Stay for the cause. Run for the heroes. 🦸💚

name: I Can And I Will Run!
description:
I can and I will is the mantra Olivia and her mom, Alisa, have been saying since 2018. Whether it's prepping to be poked by a needle or running up a big hill, we remind ourselves that we can and we will! We take these words to heart and they have been pushing us to do big things!

Our goal with this run is to raise money for the Uncompensated Care Fund at Seattle Children's Hospital. Race day is Sunday, October 18th, 2026. The event offers kids dashes, a professionally timed 5k and a 10k, as well as a virtual run for our friends and fans who are not able to travel to Seattle. The start will be at Green Lake Community Center using both the inner trail, and surrounding park for the 10k, finishing back at the start. The kids' runs will be held near the starting line after the other races are completed. We will have t-shirts for those registering early as long as supplies last as well as finisher medals!

We created this event to help Seattle Children's Hospital provide world class care to patients regardless of their ability to pay. Everyday a family walks into Seattle Children's Hospital and learns something that will forever change them. No parent should have to deal with a difficult diagnosis for their child and face financial hardship when seeking care for their child. 

Every step you take will make a difference in the lives of families who are impacted by a devastating diagnosis and wondering how they will pay the medical bills. 100% of race net proceeds from this fun run will benefit uncompensated care at Seattle Children’s Hospital. Thank you for your participation and help. You are ensuring that families can focus on their child's wellbeing; not the medical bill in their mailbox.

If you've been to the Run before, awesome, thank you for the ongoing support! And if you are joining us for the first time, welcome to the party!

Our goal with this run is to raise money for the Uncompensated Care Fund at Seattle Children's Hospital. Race day is Sunday, October 18th, 2026. The event offers kids dashes, a professionally timed 5k and a 10k, as well as a virtual run for our friends and fans who are not able to travel to Seattle. The start will be at Green Lake Community Center using both the inner trail, and surrounding park for the 10k, finishing back at the start. The kids' runs will be held near the starting line after the other races are completed. We will have t-shirts for those registering early as long as supplies last as well as finisher medals!

We created this event to help Seattle Children's Hospital provide world class care to patients regardless of their ability to pay. Everyday a family walks into Seattle Children's Hospital and learns something that will forever change them. No parent should have to deal with a difficult diagnosis for their child and face financial hardship when seeking care for their child. 

Every step you take will make a difference in the lives of families who are impacted by a devastating diagnosis and wondering how they will pay the medical bills. 100% of race net proceeds from this fun run will benefit uncompensated care at Seattle Children’s Hospital. Thank you for your participation and help. You are ensuring that families can focus on their child's wellbeing; not the medical bill in their mailbox.

If you've been to the Run before, awesome, thank you for the ongoing support! And if you are joining us for the first time, welcome to the party!

name: I love the 90s 5k
description:
I love the 90s 5k! 

Get ready to groove and run down memory lane at the I Love the 90s 5K, where you can lace up your sneakers & jam to classic 90s tunes!
Join us for the I Love the 90s 5k! Lace up your sneakers and get ready to groove to the best hits of the 90s while running through beautiful Green Lake Park in Seattle, WA. This in-person event is a blast from the past, celebrating all things 90s. Whether you're a fan of grunge, pop, or hip-hop, this 5k is for you! Dress up in your favorite 90s attire and relive the nostalgia with fellow participants. The course will take you around the scenic Green Lake, providing a picturesque backdrop for your run. So grab your friends, put on your Walkman, and let's make some memories together at the I Love the 90s 5k!
 
Questions? Concerns? Email us! General inquiries:  info@run2befit.com

name: Iron Horse Half Marathon
description:
IMPORTANT FOR 2027: Damage to the Iron Horse trail from the December 2025 floods mean that no events are being held there in 2027, including the Iron Horse Half. Our course has been re-routed to adjust to this. The new course is a modified out and back, point-to-point route. While it is no longer downhill for the first 10 miles, the incline is mild and limited to the first few miles.

Race Website

Check out our Bundle/Save

VIRTUAL RACE INFO - We have 40 spots for virtual runners. Once they sell out there are no more available. You can run the distance all at once or break it up into chunks and run it on the date of your choosing. You will receive a shirt and medal that will be mailed after the in person race.

name: Issaquah Schools Foundation Monster Mash 5K
description:
Help us raise a MONSTROUS amount of support for local students on October 24th! ISF Monster Mash 5K is a community-based, family-friendly event that raises funds for programs that serve students attending all 27 ISD schools.

We welcome all-ages and abilities. Convenient onsite parking, phased start times, and a professionally chip-timed course ensure a great experience for all. You’ll appreciate the flat, paved, out-and-back route whether you’re setting a new 5K PR or enjoying a brisk walk together as a family! Bring your creativity – festive costumes are encouraged!
This event sells out every year, so don't wait to register! Every registration submitted by October 11th receives the option of receiving a 2026 Monster Mash technical race tee & medal. Option to waive the shirt (No-Shirt Registration), if wearing monsters isn't your jam - more of your registration fee will go to support students! Registrants are eligible for placement awards, receive free event photos,  and raffle tickets for prizes! See below for details.

name: Issaquah Turkey Trot 2026
description:
The Issaquah Turkey Trot 5K is a fun, casual, all-ages event benefitting the crucial work of the Issaquah Food & Clothing Bank to provide food and vital resources in East King County. 

When? Thanksgiving Morning @ 9 a.m.
Where? Downtown Issaquah

 
Kids can participate in a “Gobble Wobble” along the route, and trotters often show their spirit with Thanksgiving-themed costumes and accessories as they run, walk, stroll, or trot a three-mile course through the heart of picturesque downtown Issaquah. 
 
 We welcomed over 5,000 trotters in 2025, and we are hoping to see another great turnout this year as our community rallies behind such an important cause.

All registrations include a race bib and t-shirt (t-shirt sizes only guaranteed for Early Bird registrations by October 30).

$35    11 and up – Now through October 30
$40    11 and up – October 31-November 25
$45    11 and up – Thanksgiving Day
$15    10 and under*

*Infants and toddlers only need to be registered if a t-shirt is desired.

name: Jack & Jill Marathon & Half
description:
• Ranked #35 Fastest Marathon in the U.S. (FindMyMarathon) 
 • 1 in 5 runners BQ
 • ~1,000 feet of net downhill with NO Boston Qualifier time penalty
 • Smooth, fast rail-trail surface built for negative splits
 • Jack & Jill has sent thousands of runners to Boston
 • Iconic Snoqualmie Tunnel experience
 • Abbott World Marathon Majors Age Group World Rankings Qualifier
 • Professionally timed with live tracking, detailed results, and printed results cards
 • Super Pacers for key Boston Qualifying times

Over a decade of experience delivering one of the fastest and most trusted downhill races in the country.


What Runners Are Saying

"BQ and PR!! Boston 2026 here I come💙🦄💛 Jack and Jill was my race to get a larger buffer"- Carolyn

"BQ last July at Jack and Jill, Boston 2026 here I come! I love running this course, I would run it just for the peace and tranquility the course provides. P.S. - I love the tunnel, part of the experience" - Jon

"The finish line was awesome! They announce your name and let you know if you qualified for Boston. The crowd was amazing at the finish. And yes, I rang that PR bell with Pride! Would I run this marathon again? Absolutely!" - Annie|

"10 min PR from my Boston Time, so it was very successful! Was a really fun race and loved the finish line!! Such a great atmosphere!"

name: Jasper Mountain Trail Fest 2027
description:
USA Track & Field-Sanctioned Event

2026 Jasper Mountain Trail Fest Video

Introduction

Welcome to one of the most unique and rewarding trail running experiences in the Pacific Northwest. Jasper Mountain Trail Fest features some of the best-maintained and most thoughtfully designed single-track trails in Eastern Washington, set within the protected Jasper Mountain Reserve, an environmental 501(c)3 non-profit organization dedicated to conservation and public enjoyment.

Whether you are a seasoned trail runner looking for a rugged, higher-elevation challenge, a marathoner ready to push your limits off-road, or a team eager to take on a truly one-of-a-kind relay adventure, this event delivers. With distances ranging from a family-friendly 7K to a demanding full marathon and an all-day relay, there is something here for every level of runner. Come test yourself on beautiful, wild terrain while supporting conservation and experiencing a trail system that truly stands apart.

For 2027, we are offering four unique race options:

1) Our classic (seventh annual!) 4-person relay race, 52.4 miles total distance
2) Solo Half marathon, 13.1 miles with 2,570 feet of elevation gain
3) Solo Full marathon, 26.2 miles with 5,140 feet of elevation gain
4) Solo 7k Family Run (4.4 miles) with minimal elevation gain

Price increases are on  April 15, 2027, May 16, 2027, and June 12, 2027. Sign up by May 31, 2027 to guarantee you receive a race t-shirt and medal! Contact info@jaspermountainreserve.org with any questions.

All races take place on the following single track trails (click on each for details):

Red Loop (3.3 miles)
Green Loop (4.4 miles)
Black Loop (5.4 miles)

Visit our trail page for course records. 

Reserve Information and Accommodations

The start and finish line is at Jasper Mountain Reserve, Dayton, WA 99328. Type "Jasper Mountain Reserve" into Google or Apple Maps and follow online directions.

Your race registration includes camping and parking on the reserve directly on the race course. On-site camping guarantees an stress-free morning. We suggest arriving during daylight a day or two prior to the race, and departing the day after the race. There will be an informal welcome reception and short presentation about the race at around 9:00PM on the evening prior to the race. BIB-pickup starts at 6pm the evening prior to the race, and we strongly encourage getting it that evening to avoid a morning rush.

Campsites for racers are within Jasper Mountain Reserve. As this is a nature reserve, loud noises, including car engines, power generators, high volume loudspeakers etc. are strictly forbidden. Dogs must be on leash at all times. Camp-fires are only allowed at one designated area (please familiarize yourself with WA State and Columbia County seasonal camp fire restrictions). Bring your own food, water, and (battery) power sources (Jasper Mountain Reserve is off the grid, meaning there is no water or electricity). Portable sanitary facilities will be provided. As there is no garbage and recycling collection service please collect all trash and take it with you when you depart.

Accommodation options are also available just a short drive from the race! Choose from hotels and Airbnbs in nearby Dayton (11 miles from the event), Waitsburg (16 miles), or Walla Walla (37 miles).

Relay Race Details (Start Time 7:00AM):

Relay teams consist of 4 people sharing one assigned bib with an adjustable belt that can be exchanged between team members. Each racer signs up individually and can choose one of the following options:

1) No Team (the race organizers will assign you to a team)
2) Join an Existing Team
3) Create a New Team

All teams start together with the 1st runner of each team running the red loop at the same time. Once completed, the 1st runner passes the bib to the 2nd team member who will complete the green loop. Once completed, the 2nd team member passes the bib to the 3rd team member who will complete the black loop. Once completed, the 3rd team member passes on the bib to the 4th team member who will run the red loop, followed by the 1st team member who will run the green loop, followed by the 2nd team member who will run the black loop and so on, until all 4 team members each have completed all three loops for 12 loops total. Race timing will provide results for entire teams as well as individual times (splits) on each separate trail loop. All three loops combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon.

The relay race is expected to take 8-12 hours and the race course closes at 7pm. If a team is at risk of not completing the race by 7pm, the race director will work with that team to double or triple up runners to ensure completion. 

Half Marathon and Full Marathon Details (Start Time 7:00AM)

Calling all Ultra Trail Runners! Our course is crafted specifically for the adventurous spirit of the ultra trail community. The half marathon is the perfect choice for those eager to test their limits or begin their journey toward ultra distances. For the fearless and bold, the full marathon awaits: 26.2 miles with over 5,000 feet of elevation gain, set against a backdrop of breathtaking natural beauty in the Blue Mountains. This isn't just a race; it’s a chance to immerse yourself in the beautiful landscape of a pristine nature reserve. Get ready to experience the ultimate trail running adventure, you won't be disappointed! All three trail loops within Jasper Mountain Reserve combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon, The full marathon will run the combined trail loops twice.

Aid Stations for the Half Marathon (13.1 Miles):

  • Mile 3.3
  • Mile 7.7
  • Mile 10.3
  • Mile 13.1 (Finish)
     

Aid Stations for Full Marathon (26.2 Miles):

  • Mile 3.3
  • Mile 7.7
  • Mile 10.3
  • Mile 13.1
  • Mile 16.4
  • Mile 20.8
  • Mile 23.4
  • Mile 26.2 (Finish)

 

7k (4.4 miles) Family Run Details (Start Time 7:15AM)

This option is on our beautiful Green Trail, which is 4.3 miles long with minimal elevation gain. It is ideal for runners who prefer a sprint, families with kids who want to run together, and for participants who prefer to walk.

Whether you are a seasoned trail runner looking for a rugged, higher-elevation challenge, a marathoner ready to push your limits off-road, or a team eager to take on a truly one-of-a-kind relay adventure, this event delivers. With distances ranging from a family-friendly 7K to a demanding full marathon and an all-day relay, there is something here for every level of runner. Come test yourself on beautiful, wild terrain while supporting conservation and experiencing a trail system that truly stands apart.

For 2027, we are offering four unique race options:

1) Our classic (seventh annual!) 4-person relay race, 52.4 miles total distance
2) Solo Half marathon, 13.1 miles with 2,570 feet of elevation gain
3) Solo Full marathon, 26.2 miles with 5,140 feet of elevation gain
4) Solo 7k Family Run (4.4 miles) with minimal elevation gain

Price increases are on  April 15, 2027, May 16, 2027, and June 12, 2027. Sign up by May 31, 2027 to guarantee you receive a race t-shirt and medal! Contact info@jaspermountainreserve.org with any questions.

All races take place on the following single track trails (click on each for details):

Red Loop (3.3 miles)
Green Loop (4.4 miles)
Black Loop (5.4 miles)

Visit our trail page for course records. 

Reserve Information and Accommodations

The start and finish line is at Jasper Mountain Reserve, Dayton, WA 99328. Type "Jasper Mountain Reserve" into Google or Apple Maps and follow online directions.

Your race registration includes camping and parking on the reserve directly on the race course. On-site camping guarantees an stress-free morning. We suggest arriving during daylight a day or two prior to the race, and departing the day after the race. There will be an informal welcome reception and short presentation about the race at around 9:00PM on the evening prior to the race. BIB-pickup starts at 6pm the evening prior to the race, and we strongly encourage getting it that evening to avoid a morning rush.

Campsites for racers are within Jasper Mountain Reserve. As this is a nature reserve, loud noises, including car engines, power generators, high volume loudspeakers etc. are strictly forbidden. Dogs must be on leash at all times. Camp-fires are only allowed at one designated area (please familiarize yourself with WA State and Columbia County seasonal camp fire restrictions). Bring your own food, water, and (battery) power sources (Jasper Mountain Reserve is off the grid, meaning there is no water or electricity). Portable sanitary facilities will be provided. As there is no garbage and recycling collection service please collect all trash and take it with you when you depart.

Accommodation options are also available just a short drive from the race! Choose from hotels and Airbnbs in nearby Dayton (11 miles from the event), Waitsburg (16 miles), or Walla Walla (37 miles).

Relay Race Details (Start Time 7:00AM):

Relay teams consist of 4 people sharing one assigned bib with an adjustable belt that can be exchanged between team members. Each racer signs up individually and can choose one of the following options:

1) No Team (the race organizers will assign you to a team)
2) Join an Existing Team
3) Create a New Team

All teams start together with the 1st runner of each team running the red loop at the same time. Once completed, the 1st runner passes the bib to the 2nd team member who will complete the green loop. Once completed, the 2nd team member passes the bib to the 3rd team member who will complete the black loop. Once completed, the 3rd team member passes on the bib to the 4th team member who will run the red loop, followed by the 1st team member who will run the green loop, followed by the 2nd team member who will run the black loop and so on, until all 4 team members each have completed all three loops for 12 loops total. Race timing will provide results for entire teams as well as individual times (splits) on each separate trail loop. All three loops combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon.

The relay race is expected to take 8-12 hours and the race course closes at 7pm. If a team is at risk of not completing the race by 7pm, the race director will work with that team to double or triple up runners to ensure completion. 

Half Marathon and Full Marathon Details (Start Time 7:00AM)

Calling all Ultra Trail Runners! Our course is crafted specifically for the adventurous spirit of the ultra trail community. The half marathon is the perfect choice for those eager to test their limits or begin their journey toward ultra distances. For the fearless and bold, the full marathon awaits: 26.2 miles with over 5,000 feet of elevation gain, set against a backdrop of breathtaking natural beauty in the Blue Mountains. This isn't just a race; it’s a chance to immerse yourself in the beautiful landscape of a pristine nature reserve. Get ready to experience the ultimate trail running adventure, you won't be disappointed! All three trail loops within Jasper Mountain Reserve combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon, The full marathon will run the combined trail loops twice.

Aid Stations for the Half Marathon (13.1 Miles):

  • Mile 3.3
  • Mile 7.7
  • Mile 10.3
  • Mile 13.1 (Finish)
     

Aid Stations for Full Marathon (26.2 Miles):

  • Mile 3.3
  • Mile 7.7
  • Mile 10.3
  • Mile 13.1
  • Mile 16.4
  • Mile 20.8
  • Mile 23.4
  • Mile 26.2 (Finish)

 

7k (4.4 miles) Family Run Details (Start Time 7:15AM)

This option is on our beautiful Green Trail, which is 4.3 miles long with minimal elevation gain. It is ideal for runners who prefer a sprint, families with kids who want to run together, and for participants who prefer to walk.

name: Jog the Bog
description:
We are excited to announce:

This year's 33rd Cranberry Harvest Festival will again offer The Bog Jog on Sunday, October 11, 2026.  It's back after a long covid break! 

The courses include a combination of flat roads past Cranberry Bogs, and for the 10K Run, a section on the Pacific Ocean beach. 

This event includes your choice of a Timed 10K Run, Timed 5K Run or Untimed 3K Walk/Run. 

First male and First female to cross the Finish Line each race win a big bag of Truly Fresh and Locally Grown Cranberries! 

All Participants receive a Long Sleeve T-Shirt and a medal.

Bibs and T-shirts will be available for pickup the Morning of the Races at the Grayland Hall.

The race will start and finish Sunday October 11 at the Grayland Community Hall, a country block off State Route 105 at the corner of Grange and Cranberry Road in Grayland.

name: Juanita Unified 5K - Heroes in motion
description:
The Juanita Unified 5K is more than just a run (or walk!), it's a step toward a more inclusive and connected community. Juanita High School serves over 1,700 diverse students and is committed to creating an environment where every student feels valued. The 5K aims to support this vision by offering an inclusive experience for everyone in the Juanita community - school and beyond.

The Juanita Unified 5K is organized by the Juanita High School DECA chapter. DECA is an internationally recognized program that prepares emerging leaders and entrepreneurs through real-world experiences and strives to create confident, capable contributors to society. 

JHS Booster Club in support of JHS DECA. Funds raised will support Juanita DECA and the Unified program at Juanita. All donations will be processed through the JHS Booster Club.

name: Jumping Mouse Turkey Trot
description:
Join us for the Jumping Mouse Annual Turkey Trot 5K — a community tradition that brings people together to celebrate health, gratitude, and giving back!

This year’s Turkey Trot will take place Saturday, November 21st, 2026, on the beautiful Larry Scott Trail in Port Townsend, WA. 

Whether you’re running, walking, or trotting with family and friends, every step you take helps support Jumping Mouse Children’s Center and its mission to provide transformative therapy and advocacy for children’s mental health.

Event Highlights:

Scenic, flat 5K course on the Larry Scott Trail
Family-friendly and dog-friendly atmosphere (strollers welcome too!)
An uplifting way to kick off the holiday season while giving back to kids in need
Let’s lace up, have fun, and make a difference together. 🦃💛

name: K is for Kindness 5 K and 1K Run
description:
K is for Kindness is a 5K and 1K fun run to benefit Spectrum Studios and Empower Center for Growth.  

The Tri-Cities only nonprofit for young adults on the Autism Spectrum who have aged out of school—creating opportunities, connections, enrichment and growth.

Empower Center for Growth is a welcoming community hub dedicated to individuals on the Autism Spectrum who are looking for a place to connect, learn, and grow. It’s a space to hang out with new friends, take creative and life-skills classes, and discover new interests in a supportive, inclusive environment. Whether you want to explore art, cooking, technology, or personal development, Empower Center for Growth is here to help you build confidence, friendships, and lifelong skills.

Strollers and pets welcome.

name: K9 Candy Cane 5K Fun Run
description:
The K9 Candy Cane 5K Fun Run and Walk is held at the Renton Community Center Campus. Runners and walkers travel along the paved beautiful Cedar River Trail before looping back to the Community Center Campus. Competitive runners, fun runners, walkers and families (with or without) dogs are all invited to this annual event. Accurate and professional chip timing is provided by Negative Split. If registered before 9:00AM on Wednesday, November 25, participants will receive a hooded sweatshirt. Don't forget about our Annual Pet Food Drive for furry friends in need, help us FILL THE TRUCK! 

Registration Windows:

  • Early Bird Registration - August 19 to November 1.
    • Guarantees you a hooded sweatshirt. 
    • Ages 4 to 17 fee:        $20
    • Ages 18 and up fee:   $30
  • Standard Price Registration - November 2, ending at 9:00AM, November 25.
    • Guarantees you a hooded sweatshirt.  
    • Ages 4 to 17 fee:       $30
    • Ages 18 and up fee:  $40
  • Last Chance Registration -  Begins 9:01AM November 25, through 1:00PM on Saturday December 5.
    • Not eligible to receive a hooded sweatshirt, Fun Run Only.
    • Ages 4 to 17 fee:       $30
    • Ages 18 and up fee:  $40

Race Bib Number Pick Up:
If you have pre-registered, you may pick up your race bib and sweatshirt (if applicable) at The Renton Community Center, 1715 Maple Valley Hwy. Renton, 98057, Saturday, December 6, 9:30AM – 5:00PM. If you are picking up for family members or friends, you will need their race day registration confirmation. You will also have the opportunity to pickup your race bib and sweatshirt onsite the morning of the race. 

Race Guidelines for Humans and Dogs:

  • Strollers are welcome on the course for both humans and dogs.
  • Participants NOT wanting to be timed should NOT pass through the finish line, please exit the course to the left or right prior to entering the timing chute.
  • Your race bib is your timing chip. Please wear it outside of your clothing facing forward for accurate timing.
  • Timing will conclude 45 minutes after the start of the race.
  • Walkers stay to the right of the race course.
  • Extra sweatshirts are NOT purchased and will NOT be available day of race.
  • No more than two dogs per person.
  • All dogs are required to be current on vaccinations.
  • No dogs under six months of age.
  • Dogs must be on leash no more than 6 feet in length.
  • Owners are responsible for the well-being and safety of their dog(s) at all times
  • No female dogs in heat. 
  • No aggressive dogs or aggressive owners. Any signs of aggression towards other dogs or participants will result in being asked to leave the event.
  • Owners are responsible for always picking up after their dog(s). 

Pet Food Drive:
Please bring a can/bag of pet food to be donated to local animals in need. Help us FILL THE TRUCK! 

Click here: Course Map

Course Closure:
Recreational walkers/runners are non-competitive and will not be timed if finishing after 45 minutes. If you are participating in this event but are not being timed please be considerate and not cross the finish line where timing is taking place. Keep to the right or left of the timing chute.

Awards and Results:
Awards will be given to the top three runners overall in the following categories: Male 55+, Female 55+, Male 18-54, Female 18-54, Non-Binary Adult 18+, Youth 1-17. 

Hooded Sweatshirts:
After 9:00AM November 26, hooded Sweatshirts are no longer available. Extra sweatshirts are not purchased and will NOT be available at the end of the race. The sweatshirt size you selected is what's purchased. Sweatshirts are unisex sizing.

name: Kirkland Turkey Trot
description:
Run Together at the Kirkland Turkey Trot!

Gather your family, invite your friends, and kick off the holiday season together at the Kirkland Turkey Trot 5K, 10K, and Lil’ Gobbler Run!

Join us Sunday, November 15, 2026, at 9:00 AM at Juanita Beach Park for a fun and welcoming event designed for runners and walkers of all ages and abilities. Whether you are chasing a personal best, completing your first race, or simply enjoying an active morning with the people you care about, the Kirkland Turkey Trot is about moving together and creating lasting memories.

The scenic 5K and 10K courses begin and end at Juanita Beach Park. Along the way, participants will travel to and through Juanita Bay Park, enjoy views of Lake Washington and the Seattle skyline, and return across the historic Market Street Bridge.

Inspiring the Next Generation

The Kirkland Turkey Trot is a wonderful opportunity to introduce younger runners to the joy of being active. Families can participate together, encourage one another along the course, and show children that exercise can be fun, social, and rewarding.

Every young person who reaches the finish line has something to celebrate—whether they run, jog, walk, or receive a little help along the way.

Lil’ Gobbler Run

The Lil’ Gobbler Run gives our youngest participants their own moment to shine! This quarter-mile run takes place entirely within Juanita Beach Park and is designed for children ages 2–6.

Parents, grandparents, siblings, and friends are encouraged to cheer them on as they experience the excitement of participating in their own race and crossing the finish line.

Keep the Celebration Going

After the race, bring your family and friends to Moss Bay Hall at 111 Central Way in downtown Kirkland for a festive post-race celebration featuring great beer, delicious pretzels, and plenty of holiday cheer.

Make the Kirkland Turkey Trot part of your family’s holiday tradition—because being active is even better when we do it together!
