name: Lake Wilderness Triathlon and Run
description:
Lake Wilderness Triathlon is celebrating our 22nd year!!  This event is scenic in all aspects of the race and has something for every level of participation. This is an excellent venue for a first time triathlete and the triathlete that's looking for some great competition. We have many first time triathletes and those that compete in Ironman.  

The swim is in Lake Wilderness, you'll have a beautiful view of Mt. Rainier as you swim. The bike ride is along the rolling hills of Maple Valley and the surrounding area. The  run is along the Lake Wilderness Trial. This trail is about 10 feet across and it's soft gravel.  You'll have views of Mt. Rainer,  lake wilderness and beautiful Cedar River. Everyone is welcome to join us on this great event 

Lake Wilderness Run has beautiful trails to run along with views of Mount Rainer, Cedar River and Lake Wilderness.

Event Details and schedule:

Lake Wilderness park will open for competitors at 5:15am.  If you're picking up your packet the day of the event you can pick up your packet from 5:15-6:30am. 

Each participant must bring picture I.D. to pick up their packet .  You many not pick up a packet for other participants.

name: Lampson Cable Bridge Run
description:
This year marks the 48th annual running of the Lampson Cable Bridge Run! Finisher Medals will be given out to the first 2200 participants who finish the run. To receive your medal please ensure that your race bib is visible as you cross the finish line. So tell your friends and come out and enjoy this fun and exciting holiday tradition! Runners, no matter the distance they choose (5K or 10K) will start their race crossing over the Columbia River from Kennewick to Pasco, WA on the scenic Cable Bridge. The 1-Mile runners will end shortly after crossing the bridge and be shuttled to the 5K/10K finish area. The 5K & 10K finish line is located at the Lampson warehouse. At the finish line you will receive your medal and refreshments before proceeding to catch the shuttle bus back to the fairground's parking lot. 

There is a discounted, non-timed 1-Mile Fun Run category for those that want to experience the fun and excitement of this yearly event, and still receive the finisher medal. Also there is a Kids 4 & Under category that is free of charge. Participants in this category will receive their own special bib but will not be timed nor receive a finisher medal, instead they will receive a child's finisher ribbon.

For all timed race categories, timing chips are used and awards are given to the top participants in each age category. So if you are a competitive runner or someone who just wants to have fun walking with your friends, the Lampson Cable Bridge Run has what you are looking for.

name: Langlauf 10K XC Ski Race
description:
Langlauf is a 10K Cross Country Ski Race that takes place at the Mount Spokane Nordic Ski Center which is the premier Cross Country Ski Area in the Inland Northwest.  The race takes place on the traditional 10K course and has wave starts to accommodate skiers of all abilities and speeds.  Even maybe more epic than the race itself, are the pre and post race amenities that are enjoyed by all racers.  This is the biggest and oldest Cross Country Race in the Pacific Northwest...you don't want to miss it!

Once again, this year we are offering an adaptive skier category. If you are visually impaired or a sit skier you will be able to participate in our Wave start, but at Junction 1 will continue on Linder Road to a turnaround at the Inland gate then back to Brian's and our traditional finish line. Adaptive skiers must register but their guide skier can accompany them for no cost. Guides will need to sign a waiver the morning of the race and do not need to pay to register unless they want to be timed. Guides will be considered a volunteer and be entered in the prize drawing.

name: Last Chance Marathon and Half Marathon
description:
OK, here is your Last Chance to run a 1/2 marathon or full marathon this year! The 1/2 marathon course is an out and back and the full marathon course is the same out and back course two times, starting at Fairhaven Park Pavillion, running the Interurban trail out to Clayton Beach for the full 13.1 miles or 26.2. Course is subject to change if trail conditions mandate.

 

This trail has spectacular views and very few hills, just enough hills to make it interesting, and break up the flat sections. FYI: We have been known to have SNOW this time of the year so plan accordingly. The majority of this trail is covered with a canopy of trees which deflects some of the rain or snow, but this also means it doesn’t heat as fast as an open course would. It can get cold. The majority of the trail is an old railroad bed, very easy to run on gravel surface, with the exception of Arroyos Park. Arroyos Park is a double track trail with a few bridges and a few fun hills. It is a very well maintained set of trails.

 

The bathrooms at Fairhaven Park will be unlocked as well as the warm heated Pavillion.

 

You should plan on being self-sufficient and carrying your own water and aid. The 1st aid station on the course is ~ 3.5 miles into the race off Chuckanut Crest Drive. In the 1/2 marathon you will run by this aid station twice, and 4 times in the full marathon.  There will be an aid station at the turn around which you will access once in the 1/2 marathon and twice in the full marathon. We will also have an aid station at the start/finish so full 1/2 marathoners will have 3 chances to refill their water bottles, about every 3 to 3.5 miles, & marathoners will have 7 chances to refill their water bottles.  We will have water, an electrolyte drink and other snacks at the aid stations.  Usually I put some type of candy like candy corn, gummy bears, bananas, pretzels, typical ultra style foods. You won’t go hungry!
Keep an eye on the website for any changes to the event. Finishers will receive a Last Chance coin/medal similar to the quality of the Woolley Runs coin.  We will provide food at the end like all the NW Ultra Events.  While all your friends are recovering from their hang over and resting up before the evening’s festivities, you’ll be burning calories and ready to PARTY hardy knowing you’ve already burned off that extra beer or two, or three.

name: LivFree 24 Hour Hockey Marathon - Seattle
description:
What is the LivSports 24 Hour Adult Hockey Marathon benefiting LivFree?

Here’s how it all works - the event is a continuous game with 60 to 90 skaters playing on two teams in 3 rotating groups based on ability, with a running score from opening puck drop to the final horn. Each player raises $1500 dollars for the cause. LivFree is a pediatric cancer non-profit organization that provides children and their families with moments of joy to take a break from struggle and enjoy some family time together. Whether it's tickets to a game, a Broadway show, or a night out, LivFree is here to help the whole family. 

When will this take place and how does it work?

The event starts at 10 am on Saturday, June 26th, 2027, and the final horn will sound at 10 am on Sunday, June 27th. Teams will be broken up into 3 groups (A, B, and C) based on ability, and each skater will get a minimum of 7 hours of ice time. The standard swag for each player will be a custom jersey, synthetic hockey socks, an event T-shirt, meals, snacks, drinks, and more. 

What arena will this take place at?

We knew coming into this that the best way to honor the effort of the players, both in their fundraising and in their time on the ice, was by securing an amazing venue. After a few steps into the Kraken Community Iceplex in Seattle, WA, you will see that we found an absolute gem.

There will be more...

There is so much more that will be involved in this event, with opportunities for family members to come watch, raffles, fundraising incentives, corporate sponsorships, and more. 

So get in touch with your teams, sign up, and spread the word. Don’t miss your chance to take the ice with LivFree and help change the lives of kids and families battling childhood cancer - one shift at a time. 

FOR FULL 24-HOUR MARATHON INFORMATION, PLEASE VISIT OUR HOMEPAGE AT www.LivFreeToday.org/24HourHockey

name: LivFree 24 Hour Hockey Marathon - Seattle
description:
What is the LivSports 24 Hour Adult Hockey Marathon benefiting LivFree?

Here’s how it all works - the event is a continuous game with 60 to 90 skaters playing on two teams in 3 rotating groups based on ability, with a running score from opening puck drop to the final horn. Each player raises $1500 dollars for the cause. LivFree is a pediatric cancer non-profit organization that provides children and their families with moments of joy to take a break from struggle and enjoy some family time together. Whether it's tickets to a game, a Broadway show, or a night out, LivFree is here to help the whole family. 

When will this take place and how does it work?

The event starts at 10 am on Saturday, June 26th, 2027, and the final horn will sound at 10 am on Sunday, June 27th. Teams will be broken up into 3 groups (A, B, and C) based on ability, and each skater will get a minimum of 7 hours of ice time. The standard swag for each player will be a custom jersey, synthetic hockey socks, an event T-shirt, meals, snacks, drinks, and more. 

What arena will this take place at?

We knew coming into this that the best way to honor the effort of the players, both in their fundraising and in their time on the ice, was by securing an amazing venue. After a few steps into the Kraken Community Iceplex in Seattle, WA, you will see that we found an absolute gem.

There will be more...

There is so much more that will be involved in this event, with opportunities for family members to come watch, raffles, fundraising incentives, corporate sponsorships, and more. 

So get in touch with your teams, sign up, and spread the word. Don’t miss your chance to take the ice with LivFree and help change the lives of kids and families battling childhood cancer - one shift at a time. 

FOR FULL 24-HOUR MARATHON INFORMATION, PLEASE VISIT OUR HOMEPAGE AT www.LivFreeToday.org/24HourHockey

name: Lookin For A Cure Seattle
description:
"We're "Lookin' For a Cure" in scenic Warren G Magnesun Park! Join A Cure In Sight on Saturday May 29, 2027 from 8AM-11AM, to walk or run with us. We will be taking steps to find a cure for a rare eye cancer, Ocular Melanoma. Ocular Melanoma is estimated by the American Cancer Society to have roughly 3000 new cases each year nationwide. Bring your friends and family to the race day--all ages welcome to walk or run with us.

Register, become a fund raiser, make a team, grab your friends and family and raise money to support local research with Dr. Stacey and Fred Hutch Cancer Center.  Prizes will be awarded for largest team, largest fundraiser as well as top finishers.

Race Swag

  • Guarantee t-shirt if registered by May 15th, 2027
  • Finisher Medal
  • Food & Drink
  • Aid Station
  • Commemorative Race Bib
  • Free downloadable photos
  • Official finishers time with age group placements

Race day schedule

  • Registration 8AM
  • Race start 9AM
  • Announcements Awards 10AM

Parking

Free parking past the boat launch area, just steps from the start line. 

 

Directions 

Cross streets are Sand Point Way NE and NE 65th, go east on 65th past the boat ramps and follow the signs to the start line.  If you have an issue on race day, please call 919-885-5264 for directions.

name: MCCM Monster Mash 5k & Creature Crawl 1k
description:
🎃 4th Annual Monster Mash 5K & Creature Crawl 1K 👾

Join the Mid-Columbia Children's Museum for the 4th Annual Monster Mash 5K & Creature Crawl 1K, a family-friendly Halloween event bringing together costumes, movement, and hands-on fun in support of the future Mid-Columbia Children's Museum.

Whether you're running the 5K, walking with friends, or cheering on your little monster in the Creature Crawl, there's something for everyone!

📅 Saturday, October 24, 2026
📍 Howard Amon Park | Richland, WA

What to Expect
🏃 Costume-friendly 5K run/walk
👾 Creature Crawl 1K for kids and families
🔬 STEM-inspired activities
🍂 Family-friendly fall fun
❤️ Support the future Mid-Columbia Children's Museum

🎟️ Registration
Registration opens at 9:00 AM on September 1, 2026! 

Register early and join us for one of our favorite family events of the year. Early registration ends October 1st!

💙 Foster & Kinship Families
Discounted registration is available for foster and kinship families. To receive a special registration code, please reach out to us at info@mccmuseum.org.

We want Monster Mash to be an event all families in our community can enjoy! 🎃👾

Race Day Rules
🎃 Costumes encouraged — keep them safe to run or walk in!
👶 Strollers welcome — please start toward the back.
🐾 Please leave pets at home (service animals welcome).
👾 Keep little monsters supervised.
➡️ Stay on the marked course and follow volunteer directions.
❤️ Be kind, have fun, and cheer each other on!

Additional race-day details, including check-in and start times, will be shared closer to the event.

We can't wait to celebrate another year of community, creativity, curiosity, and fun with you!

name: McKenzie Mott Memorial Turkey Trot
description:
After the tragic loss of our 15 year old daughter the family tradition of getting together for a movie, thanksgiving dinner and lots of family time was so hard to face without her. Kenzie loved tradition so to help us honor her legacy we created a new tradition for our family. Our family friends "the Larsen's"  inspired us to do something Kenzie would love to do so we did, we ran! We were so blessed to have over fifty of our friends and family join us for our first race as well as overwhelmed by the monetary donation that helped support our Safe Driving Scholarship for all local High School seniors. This is our 10th annual race and all proceeds continue to fund our scholarships.

Race Check-in/ Shirt Pick Up -Nov 24th-Selkirk Middle School 5:30-7:00, Nov 25th- Selkirk Middle School 5:30-7:00 -1409 N. Harvest PKWY, Liberty Lake, WA 99019

Race Day check in Nov 26th 7:45 a.m.- 8:45 a.m. at  Pavilion Park, 727 N. Molter Rd, Liberty Lake, WA 99019

 

Race will start promptly at 9:00 a.m. NE corner of pavilion park. Parking is available at Liberty Lake Elementary and Liberty Creek Elementary.

*To guarantee a shirt size, register by November 10th, 2026.

name: Medal Madness 5K, 10K, 13.1M at Vancouver, WA (44)
description:
US Road Running Races

US Road Running races are built for runners and walkers who like friendly, low-pressure race days with just enough competition to keep things exciting. Our events are local, welcoming, and easy to jump into, whether you are chasing a PR, collecting another themed medal, working toward series points, or just getting outside with good people.

Most races are small enough to feel personal but organized enough to feel official. You can expect a clear course, helpful race staff, finisher medals, results, and a relaxed community feel. Bring your fast shoes, your steady walking pace, your favorite running buddy, or your best “I signed up for this on purpose” smile. We will be glad to see you at the start line.

A quick race-day note: because many US Road Running events are small local races, we normally have one or two staff members at each race. EMS is not stationed on site, and water stations are limited to the finish area at the end of each lap and at the race finish. Please plan for the weather, bring anything you may want between laps, and check in with race staff if you need help.

View Race Course, Results, and Race Information on the US Road Running race page.

name: Medical Lake Lions Club- 49th Annual Only Fools Run at Midnight
description:
Welcome to the 49th Annual Only Fools Run at Midnight!  We will continue to offer both live and virtual options this year. 

Our live event will take place on April 3rd with a start time of 11:30 pm. 

Runners will once again be able to run the mean streets of Medical Lake at midnight.  We will start at Medical Lake High School and have race monitors throughout the course with our finish line at the Pizza Factory to celebrate our achievements.  They will be open late just for the race. 

For virtual runners, you can run and post your times any time between April 3rd, 2027, and April 10, 2026. 

Our race sponsors this year include TNC Ramps, Farm Salvation, the Pizza Factory, and Johnson Homestead.  Please be sure to check them out.  We thank them for their support.  If you are interested in being a race sponsor, please contact Kim Headrick at kheadri2000@yahoo.com or 509-304-4891.  

Let's get racing!!

name: Medical Lake- Trailblazer Triathlon/Duathlon/5K
description:
The Medical Lake Trailblazer Tri/Du/5k is one of the many things to do in Medical Lake on Founders Day weekend. This is an athlete-friendly race with an out-and-back open water swim, bike, and run on paved roads & trails.

Trailblazer Triathlon
A 350m swim, 10.2mi bike ride, and 2.92 mi run starting and ending at Waterfront Park. 

Trailblazer Duathlon
A 1mi run, 10.2mi bike ride, and 2.92 mi run starting and ending at Waterfront Park. 

Trailblazer 5k
A traditional 2.92 mi run around Medical Lake Trail starting and ending at Waterfront Park.

name: Meridian Booster Turkey Trot Fun Run
description:
Whether you walk, jog, or run, come join us for our Turkey Trot at Bellewood Farms and help support the Meridian High School Cross Country Team!

Think you can keep up with our speedy cross country runners? Give it a try! Or, simply trot along at your own pace and enjoy a fun morning with family and friends. 

Kids, get ready to chase the turkeys! Two big turkeys will be making their way around the course, and if you catch them, there’s candy waiting for you! Costumes are encouraged, so get creative and make this Turkey Trot extra fun!

Rain or shine, we’re running! Come ready for a fun, family-friendly event while helping raise funds to support the Meridian High School Cross Country Team.

Strollers designed for trail running are welcome, but our furry friends will need to sit this one out.


Where: 
Bellewood Farms
6140 Guide Meridian Rd., Lynden, WA

When:  Saturday November 14th

Time: 
9:00am:    Bib pickup
9:30am:    1 mile Fun Run Starts
10:00am:  5k Race Starts

Cost: $15 per person or $45 per family with advance registration
             Day of event - $20 per person or $60 per family 
             *Registration is non-refundable

name: Metaline Falls Bigfoot 5K Race & LittleFoot Kids Run
description:
Bigfoot 5k Race - Saturday, June 20, 2026 at 8:00am

Join us at our 6th Annual Bigfoot 5k Race in beautiful Metaline Falls, WA on Saturday, June 20th at 8:00am! The course will take you from downtown Metaline Falls, up and down Lehigh Hill with gorgeous mountain views, past the historic Cutter Theatre, along the beautiful Pend Oreille river, and finish at the town's Busta Park.

After the event, join in at the fun festivities of the Metaline Falls Bigfoot Festival! There will be vendors, food, and entertainment!

A virtual race option is also available and swag will be mailed to you after the race!

Registration fee includes:

  • Long-sleeve tech material shirt
  • Finisher medal
  • Post-Race snacks
  • 1st, 2nd, & 3rd place medals for men's and women's categories

Bigfoot 5k Race Packet Pickup will take place on Friday and Saturday at Busta Park in Metaline Falls. We strongly encourage runners to attend the Friday packet pick-up to make your race morning less stressful. At packet pickup you will be able to retrieve your race bib and your shirt (if applicable).

Race packet pickup times are as follows:

  • Pre-race Packet Pickup: Friday, June 19 from 4:00 - 6:00 pm at Busta Park
  • Race day Packet Pickup: Saturday, June 20 from 6:00 - 7:30 am at Busta Park
     

 

LittleFoot Kids Run - Sunday, June 21, 2026 at 9:00am

Join us at our 1st Annual LittleFoot Kids Run! The race will begin and end at the Cutter Theatre, 302 Park Street, Metaline Falls, WA.

DISTANCE: The distance will be either 1K or 2K (you choose based on your abilities). This is a fun run that is not timed.

AGES: Ages 13 and under welcome and parents can participate with their small kiddos too. Parents don't need to register.

SWAG: All participants will receive a LittleFoot shirt and finisher medal. Be sure to register before June 1 to guarantee a shirt on race day. 

PACKET PICKUP: Sunday morning beginning at 8:00am.

name: Monster Dash 5K and Kids' Fun Run
description:
Spokane's Premier Halloween 5K Race and Kids' Fun Run.  Bring your costume.  Bring your shoes.  Let's dash!

Join us for the 18th Annual Monster Dash 5K Race and Kids' Fun Run, held in beautiful Manito Park on Spokane's South Hill. Enjoy autumn leaves. Show off your look. Run with friends. Monsters welcome.

You must register by end of day on October 12th to be guaranteed a shirt.  If you miss this cut-off, you can look for extra shirts after the race but quantities will be limited and first-come first-served.

 

Race Day - Sunday October 25, 2026

9:00am - Day-of bib and t-shirt pickup at the Lower Manito Park Picnic Shelter.

10:00am - The starting horn sounds to kick off the 5K Race. Dash!

11:00am - The Kids' Fun Run begins. Move those monster toes!

The Fun Run is offered at 1-mile, half-mile, and quarter-mile distances, each ending with candy goodie bags as kids cross the finish line. Grownups are welcome to walk or run next to their children on the entire course.

The 5K Race will be chip timed. Many parents complete the 5K on their own, then meet their children for the Fun Run. We love a family dash!

There will be prizes for overall winners and ribbons for age category winners.

----------------------------------

All proceeds from the race are donated to Active4Youth, a local non-profit that believes that by teaching sports and introducing healthy activities to children at a young age, we can begin to address the alarming rise of childhood obesity, while providing children with a safe place to play after school. Its elementary running program is provided at no cost to children in Spokane Public Schools, West Valley School District, and Central Valley School District.

$35 - 5K Race with T-Shirt *before or on October 12th*

$17 - Kids' Fun Run with T-Shirt *before or on October 12th*

name: My Better Half Marathon
description:
Prepare yourself for a running event like no other. Romance. Kitsch. Sweat. My Better Half Marathon is a celebration of running, romance and rom-coms. There are 4 categories: Bromance (two guy friends), Besties (two best friends), Lovers (romantically involved) and Lonely Hearts (self-explanatory). Join Orca Running, February 14th, 2027, as we celebrate love in all of its forms!

Lover's registration is for couples of all kinds! Bestie's registration is for two girlfriends, mom and daughter, guy and gal, or anyone you call your bestie. Bromance registration is for two dudes who probably don't want to admit that they're inseparable. Lonely Heart's registration is for those currently enjoying being single or looking for love.

The half marathon course is a total of 2 laps.  The first lap has a steep but quick hill early on and is 6.9 miles in length.  The second lap is 6.2 miles long and is nice and flat! The 10K course is a total of 2 laps.  The first lap has some hills in the beginning and is 3.7 miles long whereas the second lap is nice and flat and is 2.5 miles in length! The 5k course is 3.1 miles long.  A steep but quick hill in the beginning is a great warm-up but once you come back down it’s a breeze!

Half Marathon Relay: The relay course can be completed in any way you prefer, as long as both laps are completed.  Lap one is 6.9 miles long and has a quick but steep hill in the beginning, Lap two is 6.2 miles long and is nice and flat!  It doesn’t matter who completes which lap.  There is a relay hand off area just before the finish line (in the park gazebo) where you make the exchange from one runner to the other.

Your entry comes with long sleeve 1/4 zip shirt, finisher medal, hot post-race oatmeal, and free race photos!

The My Better Half Marathon supports Rebuilding Seattle Together.

name: Never Ending Nolte 6-Hour
description:
What is it? 

A 6-Hour race around scenic Nolte State Park, featuring a 1.4 mile loop course. With minimal elevation gain, crushed gravel/packed dirt terrain, and few roots and rocks, this course is and accessible to every level of runner/walker. It's also pretty speedy for those looking to chase 50k PRs. Yes, it is November and the weather may be awful, but that's all part of the fun. Half sufferfest and half party, NEN is a celebration of running and the fellowship it creates.

This year, we will be waiving registration fees and accepting optional donations to benefit the Washington Trail Association (WTA). So come get loopy, make friends, and support a good cause. This event is more about building community than competition, but prizes will be awarded to the top male, female, and non-binary athletes.

Additional Information

  • There will be an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, and a limited amount of traditional ultra running snacks. Participants are encouraged to bring something to contribute to the aid station if they have the means to do so. Bringing your own reusable cup is also highly appreciated.
  • Nolte has a large parking lot and road parking is also permitted. The gate to the park opens at 8am and a Discover Pass is required.
  • No running with dogs-Unfortunately, while the park allows dogs, our insurance does not. Dogs may be present, if they are leashed and minded by someone besides the runner, but they cannot run with participants during the race.
  • Pacing-It is a public park and friends and family can be on the course with you, but please be respectful of other visitors. If the park is crowded (unlikely during November, but you never know), please don't run with a large entourage.
  • Permitting for this event is still in process, but should be approved (per the park ranger). In the event NEN does not receive permitting, everyone will have the opportunity to recoup their donations.

name: New Year's Day 5K & 8K and Prediction 5K & 8K
description:
New Year’s Day 5K & 8K — Traditional & Prediction Race 🎉🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️

Start 2027 on the right foot!

Join us for a fun and inspiring New Year’s Day run/walk as we celebrate new beginnings, fresh goals, and endless possibilities. Whether you're chasing a new personal record, kickstarting a healthier lifestyle, or simply enjoying time outdoors with friends and family, this is the perfect way to welcome the New Year.

You choose how you want to race — Traditional or Prediction!

⏱️ Take the Prediction Challenge

Choose the Prediction 5K (3.1 miles) or Prediction 8K (4.97 miles) and predict how long you think it will take you to finish.

Here’s the twist: NO watches, phones, GPS devices, earbuds giving pace updates, or other timing devices allowed! You’ll have to rely completely on your own internal clock.

Your predicted finish time will be submitted the morning of the race, and the official computer time will determine your actual finish. Prediction awards go to the participants who finish closest to their predicted time — not necessarily the fastest!

🏃 Or Keep It Traditional

Not into predicting your time? No problem! Choose the Traditional 5K or 8K and simply run or walk your race.

Set a new PR, work toward a new goal, or just enjoy a scenic course and a great morning with the running and walking community.

Please note: There are NO overall top-finisher prizes for the Traditional 5K or 8K. This option is all about your time, your goals, and starting 2027 your way!

🏆 Prediction Race Awards

For participants registered in the Prediction 5K & 8K, prizes will be awarded to:

5K — Overall Top 3 Male & Female
8K — Overall Top 3 Male & Female

However you choose to tackle it — Traditional or Prediction, 5K or 8K — come celebrate the first day of 2027 with us!

✨ New Year. New Goals. New Achievements.

All participants will receive:
Finisher Medal, guaranteed until December 1st
Race Bib
Post-Race Snacks
A memorable way to begin the New Year

This event is open to runners and walkers of all abilities. Gather your friends, family, and running/walking buddies and make the New Year's Day 5K & 8K part of your annual tradition.

Let's celebrate a fresh start, new adventures, and the exciting journey ahead!

Long Sleeve Lifestyle Shirts available for purchase: 
                $25 sm- XL
                $30 2XL - 3XL
Shirts available until December 5th

Sorry, Absolutely No Dogs!  Our insurance does not cover our furry friends.

No selling, transfers or refunds.

name: New Year's Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
🎉 Start Your Year on the Right Foot! 🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️
Join the New Year's Run - New Beginnings Starts Today!
Kick off the new year with energy, excitement, and a community of runners ready to chase their goals for the New Year!

 
Forget the massive, impersonal race-day crowds. We keep things small, personal, and local, so every run feels less like a number and more like a memory. Whether it's a 5K, 10K, half-marathon, or virtual run, you'll get the warmth of a hometown event.
Overview:
Spots sell out FAST! We close each wave the moment it fills. Once a wave sells out, you can grab the virtual run option or join the waitlist.
This is a smaller, private group run with a capped field per wave - so it never feels crowded, and you're never just a bib number.
All paces and ages welcome (under 18 with a guardian) - run it, walk it, however you like!
There's no gear, no setup, no fuss - just you, the course, and our coordinators cheering you on in a relaxed, stress-free setting.
When you sign up, you're not just registering for a race - you're getting real support toward your fitness goals, plus an invite to join one of our local run clubs to keep the momentum going.
 
Timing:
Optional! Track your own time via Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, or similar, then submit it through our easy online form to get posted.
Or just ask a coordinator to help time you.
No timing chips - this is about progress, not pressure.
 
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-shirt (shipped to your address - US only)
- Finisher's medal
- Virtual Training Run (emailed to you a month before your run)
- Online results & certificate of completion
- Invitation to join a local running club
- NEW: Upgrade to a lightweight, moisture-wicking technical shirt for just $5 more
 
Packet Pickup?
Skip It. No lines, no hassle - your swag ships straight to your door. (Double-check your full US mailing address, including apartment number, when you register as your shirt is sent to this address!) Race bibs are simply handed out on race day.
 
When Will My Swag Arrive?
Your shirt will land at your mailing address the week of your race.
 
Signing Up Last Minute? (Within 2 Weeks of the Race)
No problem - just know shipping may not catch up in time, so your shirt could arrive after race day. No worries, though: wear whatever you like and come run with us anyway!
 
When Will I Receive get the Course Map and Details?
We'll send a final participant info by the Wednesday before race day with all the details and course maps.
 
Wave Times (Once you've registered, use your confirmation number to reserve a wave here.)
Wave A: 7:30 AM
Wave B: 8:00 AM
Wave C: 8:30 AM
Running late? Jump in when you arrive - our coordinators stay on-site for 3 hours after the first wave. Times may be subject to change depending on seasons, please check your participant info email!
Got more questions? Check our FAQ.
 
Virtual Run Option
Prefer to run on your own time? Our Virtual Run includes a digital training pack to keep you on track. Run it whenever, wherever, with any tracking device you like (optional) — then send your results to info@thebestraces.com to claim your medal.
 
Race Bundle
Sign up for multiple races and save with a bundle discount.
 
Sponsorships & Promoting Your Business
Want to put your business in front of our community? We'd love to feature you as a sponsor. Learn more
 
Team Glo Volunteers
Love helping people cross finish lines? Join our volunteer team and help bring these community runs to life. Sign up here
 
Be Part of the Journey
Discover our charity initiatives at https://www.thebestraces.com/runforothers/
Got a mission that helps people around the world? Let us help you fundraise at no cost to you.
 
Smaller Races, Warm Memories, Always Ready for You

name: North Olympic Discovery Marathon (5K / 10K/ Half / Full / Relay / Kids Marathon)
description:
The North Olympic Discovery Marathon, Marathon Walk, Marathon Relay and Half Marathon take place on a unique point to point course that incorporates the beautiful Olympic Discovery Trail with stunning views of the Olympic Mountains and a five mile finishing stretch along the shores of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. The 10K,  5K and Kids Marathon are an out-and-back along the shores of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. 

Frequent sightings of seals, eagles, and an array of shore birds are common from the trail. Iconic trestle bridges provide beautiful back drops. Salmon can be seen spawning at the Morse Creek crossing in the fall. The North Olympic Discovery Marathon is truly one of the most beautiful marathon venues anywhere.

This rails to trails course is a wide, hard surface (99% paved) trail. The course is marked at every mile and water stations are located approximately every two miles. Cool June weather can be expected  – average high is 65F, average low is 49F, average mean is 57F.

The race is organized by the Port Angeles Marathon Association – a group of accomplished amateur athletes.

The Marathon is a USATF certified course and a Boston Marathon qualifier.

name: Northshore Spring 5k for Schools
description:
A Community 5K for Every Pace


A day of movement, connection, and community impact! The Northshore Spring 5K for Schools is proudly presented and hosted by the Northshore Schools Foundation, bringing our community together in support of local students and schools.

Taking place in June 2027, this inclusive event welcomes participants of all ages and abilities! You can run the full 5K, walk with friends, strolling with a stroller, or cheer from the sidelines. 

What to Expect

The scenic 5K course starts and ends on the University of Washington Bothell campus, with the race route running along the Sammamish River Trail.

Every finisher will cross the line to a festive finish area featuring local vendors, family-friendly activities, refreshments, and opportunities to connect with neighbors and supporters of our schools and Northshore Schools Foundation.

What You're Supporting

Proceeds from the Northshore Spring 5K for Schools will support and advance Northshore Schools Foundation's service work for over 22,000 students across Bothell, Woodinville, and Kenmore in all 36 Northshore schools and programs.

Learn more about what we do, click here.

As an inaugural event, every participant becomes part of the 5K race's story. Join us as we launch into an annual spring tradition that brings together runners, walkers, families, educators, students, and community partners for a morning of fun, fitness, and purpose!

Race Highlights

  • Certified 5K course open to runners and walkers of all ages and paces
  • Chip timing with age group awards
  • Finisher medal for all participants
  • Family-friendly atmosphere
  • Music, refreshments, and post-race celebration
  • Supporting local Northshore schools and students with every registration

Lace up your running shoes, gather your friends and family, and help us kick off Northshore Schools Foundation's very first Northshore Spring 5K for Schools. Together, we'll be All In for Kids!

name: OAT Run
description:
* 50K * Half Marathon * 12K *

The Olympic Adventure Trail Run (OAT Run) is a point-to-point trail 12K and half marathon as well as an out-and-back 50K that traverses Kelly Ridge between the Olympic National Park and the Strait of Juan de Fuca in Washington State, all on single-track trail.  Limit 130 runners per distance.

The OAT Run Experience

OAT Run is for trail runners who enjoy lush green forests filled with moss and ferns, towering evergreens, and spring trailside flowers. Runners will get a stunning view of the Elwha River Valley as they run by the “Living Room”. And if this wasn’t epic enough, get ready to eat, drink, and relax post-race with an amazing view of the Olympic Mountains. The after-party at Extreme Sports Park is a fun atmosphere, and racers will get hot burritos from Little Devil's Lunchbox and cold drinks, a toasty campfire, and door prizes (woot!). There will be a beer garden at the after-party as well, with proceeds to support 4PA, a local non-profit organization. 

What’s included?

In addition to an epic outdoor experience in the far northwest corner, all runners receive a professional well-organized event, a well-marked course, hydration and snacks at water stations along the course, a great piece of custom race swag, shuttle to start (and return shuttle back to parking area / party), chip timing, race photos, and after-party at Extreme Sports Park including a hot meal and a chance to win great door prizes from our local retailers. 

Bring cash or card as there will be a beer garden at the finish line, hosted by and benefitting local non-profit organization 4PA. 

This race sells out every year, so don't delay registering!

Giving Back

This race is a friendly, community-based event, and a portion of race proceeds is donated to the Peninsula Trails Coalition (Olympic Discovery Trail) and the Peninsula Chapter of the Back Country Horsemen of Washington, in appreciation for their countless hours of trail construction and maintenance on the North Olympic Peninsula.

Where to stay
Olympic Lodge in Port Angeles is offering a special 25% off discount for OAT Runners.
Booking link here. 
Or phone direct at 360-452-2993 and use booking code OAT to receive the same discounted pricing.

REFUND POLICY:
  • 50% refund available until March 15, NO REFUNDS AFTER THIS DATE. No deferrals to another race or next year's race.
  • You will have the choice during the registration process to buy cancellation insurance (unavailable for Canadian racers 
     - rules of the insurance company and not us or RunSignUp). With the insurance, you will get a full refund in certain circumstances including accident, illness and family emergency, even after the March 15th date. Here are details and FAQ about the RegShield insurance.
  • Transfers are allowed until 3 days before the race  Transfer instructions.
  • No deferrals
  • If we are forced to cancel for any reason, runners will get a free transfer to the next year, or an 80% refund

name: One Step Closer
description:
What do you get when you take Orca Running and mix it with Evergreen Trail!? Welcome to One Step Closer. An exciting summer endurance event created by Orca Running AND Evergreen Trail Runs. Part whale, part trail-and loopy. Held in the one and only Lincoln Park, this race is going to be THE summer endurance event you won’t want to miss.

Course: Loops at Lincoln Park. Amazingly diverse for its size, this race experience has a bit of everything. Runners will take on a 2 mile course loop, and complete the loop as many times as they can during their selected time period: 18 hours, 12 hours, 6 hours, or 3 hours. All runners will finish together at 10:00pm with a finish line party! 

Check out all the details on our website!

NEW for 2026:

Battle of the run clubs: During registration, you will have the opportunity to be part of a “team.” Teams can consist of 2-5 members and The top 3 teams with the most loops at the end of the event will earn a special finishers plaque and ultimate run club (or friend group) bragging rights.

Kid's Loopy Race:  Kid’s will complete as many loops around the baseball field as they can within 30 minutes. Kids can take as many breaks as they choose, and the course will run through the snack station for treats as they go (just like the adults). All of the kids will finish together in a special One Step Closer kid’s race celebration. Each Kid’s Race runner will be awarded a One Step Closer medal upon completion.

Part whale, part trail-and loopy. Held in the one and only Lincoln Park, this race is going to be THE summer endurance event you won’t want to miss.

Course: Loops at Lincoln Park. Amazingly diverse for its size, this race experience has a bit of everything. Runners will take on a 2 mile course loop, and complete the loop as many times as they can during their selected time period: 18 hours, 12 hours, 6 hours, or 3 hours. All runners will finish together at 10:00pm with a finish line party! 

Check out all the details on our website!

NEW for 2026:

Battle of the run clubs: During registration, you will have the opportunity to be part of a “team.” Teams can consist of 2-5 members and The top 3 teams with the most loops at the end of the event will earn a special finishers plaque and ultimate run club (or friend group) bragging rights.

Kid's Loopy Race:  Kid’s will complete as many loops around the baseball field as they can within 30 minutes. Kids can take as many breaks as they choose, and the course will run through the snack station for treats as they go (just like the adults). All of the kids will finish together in a special One Step Closer kid’s race celebration. Each Kid’s Race runner will be awarded a One Step Closer medal upon completion.

name: PB&J Fuel Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
Smooth vibes. Sweet energy. Bold moves. 🥜🍓


PB&J Fuel Run is all about a combo that just works. Mix your pace, spread the fun, and stick with it all the way to the finish. No stress, no expectations, just miles that feel good and a finish that feels even better. Run it your way, enjoy every step, and fuel your finish with good energy and great company. Let’s make this run unforgettable. 🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️✨

 
Forget the massive, impersonal race-day crowds. We keep things small, personal, and local, so every run feels less like a number and more like a memory. Whether it's a 5K, 10K, half-marathon, or virtual run, you'll get the warmth of a hometown event.
Overview:
Spots sell out FAST! We close each wave the moment it fills. Once a wave sells out, you can grab the virtual run option or join the waitlist.
This is a smaller, private group run with a capped field per wave - so it never feels crowded, and you're never just a bib number.
All paces and ages welcome (under 18 with a guardian) - run it, walk it, however you like!
There's no gear, no setup, no fuss - just you, the course, and our coordinators cheering you on in a relaxed, stress-free setting.
When you sign up, you're not just registering for a race - you're getting real support toward your fitness goals, plus an invite to join one of our local run clubs to keep the momentum going.
 
Timing:
Optional! Track your own time via Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, or similar, then submit it through our easy online form to get posted.
Or just ask a coordinator to help time you.
No timing chips - this is about progress, not pressure.
 
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-shirt (shipped to your address - US only)
- Finisher's medal
- Virtual Training Run (emailed to you a month before your run)
- Online results & certificate of completion
- Invitation to join a local running club
- NEW: Upgrade to a lightweight, moisture-wicking technical shirt for just $5 more
 
Packet Pickup?
Skip It. No lines, no hassle - your swag ships straight to your door. (Double-check your full US mailing address, including apartment number, when you register as your shirt is sent to this address!) Race bibs are simply handed out on race day.
 
When Will My Swag Arrive?
Your shirt will land at your mailing address the week of your race.
 
Signing Up Last Minute? (Within 2 Weeks of the Race)
No problem - just know shipping may not catch up in time, so your shirt could arrive after race day. No worries, though: wear whatever you like and come run with us anyway!
 
When Will I Receive get the Course Map and Details?
We'll send a final participant info by the Wednesday before race day with all the details and course maps.
 
Wave Times (Once you've registered, use your confirmation number to reserve a wave here.)
Wave A: 7:30 AM
Wave B: 8:00 AM
Wave C: 8:30 AM
Running late? Jump in when you arrive - our coordinators stay on-site for 3 hours after the first wave. Times may be subject to change depending on seasons, please check your participant info email!
Got more questions? Check our FAQ.
 
Virtual Run Option
Prefer to run on your own time? Our Virtual Run includes a digital training pack to keep you on track. Run it whenever, wherever, with any tracking device you like (optional) — then send your results to info@thebestraces.com to claim your medal.

name: Peaks and Professors 5k
description:
Peaks and Professors 5K Run/Walk
Saturday, October 24th | Red Square, University of Washington

Get ready for the most adventurous race of the quarter — the first-ever Peaks and Professors 5K! Lace up and join us for a scenic route around the University of Washington campus, starting and finishing in our very own Red Square (full route attached below).

📅 When: Saturday, October 24th, 8:00 AM – 11:00 AM
📍 Where: UW Campus, starting & finishing at Red Square
🎽 Packet Pickup: 8:00 AM in Red Square
🏁 Race Start: 9:00 AM sharp, with a 90-minute time limit

Whether you're here to compete for the podium, jog alongside new friends and fellow hikers, or simply enjoy a scenic stroll around campus, this is the race for you. 

🎉 Post-Race Party
Stick around after the race for live music, free snacks, Peaks and Professors merch, and tons of sponsored giveaways — all in Red Square!

Why It Matters
Peaks and Professors is a Registered Student Organization (RSO) and up-and-coming nonprofit at UW, on a mission to bridge the gap between academia and the outdoors. We lead students and faculty on accessible hikes, camping trips, and outdoor adventures across Western Washington — and this 5K is our biggest fundraiser of the year. Every dollar raised goes directly toward our outdoor education workshops and wilderness accessibility programs, breaking down financial barriers for students seeking time outside.

Come run, cheer, and celebrate with us — we can't wait to see you at the starting line!

Official Route

name: Popsicle 5K/10K/Half - Portland (Washougal)
description:
Beat the heat and treat yourself at the Popsicle 5K/10K/Half Marathon—a sweet celebration of summer miles and frozen rewards. Whether you’re racing the speedy 5K, cruising through the 10K, or going the distance in the Half Marathon, this event is designed to be fun, festive, and refreshingly cool from start to finish.
We will be gathering at Captain William Clark Park.
When you cross the finish line, your reward is waiting: a delicious, ice-cold popsicle to help you chill out and celebrate your accomplishment. Every finisher will also receive a custom Popsicle-themed finisher medal—bright, bold, and worthy of showing off.

name: Pumpkin Spice Run
description:
New for 2026: We will have a big pumpkin festival going on during the event. We will have games, face painting, and more! We are also adding a .25 mile stroller dash.

This race is perfect for the runner who believes all seasons should be pumpkin season. Frolic through the leaves of scenic Seward Park, with a pumpkin spice twist. Choose from the 1 mile pumpkin dash, stroller dash, 5K, or 10K distance. We will also have a Kid’s Race for our littlest pumpkins.

Need some extra spice? Pick a pumpkin from our mini pumpkin patch and run with it! Finish to a festive fall finish line celebration and fresh Pumpkin Spice Latte (included with your registration). This will be the most basic race you have ever attended, and we can’t wait!

name: Puyallup Trail Challenge
description:
Are You Ready to Accept the Challenge?
Join us on Saturday, July 24, 2027, for the Puyallup Trail Challenge—a true test of endurance, strategy, and determination.

Your mission? Complete three 5K trails in the allotted time. You'll have 45 minutes to finish each 5K, followed by 30 minutes to travel to the next park and prepare for the next start. As the day progresses, each trail becomes more challenging, pushing both your physical and mental limits.

The challenge is simple:
Finish each 5K within the 45-minute time limit.
Arrive at the next starting line before the scheduled start time.
Miss the cutoff or fail to be at the next start on time, and your challenge ends.

Think you have what it takes to conquer all three trails?
Participation is limited to 100 registrants, so don't wait to claim your spot.

Awards for top finisher prizes will be presented to the top two overall finishers in each of the following categories:

  • Male
  • Female
  • Nonbinary

Are you up to the challenge?

Cost: 
Early Bird: August 6th - August 10th - $80 
Open Registration: August 11th - March 31st - $95
Not to Late April 1st - June 24th - $105
Still time: June 25th - July 24th - $120 

Create a team of 4 and save $20 (Save $5 per person. Must create or join a team during registration)Price includes:

  • Chipped time
  • Commemorative shirt (add $5 for 2XL & 3XL) 
  • Finisher Medal
  • After Race Snacks 

Pinless • Cupless • Paperless
The Puyallup Trail Challenge is committed to sustainable racing. This event is pinless, cupless, and paperless to help reduce waste and protect the beautiful Pacific Northwest trails we enjoy.
Pinless: Use a bib belt or BibBoards instead of disposable safety pins.
Cupless: Bring your own reusable hydration bottle, vest, or handheld flask.
Paperless: All race information, results, and participant communications are delivered digitally.
Together, we're proving that every step can make a positive impact. Run for today. Sustain for tomorrow.

RaceJoy App Requirement & Safety Disclaimer
For participant safety, all registrants are required to download and use the free RaceJoy app during the event. RaceJoy provides real-time participant tracking and helps event staff quickly locate and assist participants in the event of an emergency or other safety concern.
By registering for this event, you acknowledge that the RaceJoy app is a mandatory safety requirement and agree to have it installed and active on your mobile device throughout your participation.  Here is the link to RaceJoy:  RaceJoy - Changing the Race Experience!

Saturday, July 24, 2027

Riverwalk Trail (behind Fred Meyer), 1100 N. Meridian, Puyallup 98371
🚗 10:15 AM – Race #2 Begins
Wildwood Park, 1101 23rd Ave., Puyallup 98371
🚗 11:30 AM – Race #3 Begins
Clarks Creek South (Puyallup Loop Trail), 1710 12th Ave, Puyallup 98371

🚫 ABSOLUTELY NO DOGS — pets are not allowed on the course for the safety of all participants, and our insurance does not allow pets.

🚫ABSOLUTELY NO strollers.

name: Puyallup Valley Fall Hops Harvest 5K
description:
Celebrate the beauty of fall at the Puyallup Valley Fall Hops Harvest 5K on Sunday, October 18th at Firemind Brewing in downtown Puyallup! Gather your friends and family for this festive fall run/walk that combines fitness, community, and the flavors of the season.

Participants will enjoy a fun 3-loop course through downtown Puyallup while taking in the sights and crisp autumn air.  After each loop, enjoy a tasting of local fall beers or ciders and celebrate the flavors of the season with friends and fellow runners!


Please note: Participants must be 21 years of age or older to partake in beer or cider sampling. Valid ID is required at check-in for a tasting wristband.

After your run/walk, stick around and enjoy delicious food from the Radnor's Burgers and Beignets Food Truck, festive fall beverages, and great conversation with fellow participants.  Whether you are chasing a PR, walking with friends, or simply looking for a fun way to celebrate the season, the Puyallup Valley Fall Hops Harvest 5K is the perfect fall event.

Sorry, no dogs allowed. 

Space is limited, so don’t wait to register!  

Price includes Commemorative Bib, Finisher Medal, Entry into Prize drawing, and after race snacks. 

Items available for purchase:

  • Short Sleeve Lifestyle shirts $20 for Small - XL, $25 for 2XL - 3XL 
  • Commemorative JunkBrand Headband $18
  • Commemorative Pint Glass $13

PINLESS • CUPLESS • PAPERLESS
At All Things Fun Sports!, we work hard to reduce the waste footprint of our events. You’ll hear us say that our events are Pinless, Cupless & Paperless — but what does that actually mean?

PINLESS — We encourage you to skip the safety pins and use a bib belt or BibBoards. If you don’t have either, BibBoards and bib belts will be available for purchase at check-in. Prefer traditional safety pins? No problem! You are welcome to bring your own safety pins.

CUPLESS — There are no disposable cups at our events. Please bring your own handheld bottle, hydration vest, or reusable cup. Help us cut down on race-day waste while keeping our trails clean.

PAPERLESS — Race information, course information, updates, and results are provided digitally whenever possible. Please download the FREE RaceJoy app before race day. RaceJoy puts important race information right on your phone and helps us eliminate unnecessary printed materials on race morning.

It’s a few small changes that can make a BIG difference.
Pinless • Cupless • Paperless — Run for Today, Sustain for Tomorrow.

name: Redmond Harvest Half Marathon
description: Harvest the fruits of your training at the Redmond Harvest Half Marathon, to be held Labor Day Monday (September 7, 2026)! Starting from the Redmond Town Center (new for 2026!), the Harvest Half is a fast, flat out-and-back half-marathon that does a short loop around town before going out-and-back north on the Sammamish River Trail. Whether this is your first half-marathon, or you are experienced with this distance, this 13.1-mile course will give you an opportunity for your running goals to come to fruition. Come support a local, all volunteer-organized race put on by Lake Sammamish Run Club and Seattle United Runners and finish your summer with a bang.

name: Resolution Run
description: Double the course and double the fun! Welcome to the 5th Annual Resolution Run in La Center, Washington as it continues to be a fundraiser for the La Center High School Volleyball program and the Track & Field program. We brought together all of our favorite things, a challenging course to kickup your New Year training program, trails and pathways along a very scenic course, and a good old-fashioned breakfast. You will start and finish at La Center High School - one loop for the 5K and a slightly different course for the 10K to really kick up the resolution challenge a notch. Watch out for those fast track stars as they use their bib to fundraise.  After your race, join us in the cafeteria for an all you can eat pancake and sausage with your $10 donation supporting the La Center High School Volleyball program. An awards ceremony for the overall top 3 finishers and age group winners will be provided. There will be fun for all!!

name: Resolution Run 5K and Polar Bear Dive - 2027
description:
The Resolution Run is a 5K run/walk and finish festival celebrating the start of the New Year, with an optional Polar Plunge into Lake Washington.

Free chili, hot chocolate, apple cider! ★ Over 60 divisional prizes! ★ Long sleeve shirt or medal! ★ Free kids dash! ★ Beer garden (21+) if New Years Eve wasn’t enough!

Polar PLUNGE
The optional Polar Bear Dive into Lake Washington is located just before the finish line. About 60% of runners chose the Polar Bear Dive. We will have two heated gender specific changing room tents onsite for participants to change into dry clothes. Polar plunge and “dry” 5k results scored separately.

name: Richland RunFest 2027
description:
RICHLAND RUNFEST 2026 is presented by 3 Rivers Road Runners (3RRR)

DISTANCES:

  • Half Marathon, 10K and 5K (both in person and virtual options)
  • There will be a medal for each race (and they will fit together to make one big medal if you do all 3!!!)
  • You can register for one in person option and then the other distances virtually or all 3 races virtually to obtain all three medals that will fit together to make one cool medal.
  • Did I mention--Do all 3 races and you get 3 medals that go together to get one big medal--you have 3 weeks to complete the virtual options PRIOR to the in person race date and 1 week AFTER the in person race date and you get a discount.

DATES:

  • In Person Race: Saturday, February 28, 2026 
  • Virtual Race Window:  Friday February 6, 2026 to Friday, March 6, 2026 at 11:59 pm.

TIMES:

  • Half Marathon will start at 8:30am
  • 10K and 5K will start at 8:45am
  • ALL race courses close at 12:30 PM.

WHERE:  

  • Richland, WA
  • Start and Finish will be at Columbia Point Marina Park 
  • Use the address of 660 Columbia Point Drive, Richland WA 99354 for GPS directions.

FACEBOOK

  • Please like us on Facebook for updates and inspiration: www.facebook.com/richlandrunfest.
  • This year we have a running group and training plan (both beginner and intermediate/advanced) for ALL distances: the half marathon, 10K and 5K.  See Facebook for details or see the running group and training plan section.

REGISTRATION:

 

RACE DISTANCE

Until 11/16/2025

11/17/2025 to 12/31/2025

1/1/2026 to 1/31/2026

2/1/2026 to 2/28/2026**

 

Half Marathon

  • Online registration ends WHEN THE RACES FILL UP (if they don't fill up there will be race day signup), FOR VIRTUAL RACES on Wednesday, February 6, at 8 PM (For those with injuries or conflicts and need to switch to the virtual, that can be approved by the race director after that date. 
  • The entry fees include a finisher medal, light weight hoodie pullover shirt (for the half marathon only, 10K and 5K can purchase for additional cost), finish line treats (for the in person races), a surprise gift, and great company with our awesome volunteers and fellow runners (for the in person races).  
    The 10K and 5K can purchase the shirt option separately for $25 extra (until the shirt cutoff date of 2/6/2026).
  • **The cut off for shirts will be 2/6/2026. Shirts are only available for purchase by 10K and 5K runners and guaranteed for half marathon runners registered by 2/6/2026.  Shirts will be available at packet pick up on Friday and after the race on race day on a first come, first serve basis if you register after 2/6/2026.  We appreciate your understanding with this deadline that allows us to finalize event details. Shirts will be a light weight hoodie pullover (similar to the past years)**
  • All runners (virtual and in person) will need to pick up their race packets at packet pickup, those virtual runners wanting their packets mailed will need to choose the additional mailing option at check out!  If you don't pick the mailing option you will not get your packet mailed to you.  All virtual packets being mailed well be done at the latest 1-2 weeks AFTER the close of the virtual window (3/6/2026).  
  • There will be a $25 discount if you (same person) register for all 3 races (example:  the in person half marathon and the 10K and 5K virtual).
  • For every participant that signs up (in person race or virtual) we will be donating $2.50 to a local charity, Grace Collective; and  $2.50 to be split amongst our local school and community groups that man our aid stations.  For more information please check out the Grace Collective Website and the charity section below for our local groups.  
  • If you are a current 3RRR club member, your entry fee is $3 less for the half and $2 less for the 10K and 5K.  Please select that option for the discount when registering. 
    SIGN UP EARLY TO SAVE!!  
  • The in person races will have a maximum of 250 runners in the half marathon, 250 in the 10k, and 250 in the 5k. 
  • There may be packet pick up registration the day before the race and race day ONLY if there is space remaining, please sign up early.
  • You may change between race distances on-line under your race account up until 2/27/2026.  You will be charged the difference in cost if you are going up in distance, if you are going down in distance there is no extra charge-but you will not get a refund.
  • THERE ARE NO REFUNDS OR DEFERRALS.  We appreciate your understanding with our policies as a non-profit, volunteer led race, we have to balance our policies with what we can reliably provide for our runners. If life events or injury prevent you from running you can always switch to the virtual option at no charge and run it when you can (you can chose to pick up your packet at packet pick up or pay the shipping fee and it will be sent to you with all the other virtual runners who picked the mailing option).

PACKET PICKUP:

  • Packet Pickup will be on Friday February 27, 2026 from 3:30-6 pm. 
  • Location:  The Lodge at Columbia Point, 530 Columbia Point Drive, Richland, WA 99352
  • Packet Pickup will be on race morning from 7:30-8:15am ONLY for those coming from out of town (or by arrangement), locals please pick up your pack on Friday. Packet pick up will end at 8:15am race morning so don't be late.  PLEASE NOTE THIS IT NOT AT THE START AREA, it is about a 3-5 min walk from the start area.
  • For the virtual races, you MUST pick up your goodies at Packet Pickup as above or on Race Day.  If you are only doing virtual and want your goodies mailed to you then pick the shipping option (an additional charge will apply) and your packet will be sent to you 1-2 weeks after the conclusion of the virtual race window

THE IN PERSON RACE SET UP

  • Timing will be by chip.  There will be mats for timing at the start and finish.  
  • Every Finisher will receive a finisher medal--- all 3 race medals will fit together in a unique way, so you can do all three distances and it will be cool! 
  • There will be three aid stations on the course --one around mile 3 and one around mile 4.5 and 12 (same one you pass twice), and the third around mile 6.5 and 10 (same one you pass twice). 
  • The course will be about the same as last year so checkout the course maps below-it is not a flat course. 

RACE DAY PHOTOS

  • Chris Ruby is capturing your race day in photos!  
  • They will be available after the race at no charge to participants
  • Thank you Chris!
  • LINK TO THE FOTO RUBY PHOTO GALLERY and you can search the year--Click HERE  

RUNNING GROUP AND TRAINING PLAN

  • Again this year Jen Comfort of Jennifer Comfort Coaching is writing our training plans for the half marthon, 10K and 5K.  She has put together a beginner and intermediate plan for each distance so there should be something for everyone!!  Thanks Coach Jen.
  • I and several others from the run group will be leading the running group on Saturdays.  
  • The running group will be meeting on Saturday mornings at 6:45am (running by 7am) at the Wake Up Call Coffee (formerly Black Rock Coffee, formerly Roasters) on George Washington Way in Richland.  We ask that you park down in Howard Amon parking below and walk up to not overwhelm coffee shop parking lot.  All levels are welcome, we will be running the distances that are listed on the training plans but often others are running more or less.  Experienced runners are encouraged to attend (and now we have a training plan for you too) to help mentor those who are new to our beloved sport.
  • The Saturday runs will be posted on the Facebook page.
  • The training plan is posted here on this website and on the Facebook page as well. 
  • Remember that everyone is responsible for their own health and that they have checked with their doctor prior to participating.
  • If you are not a part of Facebook please just show up to a Saturday morning run and we will get you all the details you need (or contact me-the race director).

AWARDS

  • ONLY FOR THE IN PERSON RACES (virtual has no awards-only the finisher medals)
  • There will be an awards table to pick up your award at the race finish line (they will not be mailed out later).
  • OVERALL top three female finishers for each distance. 
  • OVERALL top three male finishers for each distance.
  • Age Group Awards: 14 and under, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80 and up

FINISH LINE

  • We will be following all health department and WA guidelines to have a safe in person race.
  • There will be bottled water and lots of prepackaged foods for all finishers.
  • More Info as we get closer to race day.
  • Last year we had a coffee truck and hope to have the same this year. 

RACE RESULTS:

  • All race results are posted at nsplit.com. 

VOLUNTEERING:

  • PLEASE consider having your friends or family members volunteer for the race.  The Volunteers make your race experience that much better.
  • If you know of anyone interested in volunteering, please have them contact Amanda Lang at richlandrunfest@gmail.com. or signup here on the website. 

OUR CHARITIES

  • Grace Collective (local): Grace Collective is a nonprofit that offers hope and opportunity for lasting change to women survivors of trafficking, addiction, homelessness and poverty. We do this by fostering a community of grace where women learn job and life skills that enable them to gain sustainable employment and a secure future for themselves and their children. AND Atlas Freedom: Their mission statement:  We exist to empower the rescue and restoration of those in sexual slavery and to prevent exploitation. 
  • Local School Bands that are playing and manning our aid stations.  So far we have Richland High School Band Program and will have another Band Program as well.  
  • For every race entry we will be donating $5 ($2.50 to Grace Collective/Atlas Freedom and $2.50 to the School Band Programs to split.
  • You can give additional donations, click on the donate at the top of the page or during registration.
  • Depending on how many sponsors we can get for the race we will also be donating additional monies.  If you know an organization that would like to sponsor please contact the race director (see below for information).

Any other questions, please email the race director, Amanda Lang, at richlandrunfest@gmail.com.  Please remember the race director is a volunteer and works a full time job that does not allow checking of phone, email or Facebook while at work.  Please be patient, I promise to get back to you, it just may take a day (or two/three in a really busy week).

  • The entry fees include a finisher medal, light weight hoodie pullover shirt (for the half marathon only, 10K and 5K can purchase for additional cost), finish line treats (for the in person races), a surprise gift, and great company with our awesome volunteers and fellow runners (for the in person races).  
    The 10K and 5K can purchase the shirt option separately for $25 extra (until the shirt cutoff date of 2/6/2026).
  • **The cut off for shirts will be 2/6/2026. Shirts are only available for purchase by 10K and 5K runners and guaranteed for half marathon runners registered by 2/6/2026.  Shirts will be available at packet pick up on Friday and after the race on race day on a first come, first serve basis if you register after 2/6/2026.  We appreciate your understanding with this deadline that allows us to finalize event details. Shirts will be a light weight hoodie pullover (similar to the past years)**
  • All runners (virtual and in person) will need to pick up their race packets at packet pickup, those virtual runners wanting their packets mailed will need to choose the additional mailing option at check out!  If you don't pick the mailing option you will not get your packet mailed to you.  All virtual packets being mailed well be done at the latest 1-2 weeks AFTER the close of the virtual window (3/6/2026).  
  • There will be a $25 discount if you (same person) register for all 3 races (example:  the in person half marathon and the 10K and 5K virtual).

  • If you are a current 3RRR club member, your entry fee is $3 less for the half and $2 less for the 10K and 5K.  Please select that option for the discount when registering. 
    SIGN UP EARLY TO SAVE!!  
  • The in person races will have a maximum of 250 runners in the half marathon, 250 in the 10k, and 250 in the 5k. 
  • There may be packet pick up registration the day before the race and race day ONLY if there is space remaining, please sign up early.

PACKET PICKUP:

  • Packet Pickup will be on Friday February 27, 2026 from 3:30-6 pm. 
  • Location:  The Lodge at Columbia Point, 530 Columbia Point Drive, Richland, WA 99352
  • Packet Pickup will be on race morning from 7:30-8:15am ONLY for those coming from out of town (or by arrangement), locals please pick up your pack on Friday. Packet pick up will end at 8:15am race morning so don't be late.  PLEASE NOTE THIS IT NOT AT THE START AREA, it is about a 3-5 min walk from the start area.
  • For the virtual races, you MUST pick up your goodies at Packet Pickup as above or on Race Day.  If you are only doing virtual and want your goodies mailed to you then pick the shipping option (an additional charge will apply) and your packet will be sent to you 1-2 weeks after the conclusion of the virtual race window

THE IN PERSON RACE SET UP

  • Timing will be by chip.  There will be mats for timing at the start and finish.  
  • Every Finisher will receive a finisher medal--- all 3 race medals will fit together in a unique way, so you can do all three distances and it will be cool! 
  • There will be three aid stations on the course --one around mile 3 and one around mile 4.5 and 12 (same one you pass twice), and the third around mile 6.5 and 10 (same one you pass twice). 
  • The course will be about the same as last year so checkout the course maps below-it is not a flat course. 

RACE DAY PHOTOS

  • Chris Ruby is capturing your race day in photos!  
  • They will be available after the race at no charge to participants
  • Thank you Chris!
  • LINK TO THE FOTO RUBY PHOTO GALLERY and you can search the year--Click HERE  

RUNNING GROUP AND TRAINING PLAN

  • Again this year Jen Comfort of Jennifer Comfort Coaching is writing our training plans for the half marthon, 10K and 5K.  She has put together a beginner and intermediate plan for each distance so there should be something for everyone!!  Thanks Coach Jen.
  • I and several others from the run group will be leading the running group on Saturdays.  
  • The running group will be meeting on Saturday mornings at 6:45am (running by 7am) at the Wake Up Call Coffee (formerly Black Rock Coffee, formerly Roasters) on George Washington Way in Richland.  We ask that you park down in Howard Amon parking below and walk up to not overwhelm coffee shop parking lot.  All levels are welcome, we will be running the distances that are listed on the training plans but often others are running more or less.  Experienced runners are encouraged to attend (and now we have a training plan for you too) to help mentor those who are new to our beloved sport.
  • The Saturday runs will be posted on the Facebook page.
  • The training plan is posted here on this website and on the Facebook page as well. 
  • Remember that everyone is responsible for their own health and that they have checked with their doctor prior to participating.
  • If you are not a part of Facebook please just show up to a Saturday morning run and we will get you all the details you need (or contact me-the race director).

AWARDS

  • ONLY FOR THE IN PERSON RACES (virtual has no awards-only the finisher medals)
  • There will be an awards table to pick up your award at the race finish line (they will not be mailed out later).
  • OVERALL top three female finishers for each distance. 
  • OVERALL top three male finishers for each distance.
  • Age Group Awards: 14 and under, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80 and up

FINISH LINE

  • We will be following all health department and WA guidelines to have a safe in person race.
  • There will be bottled water and lots of prepackaged foods for all finishers.
  • More Info as we get closer to race day.
  • Last year we had a coffee truck and hope to have the same this year. 

RACE RESULTS:

  • All race results are posted at nsplit.com. 

VOLUNTEERING:

  • PLEASE consider having your friends or family members volunteer for the race.  The Volunteers make your race experience that much better.
  • If you know of anyone interested in volunteering, please have them contact Amanda Lang at richlandrunfest@gmail.com. or signup here on the website. 

OUR CHARITIES

  • Grace Collective (local): Grace Collective is a nonprofit that offers hope and opportunity for lasting change to women survivors of trafficking, addiction, homelessness and poverty. We do this by fostering a community of grace where women learn job and life skills that enable them to gain sustainable employment and a secure future for themselves and their children. AND Atlas Freedom: Their mission statement:  We exist to empower the rescue and restoration of those in sexual slavery and to prevent exploitation. 
  • Local School Bands that are playing and manning our aid stations.  So far we have Richland High School Band Program and will have another Band Program as well.  
  • For every race entry we will be donating $5 ($2.50 to Grace Collective/Atlas Freedom and $2.50 to the School Band Programs to split.
  • You can give additional donations, click on the donate at the top of the page or during registration.
  • Depending on how many sponsors we can get for the race we will also be donating additional monies.  If you know an organization that would like to sponsor please contact the race director (see below for information).

Any other questions, please email the race director, Amanda Lang, at richlandrunfest@gmail.com.  Please remember the race director is a volunteer and works a full time job that does not allow checking of phone, email or Facebook while at work.  Please be patient, I promise to get back to you, it just may take a day (or two/three in a really busy week).

name: Rock Solid Marathon, Half Marathon
description:
The third annual Rock Solid Marathon & Half Marathon (RSM) will take place on Saturday, February 27 at 9:00 am PST in Coupeville, Washington on Whidbey Island. Both races feature an unforgettable course with winding coastal roads and scenic trails. The races start and finish at Goldie's and The Roost in the heart of historic Coupeville. The course will first take runners across the island over to the rugged beauty of Ebey's Landing, then through the Kettles Trail System's windy paths. The Half Marathon will then follow Madrona Way along Penn Cove and its famous mussel beds, passing by the the rustic Captain Whidbey Inn, before coming back into Coupeville and finishing at a party at Goldie's. The Marathon will diverge after the Kettles trails to take on a few miles of natural beach and meandering country roads of Whidbey Island, then finally along Penn Cove to converge with the Half Marathon route on Madrona Way to the finish. Course maps and details are provided in the Events section below.

All runners will receive a custom race t-shirt and finisher medal.

Goldie's and The Roost will serve as race headquarters all weekend. The upstairs bar and restaurant at The Roost will host a packet pickup and pizza party on Friday evening before the race, and all of Goldie's will be hopping on race day from start to finish. Race awards and speeches will take place at 3pm on Saturday.

All profits from the RSM event will be donated to The Rock Solid Foundation, a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit charity. Check the Donation option during registration for more information on the Foundation and how to donate directly to help us meet our fundraising goal.

We can't wait to see you on Whidbey Island!

name: Royal Family Superhero Fun Run, 5K, 10K
description:
Bring your family and friends to come support your community in the Royal Family Superhero one-mile Fun Run, 5K and 10K! Royal Family Kids (RFK) is a ministry that organizes a summer camp for foster children in our area. They provide life changing moments for children of abuse and neglect, helping them flourish and begin trusting adults again. For a week of the summer they get to have fun, learn about Jesus, and make meaningful connections with other children and camp leaders. 

Foster children often find themselves on paths of academic failure, drug abuse, teen pregnancy, sex trafficking, homelessness and incarceration. Royal Family Kids is an organization with a goal to interrupt these cycles and show children a different path. A highlight of the camp is "everybody's birthday party" where every child gets celebrated with a party complete with games, cake, and presents. We know that one week can make a difference in the life of child!

Your participation in this event provides you the opportunity to be a true Superhero.  Your entire registration fee goes directly to RFK, Pasco to help pay the way for these children to attend camp. 

All are welcome to come dressed as your favorite superhero, and participate in the One Mile Fun Run, and costume contest. At the start/finish line there will be food truck vendors, face painting, balloon making, and music! Awards and recognition will be given to the top 3 finishers of all events in each gender. The 10K participants will be greeted with a medal at the finish line. 

All of the races will start at the Columbia Park bandshell near the Playground of Dreams in Kennewick and run west along the river towards Richland. All races will be an out and back, and there will be aid stations at the 1 mile, 5k, and 10K turn around points with water and gatorade hydration.
