name: Gator Grinder Triathlon
description:
The North Lake Physical Therapy Gator Grinder Triathlon is an excellent introduction for the first-time triathlete, as well as a great early season event for the experienced racer.  All proceeds support the Canby Gators Swim Club.  Thank you for your support.

Swim

500-yard (20 lengths, 10 laps) pool swim in a 6-lane, 25-yard pool, with up to 4 swimmers per lane. Drafting is permitted. The swim will be seeded by 500-yard swim-time submissions. Heat assignments will be e-mailed by the Thursday before the race. The first heat will be in the water at 7:30 a.m. Check-in at least one hour before your start.

Bike

The one-loop 12-mile bike course is over the beautiful rolling country roads that surround Canby. A bike helmet is mandatory. Drafting is not legal. Volunteers will manage traffic at intersections, but roads will be open to traffic and cyclists will be responsible for their safety. 

Run

The 3.1-mile run is mostly on roadways with about one-third on a paved walking trail. The course is flat and fast. Water will be available on the course.

Duathlon (run-bike-run) and Aquabike (swim-bike)

Both variations will follow the same segments as the triathlon course.

REGISTRATION

Online registration only. All race communication is done via e-mail. Once registered, you will receive periodic informational emails. Start times will be sent the Thursday before the race.  If you do not receive these emails, please check your junk or spam folders.

CANCELLATION / WAITLIST POLICY

Cancellations by March 31, 2027, will be given a full refund less $25. No refunds will be given after March 31. Entries are non-transferable.  PLEASE NOTE: T-shirts are only guaranteed to entries registered before March 31.

AWARDS

The top 3 male and female individual finishers in each age group will receive ribbons. Additional awards will be awarded to the top overall male and female finishers and the top male and female finishers from Canby, Oregon.  

ENTRY FEE

$80 individual/$135 relay team December 1, 2026 - February 28, 2027. $90 individual/$155 relay March 1- May 6 2027. Registration deadline is April 29, 2026. No day of race registration. Registration will include a shirt, results, and a great time!  

RACE T-SHIRTS

T-shirts are included in registration for registrations received before March 31. 

PACKET DISTRIBUTION

Packets will be available starting at 6:30 AM on Saturday, May 8.

Course maps:  Bike  

From pool, turn 

Right onto S. Ivy St.

Right on Township Rd

Left on S. Redwood Rd

Right on 4th

Left on Sequoia Parkway (stop sign)

Right on Walnut (this right turn is about 100 yards or so after turning onto Sequoia Parkway)

Follow Walnut until it T's into 1st Ave.

Right on 1st Av. (which turns into Haines Rd, which turns into New Era Rd.),

from New Era, Right onto Central Point Rd.

Right on Township Rd.

Left on Sequoia Parkway 

Right on SE 13th Ave.

Turn right into the Adult Center parking lot and dismount by the bus stop shelter

 

Run

From Pool parking lot,

Run behind Ackerman Middle School and along walkway on east side of school,

Turn left on SE 13th Ave.

Left on Teakwood

Right on Baker Prairie Trail 

Left on South Molalla Forest Road aka the logging road

Exit left at SE Township Road

Left on S Redwood Street

Left on access rd. back towards Baker Prairie Trail

Right on S Teakwood Street

Right on SE 13th Ave

Right on walkway at east end of Ackerman Middle School and 

Finish on the Ackerman Middle School track.

name: Gator Grinder Triathlon
description:
The North Lake Physical Therapy Gator Grinder Triathlon is an excellent introduction for the first-time triathlete, as well as a great early season event for the experienced racer.  All proceeds support the Canby Gators Swim Club.  Thank you for your support.

Swim

500-yard (20 lengths, 10 laps) pool swim in a 6-lane, 25-yard pool, with up to 4 swimmers per lane. Drafting is permitted. The swim will be seeded by 500-yard swim-time submissions. Heat assignments will be e-mailed by the Thursday before the race. The first heat will be in the water at 7:30 a.m. Check-in at least one hour before your start.

Bike

The one-loop 12-mile bike course is over the beautiful rolling country roads that surround Canby. A bike helmet is mandatory. Drafting is not legal. Volunteers will manage traffic at intersections, but roads will be open to traffic and cyclists will be responsible for their safety. 

Run

The 3.1-mile run is mostly on roadways with about one-third on a paved walking trail. The course is flat and fast. Water will be available on the course.

Duathlon (run-bike-run) and Aquabike (swim-bike)

Both variations will follow the same segments as the triathlon course.

REGISTRATION

Online registration only. All race communication is done via e-mail. Once registered, you will receive periodic informational emails. Start times will be sent the Thursday before the race.  If you do not receive these emails, please check your junk or spam folders.

CANCELLATION / WAITLIST POLICY

Cancellations by March 31, 2027, will be given a full refund less $25. No refunds will be given after March 31. Entries are non-transferable.  PLEASE NOTE: T-shirts are only guaranteed to entries registered before March 31.

AWARDS

The top 3 male and female individual finishers in each age group will receive ribbons. Additional awards will be awarded to the top overall male and female finishers and the top male and female finishers from Canby, Oregon.  

ENTRY FEE

$80 individual/$135 relay team December 1, 2026 - February 28, 2027. $90 individual/$155 relay March 1- May 6 2027. Registration deadline is April 29, 2026. No day of race registration. Registration will include a shirt, results, and a great time!  

RACE T-SHIRTS

T-shirts are included in registration for registrations received before March 31. 

PACKET DISTRIBUTION

name: HAGG Lake Triathlon
description:
RACE AT THIS HISTORICAL EVENT AND STUNNING VENUE!

Hagg Lake Triathlon – Rich in Beauty, Rich in Tradition!

Come race at the 46th Anniversary of the Annual Hagg Lake Triathlon, one of the oldest and most gorgeous Triathlon courses in the nation! We have an Olympic & Sprint Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike & NEW Long Distance Triathlon Course Skullman 70.3

The modern sport of triathlon had its modest beginnings with an event held in Mission Bay in San Diego, CA on September 25, 1974. There were 46 athletes that day. Seven years later, Hagg Lake Triathlon became one of six stops on the Bud Light Triathlon Series Tour drawing about 500 athletes, with Dave Scott coming out on top. Today, as one of the nation’s oldest and longest-running triathlon events, Hagg Lake enters its 38th year and it continues to draw upwards of 700+ athletes. Its popularity is rooted in the rich tradition and the exceptional venue, which is one of the most scenic in the country. The Hagg Lake course offers a true test of this terrific sport with its rolling hills on both the bike and run leg portions of the event. Make the Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival one of your summer stops and compete on the course that has seen many of the greats in the sport of triathlon.

Hagg Lake Triathlon – Rich in Beauty, Rich in Tradition!

Come race at the 46th Anniversary of the Annual Hagg Lake Triathlon, one of the oldest and most gorgeous Triathlon courses in the nation! We have an Olympic & Sprint Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike & NEW Long Distance Triathlon Course Skullman 70.3

The modern sport of triathlon had its modest beginnings with an event held in Mission Bay in San Diego, CA on September 25, 1974. There were 46 athletes that day. Seven years later, Hagg Lake Triathlon became one of six stops on the Bud Light Triathlon Series Tour drawing about 500 athletes, with Dave Scott coming out on top. Today, as one of the nation’s oldest and longest-running triathlon events, Hagg Lake enters its 38th year and it continues to draw upwards of 700+ athletes. Its popularity is rooted in the rich tradition and the exceptional venue, which is one of the most scenic in the country. The Hagg Lake course offers a true test of this terrific sport with its rolling hills on both the bike and run leg portions of the event. Make the Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival one of your summer stops and compete on the course that has seen many of the greats in the sport of triathlon.

name: Haulin Aspen
description:
Mountain Trail Running Has Never Been Better

One of Oregon’s favorite trail full marathon and half marathon races returns for the 22nd year on Saturday, August 7th, 2027. 

No pavement here. Featuring a full all-trail marathon, a half marathon, and a 6.5-mile course (dubbed the “Half As”), the Haulin’ Aspen features beautiful trails that wind through the Deschutes National Forest, showcasing some epic views. With varying terrain and elevation, the cool wooded pine setting provides a challenging and exciting experience. Enjoy the beautiful single track, steep trails, fast descents, and amazing views starting at an elevation of nearly 5500'. Make it a destination this summer – Bend and the Cascades welcome you!

RUN WITH YOUR FRIENDS:

The Haulin' Aspen full marathon introduces a three-person relay option, giving teams the chance to experience the full 26.2 mile all-trail course together. The race begins and Wanoga Sno Park, where Runner 1 takes on the first 9.6 miles to Transition 1 at Aid Station 3. Runner 2 then covers the longest leg - approximately 11.7 miles - continuing along the course to Transition 2 at Aid Station 7 (mile 21.3). From there Runner 3 tackles the final 4.9 mile stretch - an uphill push back to the finish at Wanoga. This new format offers a dynamic way to share the challenge while still taking in the scenic, high-elevation terrain of the course.

name: Helvetia Wine Run 5k
description:
This race will sell out soon so sign up today!

Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Saturday, June 19, 2027 at 8:30am and 10:30am for an exciting annual event that features the amazing scenery and landscape of Helvetia Vineyards & Winery!  Helvetia Vineyards and Winery is located in the foothills of the Tualatin Mountains, the northernmost grape growing area in the Willamette Valley and just 25 minutes from downtown Portland. So, whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wine, this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience!  This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing.  Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: 
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!

name: Ho Ho 5k
description:
The triumphant return of a holiday classic.  A festive 5K exuding the holiday spirit! HoHo's and Snoballs (Hostess) to all finishers.  Dress up encouraged and, keeping with tradition, there will be free trees AND THE FRUITCAKE!!  IYKYK!! 

Get in the spirit and bring canned food and jackets/blankets and come out for a great 5K run and walk!  Also collecting cat and dog food for the humane society! Friendly dogs are welcome.  

Late registration and number pick-up will begin at 8 AM race morning.  Bring some warm clothes to change into so you can enjoy the festive post event fun!

name: HWAM Superhero Run
description:
Hearts With A Mission, in collaboration with First Community Credit Union, will host the twelfth annual Hearts With A Mission Superhero Run on Saturday, May 1st, at Valley of the Rogue State Park. This event is held to raise awareness and support for at-risk youth, families and seniors in need in Southern Oregon.

The Superhero Run is a family-friendly event that will include a 1-mile fun run, as well as a timed 5K, 10K and half marathon run. Participants are encouraged to wear their best superhero outfit during the race, prizes will be awarded for the best dressed.

The event will begin at 8:00 a.m. with the half marathon. The 10K and 5K will start promptly after, with the 1-mile run starting at 10:00 a.m. This year’s KID ZONE is sponsored by [name] and is bigger than ever. Kids will enjoy jousting, corn hole, face painting, a 45-foot obstacle course, arts and crafts, and so much more. There will also be food trucks present.

name: Longest Night Mile
description:
WHERE:  Phoenix High School Track

WHEN: Monday, December 21st, 2025

  • 6:00pm- Heat 1  5:30 min pace & Under 
  • 6:10pm -Heat 2  5:31-6:00 min Pace
  • 6:20pm- Heat 3  6:01-6:45min Pace 
  • 6:35pm- Heat 4  6:46-8min Pace 
  • 6:50pm- Heat 5  8-10min Pace 
  • 7:05pm- Heat 6  10min Pace & Up

NEW: We’ve added an additional heat and narrowed the time range for the first three heats to reduce the number of runners in each heat. This change will help create less crowded fields, especially for runners who experienced a cramped start last year.

COURSE DETAILS:  Four times around the Phoenix High School Track

RACE FEES: Option 1: Bring 2-3+ boxes of dry cereal. YES you read that right! The SOU food bank coordinator expressed to us in 2019 that the students are excited when there is cereal in the food bank because there rarely is and when it is there it doesn't last long. So, we thought it would be a fun treat before Christmas to stuff their pantry full of cereal goodness! We also hosted a can food drive at our Turkey Trot for the SOU food bank and a portion of the proceeds went to them as well so don't worry, we made sure they had other food items. 

Option 2: $13 online or $15 day of (cash or check only) which will also be donated to the SOU Student Food Pantry.

RACE DAY INFO: Registration and packet pick-up 4:45-5:45pm - Bring $15 or 2-3+ boxes of dry cereal and sign waiver to participate.  

AWARDS:  Ribbons for the top 3 places in all age groups. $100 prize for any male who wins and runs sub 4:10 minutes and any female who wins and runs sub 4:50 minutes.

RESTRICTIONS: Absolutely no roller skaters, bicycles, skateboards, baby joggers, dogs, headphones, or unregistered participants

RACE DIRECTORS: Nathan & Shayla Watt

name: Mac's Run
description:
Hilly and challenging course with breathtaking ocean views. The race is entirely on paved roads.  

For both courses, runners loop through Shore Acres heading out (south), and run straight back on the return (north).

5K Course Map

10K Course Map

Note that students are $5.00.  Please use the coupon code Student2022 to register.  To avoid credit-card fees, you will not be charged at check-out.  Please bring $5.00 (exact change appreciated) to registration!

Starting Oct 1, 2025, all vehicles require a parking pass (cost is per vehicle, not per runner).  Cost of a day pass is $10 for in-state or $12 for out-of-state.  Daily passes are available at a kiosk near registration with a QR code using your phone.  We are working with the parks to see if we can sell them as part of registration, but details have not been worked out yet.  Annual state park passes are $30 for one year and $50 for two years.  They can be purchased at the gift shop at Shore Acres or on-line.  FYI, the price will double to $60 for an annual pass January 1 and they will no longer issue two-year passes, so if you visit our beautiful state parks, it is cheaper to buy now.

name: Monsters & Mimosas 5K - Diamond Lake
description:
Get ready for a spooky-good time at the Monsters & Mimosas 5K, where Halloween fun meets festive celebration! This spirited run invites ghosts, goblins, and costumed creatures of all kinds to hit the course for a frightfully fantastic fall morning.

Join us at Diamond Lake Resort where all race participants will receive a custom finisher medal, a race-themed shirt, and a refreshing mimosa waiting for them at the finish line—because even monsters deserve a little sparkle after a solid run! We'll have juice and water for those under 21.

We’ll also be recognizing top finishers with awards in the usual five-year age groups starting at 10 & under, giving everyone a chance to show off their speed along with their costumes.

Join us for miles, mimosas, and a whole lot of Halloween magic!

name: Mountain Valley Turkey Trot 2026
description:
Get ready for Thanksgiving dinner with a 3.2 mile fun run or walk through Island City, OR ending and beginning at Mountain Valley Therapy parking lot. 

The Thanksgiving tradition, organized by MVT/MVFH, is an all-ages family event that raises money each year for a local non-profit. This year all proceeds will benefit the Friday Backpack Program . 

The Turkey Trot is a family event that has something for everyone! Come run, walk and cheer all while benefitting a great new organization that promotes physical activity in our grade schools. 

Register online today!

To find out more about the Turkey Trot, contact Danielle at hr@mountainvalleytherapy.biz

 

What is the Friday Backpack Program?

Union County Friday Backpack (UCFBP) is a nonprofit organization based in La Grande, Oregon, dedicated to preventing weekend hunger among elementary students (K–5) throughout Union County. With approximately 60% of local students qualifying for free or reduced-price meals, many children face food insecurity when school meals are unavailable. During the school year, volunteers pack and distribute weekend food bags through elementary schools in La Grande, Island City, Elgin, Imbler, Cove, Union, and North Powder, ensuring children in need have access to supplemental food outside of school.

For more information on the Friday Backpack Program, check out their website! Friday Backpack Program Website

name: My Unheard Voice: Restoring Hope 5K
description:
Join us for the My Unheard Voice Restoring Hope 5K Run/Walk—a morning of movement, worship, community, and purpose in beautiful Laurelhurst Park.

My Unheard Voice is a faith-based nonprofit organization dedicated to breaking the silence surrounding child sexual abuse. We raise awareness, create space for survivors’ stories to be heard, provide helpful resources, and support survivors as they take meaningful steps toward restoration. We believe that the wounds of the past do not have to define the future.

Participants of all ages and abilities are invited to run or walk the professionally RFID chip-timed course, which consists of four loops along the park’s paths. Finishers will be awarded a medal and an event t-shirt!

This 5K is more than a race. It is an opportunity to stand with survivors, bring an often-hidden issue into the light. Funds raised through registrations, donations, and sponsorships will support the continued growth of My Unheard Voice. This includes strengthening our organizational infrastructure, expanding our resources, and building our capacity to serve more individuals. Proceeds will also support Phase 1 of our long-term vision to establish a shelter for survivors. This foundational phase will focus on research and planning, program development, and building the community partnerships needed to create a safe place where survivors can pursue healing.

The event will include a 5K run/walk, a time of worship with live music, opportunities to learn more about our mission, and space to gather as a community around a cause that matters deeply.

Whether you run, walk, donate, or sponsor the event, your participation helps turn silence into awareness, awareness into action, and action into hope. Come take a step with us toward a future where every unheard voice has a safe place to be heard.

name: Newport Resolution Run
description:
Start Your Year the Rugged Way


Kick off 2027 on the Oregon Coast with the Newport Resolution Run & Plunge — a gritty, beautiful, community-centered way to start the new year.

Set at South Beach State Park in Newport, Oregon, this event brings together raw coastal scenery, winter grit, and one unforgettable finish-line tradition: the plunge.

Choose your distance:

Half Marathon
A rugged mix of road and trail. The half marathon starts and finishes on pavement, with a challenging stretch through the Wilder Trail system in the middle. Expect coastal air, rolling terrain, and a course that asks you to earn the finish.

The half marathon has a 2:45 cutoff for full course support, but we’ll be cheering you across the finish line either way.

10K & 5K
Flat, fast, and welcoming for runners and walkers looking to start the year strong. The 10K and 5K are road out-and-back courses — perfect for chasing a New Year’s PR, building momentum, or simply showing up with your community.

The Ultimate Coastal Finish
The Newport Resolution Run & Plunge is built around one unforgettable tradition: finishing your race and taking the plunge.

Our primary plan is to finish near the Pacific Ocean shoreline, where runners can celebrate by plunging into the ocean after crossing the finish line.

If strong winds, surf conditions, or other coastal safety concerns make the ocean finish unfavorable, we will use our alternate finish and plunge location at the South Beach Marina. This keeps the plunge tradition alive while allowing us to make the safest race-day decision for participants, volunteers, and crew.

The plunge is optional, but the memory lasts all year.

Why Join Us?
The Newport Resolution Run & Plunge is more than a race. It’s a bold beginning.

It’s about starting the year with purpose, embracing the elements, and celebrating what your body and spirit can do. You’ll find rugged coastal beauty, human grit, warm community energy, and the kind of finish-line memory that sticks with you all year.

Whether you’re chasing a goal, tackling the half marathon trails, running your first 5K, or plunging with friends, this is your invitation to start 2027 the rugged way.

Registration Policies
Refunds & Credits
There are no refunds.

Participants who cancel 30 or more days before race day may receive a 50% credit toward a future Ardor Adventures event.

No credit is available for cancellations made within 30 days of race day.

Transfers
Transfers are allowed until December 21, 2026. A $10 transfer fee applies.

Event Details
Race Date: Saturday, January 2, 2027
Location: South Beach State Park, Newport, Oregon
Distances: Half Marathon, 10K, 5K
Start Times: Half Marathon 9:00 AM, 10K 9:20 AM, 5K 9:30 AM
Medal: Included with registration
Shirt: Optional $15 add-on
Plunge: Included and encouraged. Primary plunge location is the Pacific Ocean shoreline, with South Beach Marina as the alternate location if ocean conditions are not favorable.

Don’t Miss Out
The Newport Resolution Run & Plunge is your chance to begin the year with grit, beauty, community, and courage.

Register now and start your year the rugged way.

name: Newport Turkey Trot
description:
🦃A Thanksgiving Tradition for Lincoln County Families!

Join us for the 13th Annual Newport Turkey Trot — a festive, family-friendly Thanksgiving morning tradition! Whether you're walking or running, the 5K, 10K, and Kids Fun Run offer something for everyone. Enjoy scenic views of Yaquina Bay, the Hatfield Marine Science Center, and the Pacific Ocean — and start your holiday with fun, fitness, and community.

🎭Costume Contest 
Show up in your best Thanksgiving-themed gear and you could win fun prizes! We love seeing turkeys, pies, pilgrims, and creative flair on the course.

🤝 Giving Back
A portion of every registration supports the Food Share of Lincoln County, helping local families in need during the holiday season.

 

👟Team Registration

Rally your crew and run as a team!

Social Teams: Friends, families, and fun-seekers
Corporate Teams: Represent your workplace with pride
School Teams: Parents, teachers, and students unite!

🏆 The team with the most participants will receive special recognition!

🎽Registration Includes:

  • Finisher's Medal for every participant 🏅
  • Chip-timed results ⏱️
  • A beautiful, flat course with coastal views 🌊
  • Support for a great local cause

Shirts are optional and can be added during registration:

$13 if purchased on or before November 16, 2025.
$20 after November 16, 2025



Race Day Schedule (November 27, 2025):

📦 Packet Pickup

  • Wednesday, November 26: 5:30 PM – 7:00 PM at Arctic Circle Restaurant
  • Thursday, November 27: 7:45 AM at South Beach Marina

🏃‍♂️ Race Start Times

  • 9:00 AM – Kids Fun Run (0.5 mile)
  • 9:20 AM – 5K & 10K Start

name: Oak Hills Tim Tank Turkey Trot
description:
Lace up your running shoes at 8AM Thanksgiving morning and get ready to trot a 5K! The Tim Tank Turkey Trot at Oak Hills is on! This run/walk is fun for the whole family - all ages and abilities are welcome! Every race entry contributes toward a BSD High School Scholarship in the former late race organizers name: Tim Tank.

Registration:

  • $10 per Adult 18+, $5 per kid/youth (under 18).
  • Please bring 2 cans of food for the local food pantry.
  • Bib pick up Thanksgiving morning starting 7AM in the Oak Hills Gym.
  • Early Bib pick up day prior 12-1pm and 5-6pm in the Oak Hills community room.

Race Logistics: 

  • Start at NW Oak Hills Drive & NW 153rd (4 way stop) and finish on NW Norwich.
  • Race is not timed, serious runners bring your watch to time yourself.
  • Stroller riders and dogs are free (please clean up after your dog).
  • No bikes, scooters or anything ride-on ( to avoid medical accidents).
  • Parking is limited, please walk or park at elementary school or nearby church.

About Tim Tank and the Tim Tank Memorial Non-profit:

The Tim Tank Memorial Scholarship 501c3 non-profit was created in 2024 to honor Tim Tank, long time Oak Hills resident and local leader in the sport of running. Tim's legacy was established after he fought a courageous battle of Glioblastoma (brain cancer). Tim was a collegiate competitive runner and Cross Country/Track Coach for High Schools in Beaverton School District. Tim originally relaunched the Oak Hills Turkey Trot in 2019 while he was on medical leave to give back to community and build an event to bring people together on his favorite holiday. Now we walk and run to give tribute to Tim and give back to the broader community. To date the Tim Tank Memorial has awarded $11,000 in scholarships to high school seniors.

name: ORRC 1200 Club
description:
ORRC’s 1200 Club program is available for current club members to run or walk 1,200 miles in one calendar year (averaging about 100/month, or about 25/week). The purpose is meant to be a challenge and motivational tool running from January 1 through December 31.

Participants who complete 1200 miles in one calendar year (January through December) receive a jacket the first year, and patches to add to the jacket in subsequent years. You must be prepared to track your walking and running miles and report them to the club at the end of each month.

Give yourself a challenge and join the 1200 club! Click here to join ORRC if you're not already a member.

name: ORRC Best Dam Run - 10K
description:
Come run or walk the Best Dam Run! This point-to-point 10K course features views of pristine waters, shading forests, interesting geology and bald eagles, osprey and colorful waterfowl.

Participants are bused approximately 6 miles east of Estacada to the North Fork Lake start. The course meanders along the wild and scenic Clackamas River for most of your journey to the downtown Estacada finish line.  

Post-race food and awards will take place near the finish line at SE 4th Ave and Broadway.  After your event you can also stroll along the shops and venues of Estacada.

This event is limited to 750 entrants so don't wait and register now!

name: ORRC Ralph's Run
description: Formerly the ORRC Y2K Run, now Ralph's Run in honor of longtime ORRC member Ralph Brown, this event moves back to its original premise of a changing distance every year. Starting out in 1986 as the 8.6 in '86, it will now be 20.27K in 2027. You get a new PR every year! It also features a 10K run/walk, a 5K run/walk, and a kid's run.  All events start at 9am and the course closes at noon.  (There is an 8:30 start intended ONLY for 20.27K participants who can’t make the three-hour cut-off.)

name: ORRC Turkey Trot at The Zoo
description:
The ORRC Turkey Trot at the Oregon Zoo is a multi-generational family event. Runners and walkers of all abilities love the 5K, untimed out-and-back course.  The event starts at The Oregon Zoo by the Forestry Center and the Max station, then goes out toward the International Rose Garden, and finishes inside The Oregon Zoo at the Elephant Plaza. The Tot Trot (children 0- 4 years old) and the Gobble Gallop (for children between 5 and 10 years old) events follow the 5K at the Elephant plaza inside the zoo.

Every entrant in the 5K and kids events receive an awesome beanie hat and chocolate turkey. There will be no shirts this year, but we are bringing back medals for all finishers.

PLEASE NOTE: The event is capped for non-ORRC members at 2,200 participants! The deadline to register is Thursday, November 19, 2026, and there is no day of race registration. Register early to ensure your entry!

 

Start Line Note: The last start is at 7:39 (for slower walkers, and families with strollers).

THERE IS NO LATE START! Plan to be at the Zoo NO LATER than 7:00am to have time to park, pick up your bibs, go to the bathroom, etc. before the start. If you arrive late, you might not be able to complete the entire course before it closes.

Approximately $25,000 of registration fees benefit The Oregon Zoo.

Runners and walkers of all abilities love the 5K, untimed out-and-back course.  The event starts at The Oregon Zoo by the Forestry Center and the Max station, then goes out toward the International Rose Garden, and finishes inside The Oregon Zoo at the Elephant Plaza. The Tot Trot (children 0- 4 years old) and the Gobble Gallop (for children between 5 and 10 years old) events follow the 5K at the Elephant plaza inside the zoo.

Every entrant in the 5K and kids events receive an awesome beanie hat and chocolate turkey. There will be no shirts this year, but we are bringing back medals for all finishers.

PLEASE NOTE: The event is capped for non-ORRC members at 2,200 participants! The deadline to register is Thursday, November 19, 2026, and there is no day of race registration. Register early to ensure your entry!

 

Start Line Note: The last start is at 7:39 (for slower walkers, and families with strollers).

THERE IS NO LATE START! Plan to be at the Zoo NO LATER than 7:00am to have time to park, pick up your bibs, go to the bathroom, etc. before the start. If you arrive late, you might not be able to complete the entire course before it closes.

Approximately $25,000 of registration fees benefit The Oregon Zoo.

name: ORRC Vernonia Marathon,  Half Marathon, and Marathon Relay
description: Picture yourself running a beautiful, tree-lined course along the 21 mile Banks-Vernonia State Trail.  Both events feature a gentle 7-mile, 400-foot downhill into Banks.  Hot food and hot showers await all runners and walkers. This Boston Marathon qualifier course, USATF Certified, is point-to-point, with 23 miles closed to vehicular traffic. The half marathon course is also USATF Certified.

name: OXFORD Classic Community 5k
description:
Welcome to the 36th Annual Oxford Classic.

Since 1992, one of Central Oregon's longest-running and most competitive cross country meets. Alongside the high school races, our Community 5K is open to everyone, any age and any pace.

The course loops through Drake Park along the Deschutes River, grass and pavement. Flat and fast, wide enough to run in a pack, with plenty of room to cheer.

Saturday, October 3, 2026. Drake Park, 777 NW Riverside Blvd, Bend, OR 97701. Community 5K at 12:40 PM.

High school and middle school teams: enter on athletic.net, each in their own division.

name: PDX Triathlon Festival
description:
Join us for the 44th Annual PDX Triathlon Festival at Blue Lake Regional Park and kick off the summer racing season. The fun begins on Sunday where athletes compete on our scenic, flat and fast course in either the Super Sprint, Sprint or Olympic Distances. NEW: A 5K on Sunday or try our Paddle Triathlon for those of you who would rather kayak or paddle-board! Relay options are great for friends, family & co-workers!

The Annual PDX/Blue Lake Triathlon was started by the Portland Triathlon Association and Frank Goulard, who is still an active, local Masters Triathlete. He participates in many of our events so come on out and meet the legend, the man who started it all for us here locally!

This weekend festival offers an Olympic and Sprint Distance Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike, and a Super Sprint course that offers shorter distances for those new to the sport or just going for pure, raw speed. The Super Sprint is also a great event for our Junior Triathletes!

Recognized by NW triathletes as the “must do” event to open the triathlon season, the PDX Triathlon encompasses two full days of racing (Kids races & Sunset 5k on Saturday & Super Sprint, Sprint & Olympic races on Sunday) including a Sports & Fitness Expo. Triathlon Clubs from across the NW gather to launch the MultiSport season.

The bike courses are flat and fast, with the majority occurring on a section of Marine Dr that is closed to all but local traffic. This makes the course one of the safest and fastest in the region.

PARKING IS INCLUDED WITH REGISTRATION COST.

The Annual PDX/Blue Lake Triathlon was started by the Portland Triathlon Association and Frank Goulard, who is still an active, local Masters Triathlete. He participates in many of our events so come on out and meet the legend, the man who started it all for us here locally!

This weekend festival offers an Olympic and Sprint Distance Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike, and a Super Sprint course that offers shorter distances for those new to the sport or just going for pure, raw speed. The Super Sprint is also a great event for our Junior Triathletes!

Recognized by NW triathletes as the “must do” event to open the triathlon season, the PDX Triathlon encompasses two full days of racing (Kids races & Sunset 5k on Saturday & Super Sprint, Sprint & Olympic races on Sunday) including a Sports & Fitness Expo. Triathlon Clubs from across the NW gather to launch the MultiSport season.

The bike courses are flat and fast, with the majority occurring on a section of Marine Dr that is closed to all but local traffic. This makes the course one of the safest and fastest in the region.

PARKING IS INCLUDED WITH REGISTRATION COST.

name: Popsicle 5K/10K/Half - Eugene
description:
Beat the heat and treat yourself at the Popsicle 5K/10K/Half Marathon—a sweet celebration of summer miles and frozen rewards. Whether you’re racing the speedy 5K, cruising through the 10K, or going the distance in the Half Marathon, this event is designed to be fun, festive, and refreshingly cool from start to finish.
We will be gathering at Kiwanis Park in Eugene, OR.
When you cross the finish line, your reward is waiting: a delicious, ice-cold popsicle to help you chill out and celebrate your accomplishment. Every finisher will also receive a custom Popsicle-themed finisher medal—bright, bold, and worthy of showing off.
Awards will be presented in all three distances to the top three male and female finishers in standard five-year age groups, beginning with 10 & Under. Whether you’re chasing a podium spot or just looking for a cool way to log some summer miles, the Popsicle 5K/10K/Half Marathon is the perfect blend of fun and fast.

name: Race for the Warriors
description:
This is a 5k fundraising race to help support Pink Sistas-a local organization dedicated to helping women find connections with other women as well as themselves again after a breast cancer diagnosis.

Women who have been diagnosed with breast cancer often times feel vulnerable. Although many women have the support of loved ones, many women go through the journey alone. No matter what support they have, it's a lonely journey that only those who have walked the same path can understand.

Pink Sistas offers that connection through no-cost day trips and no-cost 3-day retreats. 

At their day trips, women have the opportunity to share their story, have lunch on our 22-foot pink drifter party barge, kayak, paddle board, and network with other like-minded women who are also breast cancer survivors and warriors. The result is an amazing opportunity to create bonds and just relax and have fun. At our 3-day retreats, women share their story, relax, exercise together, enjoy meals together, doing crafts, and most importantly, create connections and get the love and support they need in a time when they need it most.

name: Race Staff 5K & 10K, Salem, OR (Training)
description:
US Road Running Races

US Road Running races are built for runners and walkers who like friendly, low-pressure race days with just enough competition to keep things exciting. Our events are local, welcoming, and easy to jump into, whether you are chasing a PR, collecting another themed medal, working toward series points, or just getting outside with good people.

Most races are small enough to feel personal but organized enough to feel official. You can expect a clear course, helpful race staff, finisher medals, results, and a relaxed community feel. Bring your fast shoes, your steady walking pace, your favorite running buddy, or your best “I signed up for this on purpose” smile. We will be glad to see you at the start line.

A quick race-day note: because many US Road Running events are small local races, we normally have one or two staff members at each race. EMS is not stationed on site, and water stations are limited to the finish area at the end of each lap and at the race finish. Please plan for the weather, bring anything you may want between laps, and check in with race staff if you need help.

View Race Course, Results, and Race Information on the US Road Running race page.

name: Roseburg Optimist 5 K RUN/WALK
description:
What is a Zombie 5 K Run?

Runners will endure a 5 K run/walk through a zombie-infested course. Test your speed, endurance, and strength while trying to avoid
ravenous zombies! Runners will wear a flag (provided) on one side of their waist (like flag football). These flags represent zombie health. Zombies will try to steal those flags throughout the course. 

5 K Zombie Run was founded to celebrate happiness, healthiness, and friendship! Our mission is not about mile markers, but about
memories made.

We hope our 5K run will be an inspiration for healthy living. Those wishing for a run time must submit their phone numbers. 
The runner’s time will be provided through this method.

What makes the 5 K the Zombie Run special?
This 5 K Zombie Run is a fundraising event for the Roseburg Optimist Club. 100% of the proceeds go to the Roseburg Optimist Club to support children’s events in Douglas County. Your participation in the 5 K Zombie Run makes a difference!

All participants will receive a FREE 5 K Zombie Run T-shirt.  A commemorative finisher medallion, a race bib, a flag, and snacks at the finish of the race will be provided by Thrive Umpqua. Commemorative medallions will be awarded to healthy racers and infected racers. Infected racers are those who lost their flag to a zombie during the race.

Race information:
The Zombie Run will take place on Saturday, October 17th, at Stewart Park. The check-in time is 8:00 am, with the race starting at 9:00 am.

name: Run for a Reason 2027 with Two Daughters Foundation
description:
Run for Two Daughters Foundation at the 2027 Eugene Marathon, raise money to cover your registration costs, and support our mission of providing free peer grief support to young adults across the country!


There's no more iconic place to achieve your running accomplishment than in Track Town USA! You can tackle the full 26.2 miles in the marathon, or sign up for the half marathon or 5k! Whatever you choose, you will be in the company of other Two Daughters Foundation team members and enjoy the beautiful scenery of South Eugene and the University of Oregon.


To run for team Two Daughters Foundation, sign up and fundraise for your spot! The fundraising minimums are listed below. Two Daughters Foundation will send you a registration link once you've achieved your fundraising goal. All profits received by Two Daughters Foundation go towards our charity's mission of providing free grief support to young adults in Oregon and beyond that are navigating the serious illness or loss of a parent or parental figure.

To learn more about what we do and our story, visit our website at www.twodaughtersfoundation.org.

All Team Members Receive:

  • FREE registration for the race! As soon as your fundraising goal is met, your registration fee is waived for the race of your choice.
  • An official Two Daughters Foundation T-shirt
  • Fundraising platform and tools, including your own fundraising page and ongoing fundraising support from Two Daughters Foundation staff

Fundraising Minimums:


Marathon: $500

Half Marathon: $350

5k: $150


Once you've achieved your fundraising goal, Two Daughters Foundation will reach out to you with a registration link that will allow you to register at no additional cost to you.

Please note that you will be accountable for covering the remaining amount to meet the fundraising minimum if the fundraising minimum is not met by the fundraising deadline.


Contact info@twodaughtersfoundation.org if you have any questions! We are happy to help you get set up and provide fundraising tips. 


We look forward to running with you!

name: Run for a Reason 2027 with Two Daughters Foundation
description:
Run for Two Daughters Foundation at the 2027 Eugene Marathon, raise money to cover your registration costs, and support our mission of providing free peer grief support to young adults across the country!


There's no more iconic place to achieve your running accomplishment than in Track Town USA! You can tackle the full 26.2 miles in the marathon, or sign up for the half marathon or 5k! Whatever you choose, you will be in the company of other Two Daughters Foundation team members and enjoy the beautiful scenery of South Eugene and the University of Oregon.


To run for team Two Daughters Foundation, sign up and fundraise for your spot! The fundraising minimums are listed below. Two Daughters Foundation will send you a registration link once you've achieved your fundraising goal. All profits received by Two Daughters Foundation go towards our charity's mission of providing free grief support to young adults in Oregon and beyond that are navigating the serious illness or loss of a parent or parental figure.

To learn more about what we do and our story, visit our website at www.twodaughtersfoundation.org.

All Team Members Receive:

  • FREE registration for the race! As soon as your fundraising goal is met, your registration fee is waived for the race of your choice.
  • An official Two Daughters Foundation T-shirt
  • Fundraising platform and tools, including your own fundraising page and ongoing fundraising support from Two Daughters Foundation staff

Fundraising Minimums:


Marathon: $500

Half Marathon: $350

5k: $150


Once you've achieved your fundraising goal, Two Daughters Foundation will reach out to you with a registration link that will allow you to register at no additional cost to you.

Please note that you will be accountable for covering the remaining amount to meet the fundraising minimum if the fundraising minimum is not met by the fundraising deadline.


Contact info@twodaughtersfoundation.org if you have any questions! We are happy to help you get set up and provide fundraising tips. 


We look forward to running with you!

name: Run Whiskey Run
description:
For more information, visit our website at South Coast Running Club

Located roughly 20 miles south of Coos Bay, the region’s first single-track trail system is open year-round to mountain bikers, but for the first time ever will be reserved for those of us who shred at running pace. 

We’ll start and finish at the main Whiskey Run Trailhead. 

Our chosen section of Whiskey Run is shaded and sheltered, which means these trails are rolling, smooth, and oh so loamy.

Course options include:

·      1.5 Mile (Shirley Temple)

·      5 Mile (Whiskey Ginger)

·      10 Mile (Double Shot) 

Please note that all courses are 100% trail, so not stroller friendly.

PRICES

Online

$15 Club member (your discount will appear at check-out), Non-member $25. 

Day of race

$20 Club member, Non-member $30

Students: $5.00.  Use the code Student2022 to register.  To avoid credit card charges, students will not be charged at on-line registration.  Please bring $5 (exact change appreciated) to registration!  

START TIMES

-      9am (10 Mile Double Shot)

-      9:30am (5 Mile Whiskey Ginger) 

-      9:45 (1.5 Mile Shirley Temple)

Course support ends at 12 PM.

Day of race registration and packet pick up begins at 8:00 at Whiskey Run Trailhead.

Runners should assemble at the starting line no later than 10 minutes before start time for instructions from the race director.  

Come dressed to run; no space is available for changing/showering.

INFORMATION ABOUT THE AREA

Whiskey Run is located on Oregon’s Adventure Coast. Our costal community offers endless opportunities for beach combing, fishing, crabbing, paddling, hiking, and golfing. And don’t forget about the mountain biking… bring your bike and explore the 30+ miles of premier single track at Whiskey Run.

Come see what attracts so many runners to Oregon’s Adventure Coast.

name: RUN/WALK FOR THE RARE!
description:
Haley's Heroes Foundation presents the 8th Annual RUN/Walk FOR THE RARE, a 10k, 5k, and 1-mile run/walk to support International Batten Disease Awareness Day.  Did you know that Rare is everywhere? Join us as we run on Sunday, June 6, 2027. 1 in 10 people have a rare disease, and 50% of those are children. There are more than 7,000 known rare diseases, and an estimated 350 million people globally are diagnosed with a rare disease. YET, 95% of all rare diseases don't have an FDA-approved treatment or cure. Let's run (or walk) to change the course of the lives of all those with rare diseases. Post pictures at #RUNWALKFORTHERARE!  

The race will start and finish outside of the Pavilion in the North Meadow. The starting time is 10 am, and all participants should be finished by 12 pm.

Cost is $45 for adults and $35 for children.

Registration fee includes: a food coupon and ice-cream coupon, a photo booth, and a t-shirt

June 05 - Early packet pick-up is 2 pm-4 pm at Gallagher's Fitness | 135 Commercial St NE, Salem, OR 97301

June 06 - Packet pick up begins at 9 am at the run

 

Can't attend? Be a Hero — Run/Walk where you are!

Be a hero from wherever you are—run/walk in place, in your neighborhood, on your favorite trail, or even on your treadmill. Every step helps us move closer to a cure.

Register to join the movement as a virtual participant. Your $45 donation includes an official event t-shirt (shipped right to you!) so you can show your support wherever you are.

Move with purpose. Make an impact. Be a Haley’s Hero.

Don’t forget to share your journey—post a selfie and tag it with #RUNFORTHERARE so we can celebrate with you!

name: Running Scared 5K/13K - Eugene
description:
Get ready for a spine-tingling race experience at the Running Scared 5K & 13K—where thrills, chills, and fast times collide!
Whether you’re brave enough to tackle the 5K or daring enough to conquer the 13K, this Halloween-themed event delivers a fun and festive atmosphere perfect for runners of all levels. Costumes are encouraged, so come dressed to impress (or frighten) as you take on a course filled with seasonal spirit.
We will gather at Kiwanis Park in Eugene, OR.
All athletes will receive a long-sleeve race shirt—perfect for those crisp fall mornings—and a custom finisher medal to commemorate their accomplishment.
For those looking to push their limits, take on the Deadly Double by completing both the 5K and the 13K. It’s the ultimate test of endurance and Halloween courage!
Competitive runners will have plenty to race for. Awards will be presented to the Top Three Male and Female Overall finishers in both the 5K and 13K, as well as the Top Three in Masters, Grand Masters, and Senior Masters Overall categories. In addition, the top three athletes in each of the traditional five-year age groups will receive awards in both race distances. For those taking on the Deadly Double, special recognition will be given to the Top Three Male and Female finishers who complete both races.
Whether you’re running for fun, fitness, or a frightfully good challenge, the Running Scared 5K & 13K is sure to be a hauntingly good time you won’t want to miss!

For those taking on the Deadly Double, special recognition will be given to the Top Three Male and Female finishers who complete both races.
Whether you’re running for fun, fitness, or a frightfully good challenge, the Running Scared 5K & 13K is sure to be a hauntingly good time you won’t want to miss!

description:
Answers to Frequently Asked Questions: 

Yes, strollers are okay.

No dogs please. Please leave them at home.

Yes, you can still register with this page up until Thanksgiving morning.

Yes, you can change races by going to your profile in RunSignUp and choosing "change event."

Walkers, please do not block the whole path. Stay right, so runners can pass on the left.

 

Music, cowbell, good times… Run’ucopia is a Salem tradition. The course will cross the new bridge through one of the largest interconnected urban park systems in the nation! Bring your family and friends and engage in some healthy activity before your feast.  Consider this your “appetite development.”  It is a tradition of friends, family and competitors. 

Distances:

1K kids run (6 & under) Free! Just sign the form on race day...
6K run/walk (4 mile)

10K run (6.2 mile)
15k run (9.3 mile)

Location: Riverfront Park, Salem, Oregon.  Start/Finish at the pavilion.

Date & Time:  Thanksgiving morning.  Thursday, November 26, 2026.  Here is your schedule:

8:00 am   Check-in opens at the pavilion. Grab your bib
8:45         1k Kids race
9:10         Race start 15k
9:12         Race start for 10k

9:14        Race start for 6k

Post-race:  Check the raffle to see if you won

9:50         6k awards. Hot chocolate & coffee from Dutch Bros is enjoyed until supplies run out. Commemorative photos are taken.
10:15      10k awards and 15k soon thereafter.

The Course:  The course is a beautiful tour of the largest interconnected urban park system in the United States and starts at the pavilion on the south side of Salem Riverfront Park.  It passes around the Eco-Earth and onto the new bridge into Minto Brown Island Park.  

The 6k run/walk course is now a little more of a loop course. It is closer to 4 miles, and you get to tour a little more of beautiful Minto Brown Island Park.

The 10k and 15k go deeper into Minto Brown Island Park before heading back to the Pavilion start/finish area. Many signs & volunteers mark the way. Be sure to check out the route below.  The 10k is a very simple out-and-back with a turnaround near the 1930's Buick.

The 15k is also an out-and-back, but on the return, you have to turn right to do your 15k loop, which takes you off the pavement onto a nice dirt trail, directing you back towards the starting line. You go deep, then do the loop.  Signs and volunteers guide the way.

View the 6k course here: 6k/ 4 mile course
 
View the 10k course here:  Revised 10k course
 
View the 15k course here: Revised 15k course

Again this year: Express what you are grateful for this year on the giant chalkboard.

Timing: The Run’ucopia is always chip-timed. 

Pre-Registration:  There is a small online sign-up fee. Register early for the best price. Entry fees are non-refundable and non-transferable.

Early packet pickup: Wednesday 11/25 in downtown Salem at Gallagher’s Fitness Resources (135 Commercial St. NE) from 2:30pm to 5:45pm (Come down to the Basement). Do not arrive early unless you are shopping please. Pickup some new running gear, sports nutrition, or Christmas gifts while you are there.

Age Groups for the 6k, 10k, 15k runs:  14 & under, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-79, 80 & over.  Ribbons for top 3 age group placers. Special gifts for top 3 men’s and women’s winners in each distance.

The 1k kids run is free this year, and is for kids 6 and under. Just report to the registration desk to sign the waiver & get their bib. This one is just for fun and is self-timed. All kids run finishers get a ribbon.  5-6 is not too young to do the 6k course, but separate sign up is required for that event.

Walking Groups: Walkers are welcome and encouraged to join in the fun.  For safety reasons, we ask walkers to stay to the right side of the path to allow runners to pass on the left.  The paths are narrow, so please do not block the whole path.

Opportunities to contribute to your community: The registration form includes a place to donate to our charity partners. The race organization also makes annual contributions. Please join us to help make Salem awesome.  

Participating again this year is Outward Church and their annual Thanksgiving Meal Program.  They are back at it this year organizing a feast for families in need.  Each Thanksgiving, they cook and deliver full meals to over 200 families, many of them were at least partially sponsored by generous Run’ucopia runners.  To sponsor a family’s full meal, it is $35.  Or please consider just the turkey at $20, or just the sides for $10.  The on-line registration form lets you donate any level you feel able to give. You can read more about it here: http://www.THXSalem.com

As you can imagine, there are a lot of logistics involved in cooking, loading and delivering this many meals. They need your help on the delivery. If you would like to join in delivering Thanksgiving meals, all are welcome, and your help is greatly appreciated. Just check out http://www.THXSalem.com

Salem Harvest is back again as a charity partner, and they also help feed economically-challenged families in our community. These volunteers will be guiding runners around the course.

Family Discount: There is a discount for families of 4+ for the race. To get the discount, on-line registration is required.  We just extended this family discount deadline to November 26. Just register and come get your bibs. As always, you get the best deal by registering early.

Raffle: After you get your bib, be sure to check out the raffle items. There are always cool gear, food, some quirky items to keep it interesting, and some kid stuff. Put your raffle tab from your bib in the jar of your favorite raffle item. You only win the stuff you want to win here.

Sponsors:

Gallagher's Fitness Resources, Dutch Bros Coffee, FastSigns South Salem.

Dutch Bros will be providing coffee and hot chocolate.

More information, including the Frequently Asked Questions, can be found on our webpage at www.RuninSalem.com.

Questions? Please email the Race Director at info@runinsalem.com or call/text 503.750.9245.  Do not contact Gallagher's Fitness Resources regarding the race. GFR is a sponsor and early packet pickup location, but questions go to info@runinsalem.com.

This is a minimalist & green event, so please use all recycling bins, and keep Salem clean.

Come early, enjoy the music and get pumped up!

name: Sandy Community Action Center Annual Tickle Trot 5K
description:
The Tickle Trot is a 5K in Sandy, Oregon that benefits the Sandy Community Action Center held Thanksgiving morning each year.

This year we will have a virtual race option for those that can't attend but wish to support our mission of feeding families in our local community.

This is a fun and informal event available to all ages and is untimed.

Last year our Thanksgiving Boxes serving 707 people in our community were completely funded by this event.  We were able to provide 8,600 pounds of food!

This year, we are excited to add the opportunity to purchase a finishers medal for $25.00 donation with your registration.  Please note, we only have 100 medals available so please register early and select the add on medal option!

description:
Come to Talent, Oregon for our Thanksgiving run! We will be hosting a food drive for the SOU food bank and a portion of the proceeds will go to SOR Student Runners Programs which include Shoes for Kids (provides shoes to Jr. High and High School athletes who would like to participate in Cross Country and Track but cannot afford proper running shoes), KidsRunFree (provides free entry to all SOR races for kids 18 & under), and XC Project (provides timing support for schools during cross country season).

When - November 26, 2025

Free Turkey Dash Kids Run( 8 and Under)8:00AM| 8 Mile Run 8:15AM|5k Run/Walk 8:30AM|2 Mile Family Run/Walk 8:40AM $20 for members| $25 for non members| Youth 18 and Under are free. name: Sprint Into Spring 5K
description:
USATF Certified, chip-timed 5K in Estacada! Experience a challenging yet rewarding course that takes you through the scenic city of Estacada. Starting with a short but steep climb that tests your early race strategy, the course then rewards you with rolling hills through beautiful neighborhoods and parks before culminating in an exhilarating downhill on Broadway that will have you flying to the finish line in downtown Estacada.

All proceeds go towards Estacada Parks & Recreation.

name: Stayton Fun Run
description:
Stayton Fun Run

Since 1983 Stayton has been celebrating fitness and this family tradition on the 4th of July. Both the runs and walk of this annual event will take place on asphalt and cross-country surfaces. The courses are excellent for the competitive runner, fun runner and walker.

The Runs and Walk is being held in conjunction with Stayton’s 4th of July festival. The festival features such activities as a Kid’s and Grand Parade, a community dinner, band concerts, variety show, kid’s games, food booths and a fantastic fireworks display. So, there is much to do after the race is over.

The MOST PATRIOTICALLY DRESSED RUNNER will win a patriotic denali blanket a $130. value 

WHEN: Every JULY 4th, starting at 9:00 a.m. (DAY OF REGISTRATION FOR TIMED RESULTS WILL END @ 8:45 AM) ***8:30am Race Day Scout Flag Ceremony (start your 4th of july off right)***

WHERE: Starts at the Stayton Community Center – 500 W Burnett St. (Off 1st St.). Stayton is 15 miles east of Salem on Highway 22.

FEE: $15.00 per person if you pre-register online (before July 4th). $20.00 per person day of the race (DAY OF REGISTRATION FOR TIMED RESULTS WILL END @ 8:45 AM). Registration begins at 7:30 a.m. at the Stayton Community Center.

INCLUDED: Ribbons to the top male and female finishers in five-year age-groups in the 5k and 10k races; Stay around after the race to see who won the most patriotically dressed!

WHAT’S NOT INCLUDED: High Entry Fees, Fancy Awards

Learn More About The Race: www.StaytonFunRun.com

name: The Fanciest 5K. Ever.
description:
The Fanciest 5K Ever is a recreational, fun, community race were runners fight human trafficking by running in formal wear! Dresses, tuxedos, bow ties, top hats, tiaras, all the glitz and glam… but on the run for a great cause! Got an old prom dress or ridiculously frilly suit you'd love to strut around in again? Fancy yourself up! All of the money raised goes directly to Safety Compass, a local organization that provides free, confidential advocacy for sex-trafficking survivors in the mid-Willamette Valley region of OR. 

Runners have the opportunity to become fundraisers and set individual or team goals for donations raised! We've got great prizes for the top fundraisers! 

2026 will be a In-Person AND VIRTUAL event, so runners can join us in Salem at West Coast Strength (290 Moyer Ln NW, Salem, OR 97304)  for all the fancy festivities and run the course across the river into River Front Park OR they can register and have a two week window to complete their fancy run and submit their time and photos virtually from wherever they are in the world! Prizes for top finishers, top fundraisers and fanciest costumes will be awarded at the end of the one week window.

RACE DAY SCHEDULE:
9:00 AM - Participant Check In, Bib and T-shirt Pick-up and Day-Of Registration Open inside the West Coast Strength (290 Moyer Ln NW, Salem, OR 97304)

10:00 AM - RACE STARTS at Start/Finish Line in the West Coast Strength parking lot. Runners head out onto the 5K Route through Wallace Marine Park and River Front Park, ending where they started!

11:00 AM - AWARDS CEREMONY starts inside West Coast Strength, Prizes for top finishers, top fundraisers and fanciest outfits!

name: The Great Books Tour 5K hosted by Gutenberg College
description:
The Great Books Tour 5K hosted by Gutenberg College

Run. Walk. Stroll.
Literary Fun for Everyone.

Join Gutenberg College for a one-of-a-kind Eugene community 5K inspired by great books, great ideas, and a healthy dose of humor.

Whether you come to race, stroll, wear a toga, or simply enjoy the atmosphere, The Great Books Tour 5K hosted by Gutenberg College is designed to be welcoming, memorable, and delightfully nerdy.

  • Humorous literary quote signs along the route
  • T-shirts available as add-on
  • Themed “tour” atmosphere
  • The legendary Socratic Sprint
  • Costumes and team themes
  • Music, community, and post-race fun
  • A custom winner medal
  • A beautiful Eugene course near Alton Baker Park and the river paths
  • All paces are welcome. Serious runners, casual walkers, families, students, book lovers, and costume enthusiasts alike are invited to join the fun.

Expect:
🏛️ Togas
📚 Literary references
🎭 Costumes
🏅 Winner medals and awards ceremony
😂 Terrible literary puns
👟 A genuinely fun morning in Eugene

Whether you’re channeling Aristotle, Austen, Tolkien, or simply your inner over-caffeinated reader, this is your chance to Run with the Greats.

Benefiting Gutenberg College, a Eugene-based liberal arts college devoted to thoughtful conversation, great books, and lifelong learning.

name: The Great Pumpkin Run
description:
Home Life is a 54 year old Oregon nonprofit that assists adults with intellectual and developmental
disabilities in Benton and Linn Counties. By signing up for the Great Pumpkin Run, you help make it
possible for over 150 of our community’s most vibrant and vulnerable citizens to receive the support
they need to live happy, healthy lives.


We are pleased to welcome local runners as well as their family and friends from all over to
participate in this Run/Walk event. We invite you to dress up for the Great Pumpkin Run.


You can choose between a 5k run/walk, or 10k run. Special pricing for those under 16.


For more information about Home Life’s work and mission and how you can support the work,
please check out our website.

name: Timing Test 5K & 10K McMinnville, OR (Timing Test)
description:
US Road Running Races

US Road Running races are built for runners and walkers who like friendly, low-pressure race days with just enough competition to keep things exciting. Our events are local, welcoming, and easy to jump into, whether you are chasing a PR, collecting another themed medal, working toward series points, or just getting outside with good people.

Most races are small enough to feel personal but organized enough to feel official. You can expect a clear course, helpful race staff, finisher medals, results, and a relaxed community feel. Bring your fast shoes, your steady walking pace, your favorite running buddy, or your best “I signed up for this on purpose” smile. We will be glad to see you at the start line.

A quick race-day note: because many US Road Running events are small local races, we normally have one or two staff members at each race. EMS is not stationed on site, and water stations are limited to the finish area at the end of each lap and at the race finish. Please plan for the weather, bring anything you may want between laps, and check in with race staff if you need help.

View Race Course, Results, and Race Information on the US Road Running race page.

name: Tofurky Trot
description:
Chase compassion Thanksgiving morning with a vegan and family friendly 5k! 

Presented by Northwest Veg, The Tofurky Trot is back with a new scenic and accessible course for 2026! Starting and finishing at OMSI in SE Portland, the trot will start off crossing the Tilikum Bridge, then head north up the west side waterfront path. After turning around, trotters will first head south, then cross Hawthorne Bridge before closing the loop by trotting south on the Eastbank Esplanade back to OMSI. 

What to Expect in 2026:

  • All Are Welcome: Kids, seniors, strollers, and leashed dogs are encouraged to join the fun. It’s not about speed — it’s about celebrating compassion together.
  • Costume Contest: Get festive! Dress up for the Tofurky-themed costume contest and show off your holiday spirit.
  • Meet the Cause: Representatives from local farm animal sanctuaries — the event’s beneficiaries will be present to connect with participants and share their mission.
  • Boka Marimba will be warming trotters up with their high energy African style marimba music from 8-8:45am
  • Enjoy post trot snacks after finishing

WHY TROT?

The Tofurky Trot is more than just a fun run — it's a meaningful way to kick-off the holiday with heart. Your registration fee helps support Northwest VEG outreach and local farm animal sanctuaries, providing food, shelter, and care for rescued animals.

This annual event promotes the benefits of a plant-based lifestyle while building a warm and welcoming community of compassionate individuals.

TROT DAY SCHEDULE: 

  • 7:30–8:30 AM: Trot check-in and same-day registration. Enjoy free beverages as you wait to kick off the Trot.
  • 8:00 AM: Boka Marimba takes the stage to get trotters warm and loosened up
  • 9:00 AM: Trot kicks off
  • Post-Trot: Enjoy free vegan bites.

PARKING AND TRANSIT:

name: USARA Adventure Race National Championships
description:
For more than 25 years, the annual USARA Adventure Race National Championships have seen some of the best teams from across the nation come together to compete in a non-stop, 30-hour adventure race. Many of these teams have to push the boundaries of human endurance and teamwork just to finish. Winning requires extreme willpower, mastery across disciplines, and sometime a little luck. 

When the race ends, teams come together for an evening meal. We announce the national champions, crown the winners of the national points series, and celebrate the amazing adventure racing community. 

The 2026 race is limited to teams of four in three divisions:  mixed gender, all-women, all-men.  There is not a separate masters division, though the top masters teams from across all divisions will be recognized.

Race check-in will be Thursday, October 22, 2026. The 30-hour race will start Friday morning, October 23, 2026, and end Saturday afternoon, October 24, 2026.

Priority registration opens January 1, 2026. Eligible teams will receive a link by email. Open registration begins February 1, 2026. You can find the most up-to-date information on the event at the USARA website.

REFUND POLICY:

The RunSignUp processing fee will be deducted from any and all refunds.  A racer who withdraws within one week of registering will receive a full refund, less processing fees.  A racer who withdraws more than one week after registering will receive a refund pursuant to the following scale: 


Before 6/1/26:  Entry fee less $50 and RSU processing fee
From 6/1/26 through 7/31/26:  Entry fee less $100 and RSU processing fee
From 8/1/26 through 8/31/25:  Entry fee less $200 and RSU processing fee 
From and after 9/1/26:  No refund


A racer can transfer their entry to another racer at no charge.  Contact nationals@usara.com to request a refund or transfer of entry.

name: 10th Annual Lake Forest Chamber Elf Yourself 5K
description:
The Lake Forest Chamber of Commerce's 9th Annual holiday FUN RUN 5K takes place in the stunning Lake Forest Sports Park on Saturday, November 21, 2026. It is a fast, flat course contained within the park. Our theme is Elf Yourself to kick off the holiday season! This is a fun family event for all, strollers and pets are welcome!

We have a large post-race expo with local restaurants passing out samples, vendors, and various fitness companies. There is even games & crafts for kids, photos with Santa, bounce houses, a hot chocolate station, and more! Make sure to bring your pets for our pet parade, there are awards for best dressed pets!

Stay up to date with our race by following our social media platforms on Facebook and Instagram!

Participants registering at the full entry price will receive our exclusive 10th Annual commemorative swag item, while discounted registrations will receive our standard race swag.

 

Packet Pick Up Information: 

Packet Pick-Up will be on Friday, November 20th from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM
Located at Spectrum Specialties & Awards/The Lake Forest Chamber Office
26239 Enterprise Court, Lake Forest, CA 92630

Next Door to South Coast Photography
MUST bring a copy of your signed waiver and an ID
If you want to pick up for a friend, you are able to do so if you have a picture of their ID and a signed copy of their waiver
If you can't make it at this time, we will also have packet pick up in the morning before the race, but make sure to arrive early! 
 

 

Day of Race Information

Parking: Enter the Sports Park from the Portola Parkway entrance (NOT Lake Forest Drive). We will be closing all park entrances prior to the race start for runner's safety. 

The Park will be on lockdown from 8 AM to 11 AM. There are NO exceptions to this rule because it is for runner's safety. 
Overflow parking will be available across the street at Saddleback Church (just a short walk away). If you need to arrive late or leave early, you must park over here and not inside the Park. 
Get to the start line early!
 

This is a timed event with 4 Waves!

  • Wave 1: Fast PR Elves
  • Wave 2: Speedy Elves
  • Wave 3: Runner/Jogger Elves
  • Wave 4: Walkers/Strollers/Pet Elves
     

Additional Runner Information:

The Start Line is located on the large grass area referred to as "the commons" before the soccer fields. 

Awards will be given in age groups for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd males and females. There will also be top overall awards for males and females. 
Every person will receive a Finishers Medal upon completion of the race!
Make sure to dress up in your best holiday gear! Don't be afraid to go all out!
 

Course Information:

It is a flat 2 1/2 looped course entirely within the Sports Park! We are running on the streets of the Park. 

It will be clearly marked with colorful arrows (one color per lap) & a lead cyclist from Pure Ride Cycles for the fastest runners.
We will have pacers leading each wave! 
 

Tentative Schedule of Events: 

8:00 AM - Runners Start to Arrive

8:30 AM - Race Announcer Starts/Line Up 

8:30-8:45 AM - Carolers 

8:45 AM - Herbalife Warm-Up

8:55 AM - National Anthem 

9:00 AM - Wave 1 Release Fast PR Elves
                Wave 2 Release Speedy Elves
                Wave 3 Release Runner/Jogger Elves
                Wave 4 Release Walker/Strollers/Pet Elves

9:00 AM - Expo Officially Opens

9:15 AM - Finish Line Medals (Ongoing)

9:30-11:00 AM - On Going Raffles & Expo Activities

10:00-10:15 AM - Podium Awards 

10:00 AM - Demo(s) 

10:30 AM - Pet Costume Contest 

10:45 AM - Pet Costume Awards

11:00 AM - Start Clean Up 

Introductions: 

  • Herbalife will be warming up the runners!
  • National Anthem
  • Jade Tully is your race announcer!
  • Caren Ware of Itz About Time will be timing our race!
  • Mary Visconte of Spectrum Specialties/CEO of the Lake Forest Chamber is our Race Director! 

Be sure to say HI to everyone! 
 

Post-Race Expo:


Don't run away after the race. Be sure to hold onto your Bib # to check if you won any raffle prizes! Raffles will be ongoing at the DJ station and written on a dry erase board. Keep checking back to see if you won! 

We have a Kid's Zone called Candy Cane Lane: photos with Santa, games, activities, bounce houses, and more!
Samples from the following: past vendors have included Urban Grill, La Casita Olvera, Coffee, Raising Cane's, A Little Something Sweet, & More! 
 

Fun Facts: 

  • Most of the race is put on by volunteers including our professional photographers: The Walman Photography, and Eagle Community Credit Union.
  • All your pictures are FREE! They will be uploaded onto our Elf Yourself Facebook photo albums, be sure to like our Page! You will be able to download the photos from there! 
  • Be sure to tag our Instagram and Facebook pages on any pictures you post of the event!
  • This Event Supports Local Chamber Charities (such as years past):

name: 11th Annual Combat Cancer Walk
description:
Get ready to make a difference and have a blast at the 11th Annual Combat Cancer Walk hosted by Support Sisterz!

This community event is all about raising funds for women in Corona, Norco, Eastvale, and surrounding areas who are battling breast and gynecologic cancers.

This isn't just any walk—it's a community celebration! We’re honoring survivors, supporting those currently fighting cancer, and remembering those we've lost.

- Registration and Festivities: Start at 7 AM 
- Opening Ceremony: 8:00 AM

name: 11th Annual SJVRC ONE MILE FOR ONE CHILD Charity Run 2026
description:

Check in time: 7 - 8AM

The race will start at 8:30AM.

name: 12th Annual Native Breast Cancer Awareness Walk/Run
description:
**If you are a Breast Cancer Survivor, please contact Adiyama before registering: 
alecanadau@wiltonrancheria-nsn.gov

Come enjoy a 1.4 mile walk or 2.8 mile run and a day of fun activities in support of NBCAWR! 


Early Bird Registration: $45 (starts June 15th; ends Aug. 9th) 

Late Registration: $55 (starts Aug. 10th; closes Sep. 11th) 


Registration includes:  event t-shirt, swag bag, light breakfast, lunch, drinks, and raffle ticket. 


Fun Zone: carnival games, jump house, balloon artist and face painting. 


Extra Fun Stuff: Mammo van onsite for screenings, health booths, exercise, Garden of Hope, honoring of Breast 
Cancer survivors, traditional healing, live entertainment.  

Please call 916-683-6000 ext. 2011 to make an appointment for a Mammogram Screening on the day of!

Our Journey:
To increase breast cancer awareness and screening, especially for 
Native American women.  Breast cancer is the second leading cause of 
death for Native American women.  It's estimated that approximately 1 in 
8 women will get breast cancer in her lifetime.  Our goal is to raise 
awareness and encourage women to screen early. 


PACKET PICKUP 
When: Friday, October 9th (Office closed on Oct. 12th)  
Time: 2PM - 6PM

Location: Wilton Rancheria Tribal Warehouse (9728 Kent Street, Elk Grove)  

Parking is available in the parking lot in front of the warehouse or on the street.

name: 13th Annual Turkey Trot OC 5K
description:
2026 ONLINE PRE-REGISTRATION IS OPEN!

Pre-registration is now open!

Now in its 13th year, we invite you to join us for the annual Turkey Trot OC 5K on Thanksgiving morning at 8:00 AM. Your participation helps continue the work of ending homelessness, one life at a time.

Lace up your shoes and help give OCRM families a hand-up as they leave homelessness behind.

REGISTRATION

Every participant must be registered to take part in the race.

Exception:  Children ages 5 and under, including those in strollers, are welcome to participate and do not need to register. However, T-shirts and medals are only for registered participants while supplies last.

Well-behaved dogs on leashes are allowed at the event and in the race. 

PACKET PICK-UP

Save time and pick up your race packet before race day. Participants may also pick up packets on behalf of other registered runners.

Packet pick-up will take place on:

  • Monday, November 23 & Tuesday, November 24 
  • 3:30 PM – 6:00 PM 
  • 1 Hope Drive, Tustin 92782

Packets may also be picked up on race morning from 6:30 AM – 7:30 AM.

RACE-DAY SCHEDULE

  • Pre-race refreshments — 6:30 AM 
  • 5K Run/Walk begins — 8:00 AM 
  • Expo & awards — immediately following the race 

This event will take place rain or shine. 

AWARDS

Age division awards will be given to the first- and second-place finishers in of each of the following category:  

9 & under, 10-14, 15-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+.

Top Finisher prizes will also be awarded to the top three overall male and female finishers.

GIVEAWAYS

2026 T-shirts & medals will be distributed to registered participants while supplies last due to limited quantities.

name: 14th Annual Luc's Run
description:
Luc's Run is held annually each spring in historic Tuolumne, California and Virtually Anywhere in the World. Luc's Run is known as one of the premier races in the county.  We are looking at welcoming our local 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under) back to Tuolumne, CA in 2023! And of course welcoming our supporters around the globe through our virtual run where hundreds of enthusiasts from around the world walk and run in support of Luc’s legacy on their own turf with a virtual 1/2 marathon, 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under). Sign up for two events and save 5%, sign up for all three and save 15%! 

On January 28, 2013, Luc, a United States Air Force pilot was on a training mission over the Adriatic Sea off the coast of Italy. During the sortie, Luc was forced to eject from his F-16 and did not survive the ejection.  Luc is survived by family and friends who continue his Legacy through the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation.

Major Lucas Gruenther was an incredible human being.  He was an outstanding F-16 fighter pilot, community role model, and a true humanitarian.  He lived his life to the fullest and never took a single day for granted.  Luc is remembered for the way he treated people with wisdom and kindness and was a genuine human being who made a tremendous positive impact.

All proceeds from this race go to the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation, an IRS-approved 501(c)(3) non-profit organization.  The purpose of the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation is to bestow scholarships to Americans for the advancement of educational goals and self development.

All proceeds from this race go to the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation, an IRS-approved 501(c)(3) non-profit organization.  The purpose of the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation is to bestow scholarships to Americans for the advancement of educational goals and self development.
