name: Bearathlon 2026
description:
Mark your calendars for October 24, 2026, and get ready to race at the Berkeley Marina! Registration is open until and on race day.

 

PACKET PICK-UP: 

Packet pick-up will tentatively be on Friday, October 23th, from 2pm - 6pm at Berkeley Sports Basement (2727 Milvia St.). 
Race morning pick-up is also available starting at 6am.
Packet pickup for friends and family is available - please just have a copy or photo of their ID

 

 

 

GENERAL INFO:

Transition opens at 6:00am for Draft Legal, at 6:45 for Classic and Relay Racers, and at 10:00am for Mixed Team Relays, with 30 minutes of swim warm-up available. The complete race schedule can be found on our website.
Transition closes at 6:45am for DL, at 9:00am for Classic and Relay Racers, and at 11:45 for Mixed Team Relays.

Please note that all timing is subject to change; any and all changes will be communicated explicitly.


If you are racing draft legal, no aero or TT bikes allowed, only road bikes. Please remove any aero bars. This race is meant for more advanced racers, so if you would like to transfer your registration, feel free to send us an email!
On all bikes: NO mirrors or glass of any kind are allowed
Draft-legal rules apply for the Mixed Team Relay, so no TT bikes allowed. The lap-out rule won't be enforced, so if you get lapped, you can still finish.
There will be a coaches/captains meeting at 6:45 AM before the Draft Legal race to cover rules and sportsmanship.
Water temperature is expected to be around 60°F, so we recommend wearing wetsuits. USAT wetsuit guidelines are found here. 

 

This year, we're excited to host four races:
🏊‍♂️ Draft-Legal Sprint: 750m swim, 20k bike, 5k run 
🚴‍♀️ Classic Sprint (Collegiate and Age Group): non-draft legal, 750m swim, 20k bike, 5k run
🏃‍♂️ Classic Relay (Collegiate and Age Group): team of three with each person racing one leg each (750m swim, 20k bike, or 5k run)
🔥 Mixed Team Relay (Collegiate and Age Group): team of four with each person racing a super sprint triathlon (250m swim, 5k bike, 1k run)

Bearathlon 2026 is designed for athletes of all levels, from beginners to elite competitors. With Open Age Group and Collegiate divisions, there’s a spot for everyone. Whether you're racing solo or as part of a team, you won’t want to miss this thrilling event! Please be sure to check the race website for packet pickup information and schedule changes: https://www.caltriathlon.com/bearathlon.

Packet pick up is available the day before: Friday, October 23th, and on race day. On Friday we will distribute packets at the local Sports Basement (2727 Milvia St., Berkeley) from 2pm - 6pm. On race day, we will be at the Berkeley Marina starting at 6am.

Join us for an unforgettable race day—see you at the start line! 🏁🐻

 

WETSUIT SERVICE: 

  • Martin from TCMTriSquad will have triathlon wetsuits available to rent to participants on race day!
  • To reserve a wetsuit in your size please email tricoachmartin@gmail.com with your weight and height. 
  • Martin will be at the race the morning of and will also have racebelts, locklaces, goggles, thermal caps and other triathlon supplies. 
  • Check out the website for information and costs: www.tricoachmartin.com/wetsuits
  • Wetsuits are not required but are recommended, the water temperature will be around 60 degrees, which is cold.

name: BEAST MODE -  HYBRID 5K CHALLENGE
description:
🔥 BEAST MODE — HYBRID 5K CHALLENGE


Sunday, April 10, 2027 | Long Beach, CA

Start the new year with something harder than a resolution.

THE RESET Hybrid 5K Challenge combines a 5K run with four fitness challenges designed to test your strength, endurance, and determination. Run your 5K, enter the Hybrid Zone, complete all four challenges, then earn your way across the finish line.

📍 Location: 5400 E. Ocean Blvd., Long Beach, CA 90803
⏰ Event Start: 8:00 AM

🏃 THE CHALLENGE
Complete the 5K run first, then enter the Hybrid Zone:

JUMP — 80m Burpee Broad Jumps
Chest to the ground. Get up. Broad jump forward. Repeat for 80 meters.

LUNGE — 100m Walking Lunges
Keep moving forward through the entire marked 100-meter zone.

CARRY — 100m Sandbag Carry
Pick it up and carry it through the complete 100-meter course.

SQUAT — 100 Bodyweight Squats
No equipment. Just you and 100 squats between you and the finish.

Then you're released to the FINISH LINE. 🏁

5K. FOUR CHALLENGES. ONE FINISH.
You don't have to be an elite athlete. You don't have to be the fastest runner. You just have to be willing to work.

Run. Jump. Lunge. Carry. Squat. Finish.

 🔥

name: Beaumont Santa Dash
description:
Run. Walk. Jingle. Parade!

Beaumont, it's time to get merry! The inaugural Beaumont Santa Dash is a festive ½-mile holiday run/walk that kicks off the Blizzard Bash Christmas Light Parade in spectacular fashion.

Grab your Santa suit, Christmas pajamas, ugly sweater, Grinch gear, elf ears, reindeer antlers or whatever makes you merry and join hundreds of holiday-loving participants as we take over the parade route before the floats and lights roll through! You don't have to be Santa to join the Santa Dash! Come dressed as Santa, Mrs. Claus, an elf, the Grinch, a reindeer, a Christmas tree, a snowman, your favorite holiday character, or simply your most festive self.

This isn't about speed - It's about fun, costumes, community and kicking off Christmas together!

WHAT TO EXPECT

  • A festive ½-mile run/walk
  • Hundreds of holiday-costumed participants
  • Music, holiday entertainment and Christmas cheer
  • And the start of Beaumont's Christmas Light Parade!

When the Dash is finished, stay where you are—the Christmas Light Parade is coming right behind you!

Let's make the inaugural Santa Dash one of Beaumont's biggest and merriest holiday traditions.

DASH DETAILS:

Date: Saturday, December 12
Race Start: 5:00 PM
Location: Beaumont Avenue & 10th Street
Course: Beaumont's half-mile Christmas Light Parade route

Starting at 10th Street & Beaumont Avenue, the parade/dash will travel south to 8th Street, turn left on 8th Street to Magnolia Avenue, where it will turn left on 6th Street and conclude at Maple Avenue and 6th Street.

Packet Pickup - Participants may pick up their bib, participant medal and Santa Hat at the following dates/locations:

  • Monday, December 7 - Thursday, December 10 from 8 am to 8 pm at the Community Recreation Center (CRC) at 1310 Oak Valley Parkway
  • Saturday, December 12th:
    • 2 pm and 4 pm at the Kids Zone at Blizzard Bash Market (Citi Bank parking lot)
    • 4:15 pm to 4:45 pm at the Race Starting Area 

Registration: $10 per person (includes bib, participant medal and custom Santa hat)

Everyone 5 years and older MUST register - unregistered runners will not receive a bib or hat

name: Bedrock Valley Gravel Ride
description:
2026 ATHLETE GUIDE  CLICK HERE                                       

                                           BEDROCK VALLEY GRAVEL RIDE

A Gravel Ride experience you don't want to miss. Choose your ride experience around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic ride in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

BEDROCK VALLEY GRAVEL RIDE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike

GRAVEL RIDE 36K takes you ONE LOOP around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Great for your first Gravel/Off-Road Ride

GRAVEL RIDE 72K takes you TWO LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Test your skills and make it a double.

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 108K takes you THREE LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Find your limits and test your endurance.

GRAVEL YOUTH 10K is a fun and flat fun ride for the spirited rider/beginner. An out and back course that gets you stoked!

NEW! GRAVEL KID'S 3k fun ride. Parents ride with your kids and get them on the dirt. For Kid's 10 and under.

TEAM CHALLENGE enjoy the ride with friends and complete laps as a team in the 72k and 108k.

name: Bedrock Valley Trail Runs
description:
BEDROCK VALLEY TRAIL RUNS

The Bedrock Valley Trail Runs is a NEW trail running experience you don't want to miss. We offer something for the whole family to enjoy. Choose from the beautiful  Bedrock Valley Trail Marathon, Trail Half Marathon, 15k, 10k, 5k, Stroller 5k and bring the kids for the the 1 Mile Kid's Fun Run around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic run in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

TRAIL MARATHON is a great introduction into trail marathons. A relatively flat loop around the lake ending with some beautiful double track. Ideal for all running levels.

TRAIL HALF MARATHON is a beautiful out and back section along the lake bed and perfect for accomplishing your first half marathon.

15K course challenges the runner with a little of everything: flat, fast, dounle track trail.

10K is a fast out and back with views of the lake.

5K is a fast and flat out and back. Great for a fast run or hike. 

STROLLER TRAIL 5k our first specific stroller only 5k is a beautiful flat 3.1 miles out and back. Enjoy with the little ones.

KID'S 1 MILE FUN RUN is open to children 10 and younger. This is a non-timed run. All kids receive a finisher’s medal and other goodies.

GRAVEL RIDE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike

We are a CUPLESS race series. Please make sure to bring some form of hydration vessel to carry hydration for your event. There will not be cups provided at aid stations.

5K is a fast and flat out and back. Great for a fast run or hike.

KID'S 1 MILE FUN RUN is open to children 10 and younger. This is a non-timed run. All kids receive a finisher’s medal and other goodies.

name: Bee Sweet Citrus Farm-K
description:
Join the Bee Sweet Citrus and Ag One teams on Saturday, February 13, 2027, for our 2nd annual Farm-K event! This run/walk is a family-friendly event that benefits the next generation of agriculturalists, and we'd love for you to join in on the fun. 

Register for our timed 5k or our 1 Mile Walk in support of the Fresno State Ag One Foundation!

The event takes place at Fresno State's O'Niell Park, and all participants earn an event shirt and a custom finisher's medallion.

name: Beginner Sailing November 7/8
description:
Two-day adult sailing classes are offered most weekends from 9 am to 4 pm at Fiddler's Cove Marina. Classes are open to all eligible MWR patrons and sponsored guests. Minimum age requirement is 16 years or older with a parent or guardian.

Class fees per person vary by military affiliation and rank. Dependent fees are calculated at the sponsoring active duty or retiree rate. Pre-registration is required as classes can fill up quickly.

Registration includes boat rental, instruction, and textbooks. Students per boat will be kept to the minimum amount possible in order to maximize learning potential and will range from one to four. Number of students per boat is dependent on the boat size, sailing conditions and the skills being developed in the class. On completion of the course, participants receive a Navy Sailing Qualification Card.

A valid California Boater Card and/or a course completion certificate is required before attending the first class. This is a free California Safety class required for all boat owners 16 years and older. California Boater Cards and/or course completion certificates will be checked at the start of the first class. A free online course is offered through https://www.boatus.org/california/.   Once the course is complete and an application has been filled out through California State Parks then a card will be sent in the mail to your address. A digital card will be emailed at the completion of the course and is a valid representation of a California Boater Card for this course.

Once you sign-up please stop by Fiddlers Cove Marina boathouse to pick up your study materials. Some preliminary reading will be given before the start of the course.

Please note: closed-toe shoes are required aboard all Navy MWR boats. Sunscreen, sunglasses, and hats are strongly recommended. The class will be held rain or shine, so please dress accordingly for weather conditions.

✨ Grab your bestie — and get ready for a day filled with movement, laughter, encouragement, and unforgettable memories by the beach. Or come solo and meet new friends who will cheer you on every step of the way.

This isn’t just a run — it’s a celebration of connection, confidence, community, and good vibes. 💖

• CHIP TIMING

This event is all about uplifting one another, building confidence, celebrating friendship, and proving that we can do hard things together.

name: Beverly Hills Run of the Stars: 2026
description:
Run for a Cause in Beautiful Beverly Hills!

Lace up and run through the flat, scenic streets of Beverly Hills at this year’s 5K on October 18th! Run on your own or on a team!

The 5K and the Kids 1K both start and end on the grounds, next to bib pick up, at El Rodeo Elementary, 605 Whittier Dr, Beverly Hills, CA 90210. All runners and walkers start together at the start time, you must be at the start line before your race starts.

Park on the streets, watch for no parking signs. BHPD will be towing anyone parked on no parking sides of the street, those are part of the race course.

Course maps and video course tour here.

Can’t make it in person? Join our Virtual Challenge and complete your 5K from anywhere in the world.

We’re also hosting a 1K “Stars of Tomorrow” Kids Race held at the same location right after the 5K- perfect for young runners ready to shine!

 

Running for a Cure

This event proudly supports Not Today Cancer and their mission to find a cure for childhood cancers.

Despite rising childhood cancer rates, only 4% of U.S. federal cancer research funding goes toward pediatric cancers.

When Mason was just 9 years old, he was diagnosed with T-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL). His treatment relied on chemotherapy drugs that have been used for decades- a painful reminder of how underfunded pediatric cancer research remains.

For two years, Mason and his family lived by the mantra “Not Today, Cancer.” After Mason’s passing, that spirit inspired the creation of the Not Today Cancer Foundation, dedicated to advancing research and offering hope to families like his.

Scientists are closer than ever to finding a cure and your participation helps make that possible.

name: Beyond The Streets 5k, 10k & Half Marathon
description:
REGISTRATION OPENS IN JANUARY!

Beyond The Streets is a FREE race benefiting North Valley Caring Services. Registration has not opened yet, but mark your calendar!

If you’ve run with Jed & Ted before, you’ll receive first access by email when registration opens. Space will be limited, so keep an eye on your inbox.

Jed & Ted's Excellent Races proudly present the second annual Beyond The Streets 5K, 10K & Half Marathon.

Join us as we take over the headwaters of the Los Angeles River near Canoga Park High School. This run is all about the real LA River experience, the sights, the sounds, the quiet moments, the unexpected pockets of life. and the community that moves along it.

This event is FREE, but we encourage donations. Every dollar goes directly to North Valley Caring Services, supporting the people and families who need it most. You’ll see an option to donate during registration.

We're making this event free because we want everyone to be able to show up, move their body, and be part of something good: no barriers, no pressure, no financial gatekeeping. But if you’re able to donate, even a little, it makes a real difference.

All donations go directly to North Valley Caring Services, an organization doing hands-on work with people experiencing homelessness, food insecurity, and crisis right here in the Valley. They run meal programs, hygiene services, family support programs, and help folks get back on their feet with dignity and real, practical assistance.

Think of it this way:

Half Marathon — 7:00 AM

The music is up. The sun is out. The ocean breeze is rolling in.

Welcome to Bidi Bidi Run Run, where vibrant colors, beach vibes, music, and feel-good energy come together for one unforgettable summer morning.

Whether you're chasing a new PR, dancing your way to the finish line, or simply soaking up the Southern California sunshine, this event is all about movement, music, community, and having a damn good time at the beach.

Bring your brightest outfit, your best energy, and get ready for a morning filled with music, miles, smiles, and summer vibes along the Long Beach shoreline.

🌊 What to Expect
✔️ Flat, fast, paved beach path course
✔️ Professional ChronoTrack chip timing ⏱️
✔️ Instant results within minutes

✔️ Custom finisher medal for every participant 🏅
✔️ Overall & Age Group Awards
✔️ Multiple on-course water stations 💧
✔️ High-energy music before, during, and after the race 🎶
✔️ Bright, colorful summer beach atmosphere 🌴
✔️ Walkers welcome
✔️ Dog-friendly & stroller-friendly

☀️ The Course
Starting at 5400 E. Ocean Blvd, you'll head out along the beautiful Long Beach shoreline on a flat, fast course with sweeping ocean views.

Feel the morning ocean breeze, take in the Pacific, and enjoy one of Southern California's most scenic places to run.

Whether you're tackling the 5K, 10K, or Half Marathon, you'll have plenty of course support, water stations, music, and CaliFlow energy waiting for you all the way to the finish line.

🌺 The Vibe
This isn't just another race...

It's a summer celebration.

🌴 Beach meets music
☀️ Sunshine meets miles
🎶 Every mile brings the energy
💃 Running shoes become dancing shoes

No pressure.
No judgment.

Just incredible people, beautiful scenery, positive energy, music, and one unforgettable summer morning on the beach.

🌺 Run. Dance. Celebrate.
Bidi Bidi Run Run is more than a finish line—it's a summer morning you'll want to come back for year after year. ☀️🌴🏃🏽‍♀️🎶

name: Bidwell Classic 5K, 10k and Half Marathon March 6th, 2027
description:
Join us for the Bidwell Classic 5K, 10k and Half Marathon. 

 

Celebrating 51 years of running in Bidwell Park in Chico CA this race has become a chico tradition for so many! We with 3 distances offered we are pleased to host the Bidwell Classic again in 2027! 

We are excited to offer a cash purse again for the top male and female in each event! 

 

BENEFITS STUDENT ATHLETES

A substantial portion of the race entry fees go to the local high school cross country running programs. When you participate in the Bidwell Classic, you are supporting local student athletes. If you would like to make an additional donation to the schools, please do so on the donation portion of the registration. Thank you so much for supporting this race and our local youth runners!

 

Online registration closes at 8:00am on Friday March 5th, 2027.  
In person registration will be available during packet pickup.
No in person registration will be available on race day.
 
Packet pickup will be available Friday March 5th 10:00am-4:00pm
Race day packet pick up will be available Saturday March 6th from 6:45am - 7:45am
Any questions about registration or packet pick up please email shawna@fleetfeetchico.com
 

 

START DATE & TIMES
When: Saturday March 6th, 2027

Where: Lower Bidwell Park/ Sycamore Field 

5K, 10k and Half Marathon run and fun walk: Starting time is 8:00am for the 5k and 8:10 for the 10k and Half Marathon.
 
Entry fees are non-refundable and non-transferable.
For special school group rates contact shawna@fleetfeetchico.com
 
Every registered runner will receive a 2027 race shirt if registered before February 5th. To guarantee your shirt size please register on or before February 5th. All registrations after February 5th will be subject to availability and size at packet pickup. Any leftover shirts after packet pick up will be available after the race at the Fleet Feet booth starting at 9:00am. 
If still running, you may have someone pick up a shirt for you. Please provide them your name and or bib #.
If you do not pick up your packet before the race (at packet pickup or at the race), your shirt will NOT be saved for you. 
 
COURSE CERTIFICATION AND MAPS
 
The 5k and 10k are flat, FRESHLY paved, and free of traffic. The half marathon has a 1/4 mile on each of the loops that are a single-track trail. All events start and finish at One Mile Recreation Area in Lower Bidwell Park.
 
The maps to all the racecourses can be found by clicking the link below:
Race Maps - Fleet Feet Chico

 

 
PACKET PICKUP
 
Packet pickup will be offered at Fleet Feet Chico (241 Main St in downtown Chico) We will also have a small window on race day to pick up your packet.
 
Packet Pickup days and hours: 
 
Friday March 5th at Fleet Feet Chico
10:00am - 4:00pm
 
Located at Fleet Feet Chico, 241 Main St., Chico CA
 
Race Day Packet Pick up at the Fleet Feet Tent
6:45am-7:45am ONLY

 

RACE SHIRTS:


Race shirts are a unisex cotton shirt printed by Arroyo (formally Upper Park Printing) To be guaranteed a shirt in your size, you need to register on or before February 5th, 2027. All registration entries received after 2/5/27 will have shirts based on limited availability on a first come first serve basis.

 
DIRECTIONS AND PARKING
 
To the course: Enter Chico via Highway 99 either from the north or from the south. If you are coming from the north on 99, take the Highway 32 offramp and turn right at the first intersection. If you are coming from the south on 99, take the 32 offramp and turn left at the second intersection. Now you're heading west on 32 (East 8th St). From here, take 8th St just under a half-mile, then turn right on Sycamore St.

Sycamore St runs a few blocks into Woodland Ave, which runs parallel to the park. The park itself will be closed to vehicle traffic on race day, so find a parking spot on or near Woodland Ave. Please be courteous and park legally. Do not park in a way that blocks local residents' entry to or exit from their homes. There are several entrances to the One Mile Recreation Area from Woodland Ave. 

To Fleet Feet packet pickup: As above, from Highway 99 head west on Highway 32 (East 8th St).
Take 8th St about a mile then turn right on Main St. Drive north on Main St. Fleet Feet is located between 2nd and 3rd Streets. Fleet Feet's phone number is 530 345-1000.

 

Bike Valet

Free and Secure Bicycle Parking provided by Chico Velo

Bike valet will be available at the race this year! We encourage you to ride your bikes to the race and Chico Velo will have their bike valet services available to make sure your bike is safe while you run! This is a great way to warm up or cool down before and after your race.

To encourage you to ride we are doing a raffle for everyone wo checks a bike in!

 

TIMING
Timing will be done by Bizz Johnson Racing. All races will be a gun start and a chip finish. If you are racing for an overall placement, you must toe the line! (Based on Gun time/first to cross the line)
 
Gun start for 5k will be at 8:00am
Gun start for 10k, and Half Marathon will be 8:10am
 

AID STATIONS AND RESTROOMS
There will be 6 aid stations for the half, 3 for the 10k and 2 for the 5k.
1.     Cedar Grove Bathrooms – Loop 1 Water / Loop 2 Water, nutrition gels and electrolytes 
2.     Peterson Drive Gate – Loop 1 Water / Loop 2 Water, nutrition gels and electrolytes 
3.     One Mile Parking Lot on Vallombrosa Side – Water and electrolytes 
Restroom on the course will be located at One Mile recreation on the North and South side of the pool, Cedar Grove Park, and Pettersen Dr. Park entrance as well as portable restrooms at the start and finish.
 
RULES
 
  • Please no dogs on the course during the race. Stollers are allowed, please be cautious of other runners. If wearing headphones, only in one ear please! Must be able to hear your surroundings.
  • Be courteous when overtaking slower runners or walkers in your elected race location. We want you to race hard and fast, but with safety of yourself and others in mind. (Please remember that this is a public park and there may be others on course that are not part of the race)
     
  • Where your Race number so it is visible on the participant's front
  • Run your race with pride!
  • You must cross the timing mat for your chip to be read. If you are planning of racing for top finisher, the race is based on gun time and first to cross the finish line.
  • Run, hard, run fast and have fun!
     
 
AWARDS FOR TOP FINISHERS
 
We will be offering a CASH PRIZE Top male and female for each race! (5k, 10k and Half) We will have an award ceremony at 8:45am for the 5k, 9:15am for the 10k and 10:00am for the Half Marathon races.
 
Age group awards can be found at the Fleet Feet tent following the award ceremony for each race. 
(Awards will also be offered to the top three in each age group category for each gender in each race)
 
All unclaimed prized will be available for pick up at Fleet Feet Chico on Sunday March 8th during regular business hours. (11:00am-4:00pm)
 
Ages groups will be as followed: 
14 and under / 15-19 / 20-29 / 30-39 / 40-49 / 50-59 / 60-69 / 70 and over
 
Finisher Medals will be provided to all Half Marathon runners who finish the race.
(Any remaining medals will be available for pick up at Fleet Feet Chico for 5k and 10k runners on Sunday March 8th)
 
 
Please visit www.fleetfeetchico.com for more information or email shawna@fleetfeetchico.com

Packet pickup will be offered at Fleet Feet Chico (241 Main St in downtown Chico) We will also have a small window on race day to pick up your packet.
 
Packet Pickup days and hours: 
 
Friday March 5th at Fleet Feet Chico
10:00am - 4:00pm
 
Located at Fleet Feet Chico, 241 Main St., Chico CA
 
Race Day Packet Pick up at the Fleet Feet Tent
6:45am-7:45am ONLY

 

RACE SHIRTS:


Race shirts are a unisex cotton shirt printed by Arroyo (formally Upper Park Printing) To be guaranteed a shirt in your size, you need to register on or before February 5th, 2027. All registration entries received after 2/5/27 will have shirts based on limited availability on a first come first serve basis.

 
DIRECTIONS AND PARKING
 
To the course: Enter Chico via Highway 99 either from the north or from the south. If you are coming from the north on 99, take the Highway 32 offramp and turn right at the first intersection. If you are coming from the south on 99, take the 32 offramp and turn left at the second intersection. Now you're heading west on 32 (East 8th St). From here, take 8th St just under a half-mile, then turn right on Sycamore St.

Sycamore St runs a few blocks into Woodland Ave, which runs parallel to the park. The park itself will be closed to vehicle traffic on race day, so find a parking spot on or near Woodland Ave. Please be courteous and park legally. Do not park in a way that blocks local residents' entry to or exit from their homes. There are several entrances to the One Mile Recreation Area from Woodland Ave. 

To Fleet Feet packet pickup: As above, from Highway 99 head west on Highway 32 (East 8th St).
Take 8th St about a mile then turn right on Main St. Drive north on Main St. Fleet Feet is located between 2nd and 3rd Streets. Fleet Feet's phone number is 530 345-1000.

 

Bike Valet

Free and Secure Bicycle Parking provided by Chico Velo

Bike valet will be available at the race this year! We encourage you to ride your bikes to the race and Chico Velo will have their bike valet services available to make sure your bike is safe while you run! This is a great way to warm up or cool down before and after your race.

To encourage you to ride we are doing a raffle for everyone wo checks a bike in!

 

TIMING
Timing will be done by Bizz Johnson Racing. All races will be a gun start and a chip finish. If you are racing for an overall placement, you must toe the line! (Based on Gun time/first to cross the line)
 
Gun start for 5k will be at 8:00am
Gun start for 10k, and Half Marathon will be 8:10am
 

AID STATIONS AND RESTROOMS
There will be 6 aid stations for the half, 3 for the 10k and 2 for the 5k.
1.     Cedar Grove Bathrooms – Loop 1 Water / Loop 2 Water, nutrition gels and electrolytes 
2.     Peterson Drive Gate – Loop 1 Water / Loop 2 Water, nutrition gels and electrolytes 
3.     One Mile Parking Lot on Vallombrosa Side – Water and electrolytes 
Restroom on the course will be located at One Mile recreation on the North and South side of the pool, Cedar Grove Park, and Pettersen Dr. Park entrance as well as portable restrooms at the start and finish.
 
RULES
 
  • Please no dogs on the course during the race. Stollers are allowed, please be cautious of other runners. If wearing headphones, only in one ear please! Must be able to hear your surroundings.
  • Be courteous when overtaking slower runners or walkers in your elected race location. We want you to race hard and fast, but with safety of yourself and others in mind. (Please remember that this is a public park and there may be others on course that are not part of the race)
     
  • Where your Race number so it is visible on the participant's front
  • Run your race with pride!
  • You must cross the timing mat for your chip to be read. If you are planning of racing for top finisher, the race is based on gun time and first to cross the finish line.
  • Run, hard, run fast and have fun!
     
 
AWARDS FOR TOP FINISHERS
 
We will be offering a CASH PRIZE Top male and female for each race! (5k, 10k and Half) We will have an award ceremony at 8:45am for the 5k, 9:15am for the 10k and 10:00am for the Half Marathon races.
 
Age group awards can be found at the Fleet Feet tent following the award ceremony for each race. 
(Awards will also be offered to the top three in each age group category for each gender in each race)
 
All unclaimed prized will be available for pick up at Fleet Feet Chico on Sunday March 8th during regular business hours. (11:00am-4:00pm)
 
Ages groups will be as followed: 
14 and under / 15-19 / 20-29 / 30-39 / 40-49 / 50-59 / 60-69 / 70 and over
 
Finisher Medals will be provided to all Half Marathon runners who finish the race.
(Any remaining medals will be available for pick up at Fleet Feet Chico for 5k and 10k runners on Sunday March 8th)
 
 
Please visit www.fleetfeetchico.com for more information or email shawna@fleetfeetchico.com

name: Big Bear Turkey Trot
description:
The 13th Annual Big Bear Turkey Trot
📍 Our new home in the Moonridge Corridor, starting and finishing at Dank Donuts.
🌲 A fresh route including the new Rathbun Creek Trail, and a memorable lap through the Moonridge Zoo 🦓🦙🦅.
🏃 A paved 3-mile run through the pines that’s approachable for everyone!
🎶 Danksgiving Celebration party at the finish line featuring live holiday music and adult beverages 🍹

 
🗓️ Event Schedule

8:00 AM - Registration & check-in opens
9:25 AM - Holiday Warmup Yoga 🧘 with Colin Schour
9:30 AM - 3-Mile Turkey Trot 🦃
10:00 AM - Danksgiving Party 🎶🍩🥂 with live music & adult beverages
10:30 AM - Awards 🏆 & Costume Contest 🎭
 
💸 Registration
Adults: $40
Youth (under 18): $25
Kids Run: Free
Locals: $5 discount with ID at packet pickup
No refunds (rain, shine, or snow—it’s all part of the fun).
 
🎁 Included with Entry:

🎄 A holiday finisher ornament
🧘 A lighthearted yoga warm-up
🎭 A lively costume contest
🥧 Race timing and awards eligibility (elite wave start available for those who's costume is considered worthy). 
🎶🍹 The Danksgiving party at the finish line
 
📦 Packet Pickup

🗓️ Monday, Nov 23 – Wednesday, Nov 25 (4–7 PM): The Yellow Post, 546 Pine Knot Blvd
🦃 Race Morning, Nov 26 (8–9 AM): Dank Donuts, 42612 Moonridge Rd Big Bear Lake, CA
 
 
🙋 FAQs

Strollers & kids? Strollers are welcome, and the kids under 5 are free.
Refunds? Nope. The Turkey Trot happens in any weather.
Local discount? Show ID for $5 off.
What’s included? Ornaments, yoga, pie, costumes, music, and memories.

The Big Bear Turkey Trot has always been about more than miles—it’s a morning of laughter, costumes, pie, and community. This year, we’ll gather in Moonridge, run the trail, visit the zoo, and then celebrate together at Danksgiving. We’ll see you out there. 🦃✨

name: Big River Adventure
description:
Welcome to the 26th annual Big River Adventure!

Join us for a unique race experience where you can choose your adventure to run, swim, walk, or paddle your way through the scenic beauty of Mendocino County's Big River.

For the past 26 years, Cancer Resource Centers of Mendocino County has been bringing our community together for this special fundraising event. While the activities may change from year to year, our mission remains steadfast: to honor and remember those impacted by cancer, and to raise vital funds to support free services for individuals facing cancer in Mendocino County.

Starting at the Big River boat launch, participants will embark on a journey filled with stunning views and the shared goal of making a difference in the lives of others.

Don't miss out on this unforgettable adventure! Register now and be part of something truly meaningful.

To keep this family-friendly event affordable and accessible to our community, we will not be providing t-shirts this year.

Here is a link to a trail map

•             5k runners will run east on the haul road to the 5k turn around.

•             10k runners dash east on the haul road to the 10K turn around (10K map).

•             5k "Fun" Walkers will follow the 5k runners route.

•             Kiddie run will begin at the boat launch

•             Swimmers will dive in at the boat lunch and swim east up Big River

•             Paddlers will begin at the boat launch and paddle east up Big River  *Please note you must bring your own vessel.

There are multiple race age divisions. Note: Participants between the ages of 6 and 17 may enter any race division at a discounted rate of $20 at signup.

Race Contact Info

Phone / Teléfono: (707) 937-3833

E-mail / Correo electrónico: info@crcmendocino.org

name: Big Sur River Run
description:
Big Sur River Run is a benefit race for two important Big Sur community organizations, Big Sur Health Center and Big Sur Fire. There are two races, a 10k and 5k. Both courses are all flat, black-top road loops alongside Big Sur River, through Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park's redwood and oak grove campgrounds. The 10k is a certified course. The 5k is a Family Fun Run or Walk. No Bicycles, dogs, strollers, skates, wagons, or other wheeled conveyances (other than wheelchairs) are permitted. Prizes for 10K Race winners and top finishers.

Since 1981 two of Big Sur’s most vital institutions have been supported by the generosity of those who love to run. Most who visit Big Sur revel in the remoteness without taking in the impact it has on emergency services. The local Volunteer Fire Department, Big Sur Fire, and the Big Sur Health Center both rely on donations to provide support for visitors and residents alike. The run’s beneficiaries, Big Sur Fire and the Big Sur Health Center, have never done more to serve and support our community than in recent years. These critical emergency services need our support more than ever and we encourage you to donate to each organization directly. To date over 30,000 runners have joined the cause, supporting these institutions, and basking in the beauty of Big Sur. Will you join us this year?

name: Bigfoot 5K. 10K. 15K by Califlow Runs
description:
👣 BIGFOOT — GRIFFITH PARK
5K • 10K • 15K
Something has been spotted in Griffith Park.

📍 Griffith Park – Crystal Springs
Crystal Springs Picnic Area
4730 Crystal Springs Dr, Los Angeles, CA 90027

Google Maps Link to Start/Finish Line:
https://maps.app.goo.gl/KvTBMBbE7HQXA4b68

📅 Sunday, February 28, 2027

🕓 Check-In & Registration: 7:00 AM

🏁 Start Times
5K: 8:00 AM
10K: 8:00 AM
15K: 8:00 AM

👣 ABOUT THE EVENT
Something has been spotted in Griffith Park.

Strange footprints. Movement between the trees. Branches snapping when no one else seems to be around.

Some say it was a hiker.

Some say it was wildlife.

Others are absolutely convinced Bigfoot is roaming Griffith Park.

On February 28, we're going looking for him.

Welcome to BIGFOOT, a 5K, 10K and 15K running adventure through one of Los Angeles' most iconic parks.

Keep your eyes on the trees. Watch for footprints. And if you hear something moving behind you...

Maybe run a little faster.

Will you spot Bigfoot?

Will you leave Griffith Park a believer?

There's only one way to find out.

🌲 WHAT TO EXPECT
✔️ 5K, 10K & 15K distances
✔️ Scenic Griffith Park course 🌿
✔️ Professional ChronoTrack chip timing ⏱️
✔️ Instant race results
✔️ FREE race-day photos 📸
✔️ Custom BIGFOOT finisher medal for all finishers 🏅
✔️ Overall & age group awards 🏆
✔️ Multiple on-course water stations 💧
✔️ Music & finish-line fun 🎶
✔️ Beginner friendly
✔️ Walkers welcome
✔️ All paces welcome
✔️ Bigfoot sightings not guaranteed 👀

🌿 THE COURSE
Set within beautiful Griffith Park, the course follows a scenic 5K loop around the golf course, surrounded by trees, open spaces and classic Southern California scenery.

Choose your adventure:

5K — 1 Loop
10K — 2 Loops
15K — 3 Loops

You'll experience stretches of sunshine and shade, wide pathways and peaceful park scenery—all while running right in the middle of Los Angeles.

The loop-style course is easy to follow and welcoming for runners and walkers of a wide range of abilities.

Race it hard. Jog it with friends. Walk it. Bring your crew.

Just remember:

Every trip around the park is another chance to see him.

👀 BIGFOOT WATCH
Bigfoot has been part of American folklore for generations—a mysterious, towering creature said to roam forests and wilderness just beyond where we're looking.

And for one morning, we're bringing the legend to Griffith Park.

You may notice a few unusual things along the course.

A footprint that seems a little too large.

Something moving between the trees.

Maybe even a Bigfoot sighting.

Was it real?

Was it your imagination?

We're not saying.

Keep your eyes on the trees.

🏃 EVERYONE BELONGS AT THE START LINE
You don't have to be fast enough to outrun Bigfoot to run with us.

At CaliFlow Runs, our start lines are built for everyone.

🔥 Chase a PR
🌲 Enjoy the scenery
🐶 Run with your four-legged partner
👟 Bring your running crew
🚶 Walk the 5K
🏅 Run all three loops and conquer the 15K
👣 Or come because you really want that Bigfoot medal

Whether you're racing, walking, chasing a goal or just coming out for a ridiculously fun morning in Griffith Park, there's a place for you here.

🌄 THE VIBE — SOMETHING'S OUT THERE
Los Angeles may be known for freeways, beaches and Hollywood, but Griffith Park has always had a wilder side.

Trees. Hills. Wildlife. Hidden corners.

And apparently...

Bigfoot.

So grab your running shoes, bring your friends and come investigate the latest Griffith Park sighting for yourself.

👣 BIGFOOT
Griffith Park • February 28, 2027
5K • 10K • 15K


SOMETHING'S OUT THERE.

Will you leave a believer?

name: Bike The Coast
description:
Experience gorgeous riding along pristine beaches, historic Pacific Coast Highway, iconic beach landmarks and unique, Southern California weather with the annual Bike The Coast Bike Tour.   Select from distances of 7, 15, 25, 50, and 100 mile rides and then come out and ride along with 2000 other enthusiast along some of Southern California's best-known cities and roadways.  When you finish, meet us back at  the Oceanside pier to celebrate with your selection of food options, a lively beer garden, great music and new friends.

This is a truly bucket list event if you are an avid rider who enjoys getting some exercise, having fun, and experience great November weather.  This is a 'rules of the road' ride so come prepared to obey all traffic laws.

name: Bikes & Beers San Diego
description:
Register for California's 14th Annual Bike Ride & Beer Festival 2026! BIKES & BEERS Cycling Event Series is back at ALESMITH BREWING COMPANY for the Best Bike Ride & Beer Event in the business! Ride a 15, 30, or 45-mile route through the beautiful area of San Diego, California followed by a post-ride Beer Festival! Bikes & Beers SAN DIEGO is the area's premier cycling event departing from ALESMITH BREWING COMPANY and traveling the scenic roads of San Diego, CA. All rides feature morning fuel stations, marked routes, GPS turn-by-turn instruction, rest stops, refreshments, ride marshals, and SAG support. Finish back at ALESMITH BREWING COMPANY for a beer festival atmosphere of rewarding craft beers, live music, a charity raffle & much more!

This is a ride for everyone - All riding levels are welcome!


WHAT IS BIKES & BEERS:

  • Pick your ride distance and create a team of friends & family (optional)
  • Mark your calendar for a fun day of cycling and craft beer!
  • Pre Ride:
    • Check in a half hour before your start time
    • We'll provide parking & further ride info in email instructions
    • Enjoy free coffee & fresh pastries
    • Local bike shops offering last-minute tune-ups
  • The Ride:
    • Ride your distance with ride leaders
    • Fully marked routes & GPS turn-by-turn instructions
    • Mechanical support vehicle
    • Rest stops with snacks & refreshments
  • Post Ride: 
    • It's time to enjoy (2) complimentary beers on us!
    • Official co-branded Bikes & Beers Pint Glass for every rider
    • Bikes & Beers high-quality neoprene koozies
    • Enjoy the food trucks, live music, games
    • Check out our Bikes & Beers merch tent & snack stand
    • Live raffle with $2,000+ in prizes!
  • Join & Post your photos on our Facebook Page
    • Keep in touch with your newly made cycling friends!

*Further event information will be communicated in emails after registration and in the days and weeks leading up to event day!


WHAT YOU'LL GET:

  • Official Bikes & Beers X ALESMITH 2026 Pint Glass
  • (2) ALESMITH Craft Beers are ON US!
  • High-Quality Neoprene Beer Koozies
  • Raffle Ticket with a Chance to WIN PRIZES!
  • Collectable Bike Plate - Event Photos!
  • Unique Pretzels & Athletic Non-Alcoholic Beer
  • Entry into the Post-Ride Party with LIVE MUSIC, RAFFLE, GAMES, FOOD TRUCKS & MORE!


NEW TO OUR 2026 EVENTS:

  • PROFESSIONAL PHOTOGRAPHERS - At least (3) photographers will be snapping pics of your Bikes & Beers experience during pre-ride, during the ride, and post-ride! We have amazing photo ops!
  • NON-ALCOHOLIC BEER OPTIONS - Still want to ride with us but don't want the alcohol? We now have Athletic Brewing sponsoring all our events! Looks for the blue tent and cooler full of flavorful non-alcoholic brews!
  • COLLECTABLE BIKE PLATES - At check-in, you'll receive a collectible event wristband and bike plate designed just for this event! They look awesome!
  • SPONSOR SNACKS & GIVEAWAYS - Morning coffee, fresh pastries, post-ride pretzel necklaces, recovery protein & much more!
 

IT'S A CELEBRATION OF CYCLING AND CRAFT BEER!

Riders will also receive a free raffle ticket for a chance to win a brand-new bike and a ton of other prizes including a private brewery tour and cycling gear!

Benefitting local cycling charities to help improve the cycling conditions in your area. Have fun, and give back!

name: Bizz Johnson
description:
Set PRs and qualify for the Boston Marathon on this fast, downhill course! Total net downhill loss for the marathon is 929 feet making it the PERFECT course to qualify on! Per official B.A.A. confirmation, there will be no time penalties assessed for this course.

All races in 2026 will be Sunday, October 11. The marathon and 50K start at 8:00 AM at Mason Station Trailhead on McCoy Road with an out-and-back before jumping onto the Bizz Johnson Trail at Mason Station where the races travel through scenic Lassen National Forest. The first few miles of the course climb approximately 280 feet through the forest to Westwood Junction, then it’s downhill to the finish at Susanville, with a 1300-foot descent over the final 20 miles. The trail follows the route of the old Fernley and Lassen Branch Line of the Southern Pacific Railroad, built in 1914.

Roughly two-thirds of the way through the race, the trail enters the Susan River Canyon. Here, you’ll pass orange cliffs and cross the river ten times on picturesque wooden railroad bridges. About four miles from the finish, you’ll pass through two former railroad tunnels, 800 feet and 450 feet in length.

The Express Half Marathon starts at at 9:00 AM at Goumaz Campground which is Mile 14 of the full marathon route. After a short up-and-back, the Express Half Marathon flies down the Bizz Johnson to the finish.

Starting at Devil's Corral, the new Express 10K on Sunday does the last 6.2 miles of the full marathon. This course promises to be a fast, fun race. 

For all four events, you will be bused to a remote start.

PACKET PICKUP

  • Saturday Noon - 6 PM (50K, Marathon, Express Half Marathon, Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road
  • Sunday Morning 6 AM - 7AM (Marathon and 50K), 7AM - 8 AM (Express Half Marathon and Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road

PLEASE visit our website for maps, schedules, and all the important details!!

USAT&F certified full marathon course (CA18035RS)

name: Bizz Johnson's Southside Scramble
description:
Are you ready to SCRAMBLE? This amazing new trail race showcases the best of the Susan River Canyon! Runners will head up the Bizz Johnson Trail from Hobo Camp for the first half and return via the beautiful and flowy singletrack on the Southside trail across the river. The Southside Scramble has 3 different distances to choose from, a 22K, a 14K, and a 7K. All races start and end at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area. For ODD-numbered years, the course is reversed! Occasionally, the RD will mix up the entire course and you'll just have to follow the signs. DON'T WORRY! IT'S VERY WELL MARKED!!

For the Dirty Devil's 22K, runners start on the Fire Road above Hobo Camp, merging onto the Bizz Johnson Trail and take the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail all the way to Devil's Corral. From Devil's Corral, runners turn and drop down to the Susan River, crossing over a seasonal foot bridge, and enter the stunningly beautiful South Side trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp.

The Tunnel's Blast 14K starts on the Fire Road above Hobo Camp, merging onto the Bizz Johnson Trail and takes the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail to the entrance to the first railroad tunnel. Before heading into the darkness of the tunnel, runners will veer off onto singletrack, where they climb over the top of the tunnel to reach the South Side Trail. From there, they will enjoy the stunningly beautiful South Side trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp

The "Hobo's Special" 7K starts on the Fire Road above Hobo Camp, merging onto the Bizz Johnson Trail  and heads up to the Twin Bridges Access connector to the South Side Trail. You'll get just enough of the Bizz Johnson's steady climb to excite your senses for the fast, flowy South Side's single-track return. Once you get to the finish, enjoy a cold beverage, snacks, BBQ hotdogs for finishers, and a cool dip in the Susan River! Families and friends are welcomed to bring chairs, put up a canopy, and use the day-use BBQ grills for more fun.

name: Blue Canyon Backcountry Trail Work
description:
Runners for Public Lands (RPL) envisions a world in which everyone has access to healthy, runnable landscapes. We are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that empowers runners to protect public lands and expand access to nature for all. 

We are excited to partner with the Santa Barbara Foundation, Los Padres Forest Association, the Santa Barbara Trail League, and the United States Forest Service (USFS), to present the 2026 Trail Work Series in Santa Barbara County. This brings our local community of runners together to learn about and care for the living landscapes we run with. Through repetitive, hands-on service events, we can grow ecological values and create strong connections that inspire runners to care for the places they love. 

This is the 5th event for our 2026 Santa Barbara Trail Work Series. Each event is approved, permitted, and insured by the USFS, led by the Los Padres Forest Association trail work leaders, and managed by Runners for Public Lands  Ambassadors. Please note that the days and times of all events are subject to change based on the discretion of the USFS, current conditions, and weather. We will keep everyone informed through the Runners for Public Lands Ventura/Santa Barbara Strava Club and direct emails to registrants.

name: BMR Sacramento Black History Month Family 5k Walk/Run! We're creating GENERATIONAL HEALTH!
description:
Black Men Run Sacramento presents our 4th Annual Black History Month Family 5k Run/Walk!

OUR MISSION: The Black History Month Family 5k Walk/Run encourages healthy lifestyles within the Black community by promoting physical activity like running and walking while fostering connections with BIPOC organizations dedicated to improving health outcomes. This event helps creates a new standard for generations to follow. This is Generational Health!

We welcome walkers and runners to choose whichever distance works for you and your family! Net proceeds go to the Roberts Family Development Center. Free medals provided (while supplies last). The race starts and ends at REI Sacramento.

name: BOLD BREAKTHROUGHS 2026 CSNK2A1 Foundation "Move Your Way" Challenge
description:
JOIN US THIS OCTOBER!

Bold Breakthroughs Month | October 1–31, 2026

Join our global Okur-Chung Neurodevelopmental Syndrome (OCNDS) community as we come together throughout the month of October to raise awareness and fund research that brings us closer to better treatments.

Our Community Celebration Weekend is October 10–11, 2026, when families and supporters around the world will share their photos, stories, and activities online. Can't participate that weekend? No problem! Complete your challenge anytime during October and celebrate with us.

Register by September 18, 2026, to help ensure your event T-shirt arrives before Celebration Weekend.

LAST YEAR, YOU MADE A BREAKTHROUGH POSSIBLE

Because of our incredible community, last year's Bold Breakthroughs campaign raised enough to fund a $50,000 pilot research grant. This year, we're working together to fund the next one.

This year, we set out to do it again and we reached that goal. Now we're stretching to $60,000. Every dollar beyond $50,000 helps us build on this investment by funding the additional research, data, tools, and next steps that can move promising discoveries forward.

Every registration, every donation, and every shared story helps move us forward.

DO I HAVE TO RUN?

Absolutely not!

Bold Breakthroughs is about moving your way—not running a race.

Choose an activity that fits your abilities, interests, and schedule.

You can:

  • Run
  • Walk
  • Roll (wheelchair, walker, scooter, stroller)
  • Ride a bike
  • Roller skate or rollerblade
  • Swim
  • Hike
  • Dance
  • Play golf
  • Walk your dog
  • Do 100 push-ups
  • Create your own challenge
  • Whether you move for five minutes or five miles, every step helps advance OCNDS research.

THIS YEAR'S THEME: BOLD BREAKTHROUGHS

WHY PARTICIPATE? WHY DONATE?

OCNDS is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition that significantly impacts the lives of affected individuals and their families.

This year, we're raising $50,000 to support research focused on the priorities identified by families and researchers during our recent scientific convening, including:

  • Sleep
  • Speech and language
  • Anxiety
  • Intellectual disability
  • Gastrointestinal health
  • Drug repurposing
  • Gene therapy feasibility studies

Your support helps turn these priorities into meaningful scientific progress.

 
HOW TO PARTICIPATE

Step 1
Register as an individual or create a team. Be sure to enter your T-shirt size and mailing address. (don't want a shirt, no problem, see below)

*Register by September 18 to help ensure your T-shirt arrives before Community Celebration Weekend.

Step 2
Choose your own challenge and complete it anytime during October.

Step 3
Invite your friends, family, coworkers, and neighbors to join your team or support your fundraiser.

Step 4
Share your photos and videos during Community Celebration Weekend (October 10–11) or anytime throughout October to inspire others around the world.

COMMUNITY AWARDS

🏆 Top Fundraiser

📱 Loudest Family or Team on Social Media

📸 Most Creative Bold Breakthroughs Photo

 
REGISTRATION INFORMATION

  • Adults: $30
  • Children (ages 2–18): $18

Each registration includes:

  • One commemorative Bold Breakthroughs event T-shirt*
  • One digital race bib

*Register by September 18 to help ensure your shirt arrives before Community Celebration Weekend.

Don't need another T-shirt? During registration, you can select "No T-shirt." The value of your shirt will stay with the Foundation to support OCNDS research.

name: Boo Run 5k & 10k
description:
The 2026 Boo Run Runners, we regret that we are cancelling the 2026 Boo Run. Health issues forced our hand and we can not manage an event of this size at this time. We intend to host a run next year and encourage you to register for the 2027 event.

 

 

Imagine Halloween Morning…

Families, runners, and walkers dressed in creative costumes, colorful decorations, music, laughter, and hundreds of people enjoying one of Porterville’s most beautiful outdoor spaces.

Join us on Saturday, October 31, 2026, for the Tule River Parkway Boo Run 5K & 10K! Whether you are a seasoned runner chasing a personal best, a casual walker, or a family looking for a fun Halloween activity, there is something for everyone.

Both races start and finish at Fallen Heroes Park in Porterville. The courses travel along the Tule River Parkway, a paved pedestrian and bicycle trail that follows the Tule River. The 5K features a shorter out-and-back course, while the 10K continues farther along the Parkway before returning to the park.

Costumes Encouraged

Come dressed as something spooky, silly, heroic, or completely original. Costumes are encouraged but not required. Please make sure your costume is safe for running or walking, does not block your vision, and does not create a tripping hazard for you or anyone around you.

Fallen Heroes Park offers restrooms, playgrounds, pavilions, picnic areas, and other amenities for participants and their families to enjoy before and after the race.

FREE BICYCLE HELMET GIVEAWAY

The Tulare County Association of Governments will be giving away bicycle helmets during the event while supplies last.
Supporting the Tule River Parkway

The Boo Run brings new visitors to the Tule River Parkway while promoting healthy lifestyles, outdoor recreation, and community spirit.

Most importantly, the Boo Run is the Tule River Parkway Association’s only annual fundraising event. Every registration helps support the Association’s work throughout the year.

About the Tule River Parkway Association

The Tule River Parkway Association is a local nonprofit organization dedicated to the restoration, protection, development, and public enjoyment of the Tule River corridor.

Working alongside the City of Porterville, the Association helps provide quality outdoor experiences for residents and visitors through:

  • The beautiful 2.7-mile pedestrian and bicycle trail connecting Fallen Heroes Park to the Highway 190/Highway 65 interchange
  • More than 32 California native plant gardens
  • Educational programs and volunteer opportunities
  • Ongoing improvements that make the Parkway a destination for recreation, nature, and community gatherings
  • Choose your distance, grab your costume, and join us for a frightfully fun Halloween morning on the Tule River Parkway!

description:
🎃 BOO-gie Glow Run
    Night Race SummerWeen Series

     July 25, 2026
🌙 5K • 10K • Half Marathon • 1 Miler • Doggie Glow Run
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803
🕓 Check-In & Registration: 5:00 PM
🏁 Start Times | Half: 5:30 PM | 5K & 10K: 7:30 PM | 1 Miler (Spooky Glow): 7:45 PM

 
💀 About the Event
Disco meets the dark side… and your dog’s invited. 🐾✨

Welcome to BOO-gie Night Run, part of our SummerWeen Series—where spooky season crashes into summer nights for one unforgettable beachside experience.

We’re talking glowing lights, eerie beats, costumed runners, and pups lighting up the course alongside their hoomans. Whether you’re chasing a PR, showing off your best spooky fit, or just vibing under the night sky, this is where fun, fitness, and a little chaos collide.

name: Boogie Nights 5K & 10K
description:
✨ Boogie Nights 5K & 10K After Dark

Join us for Boogie Nights 5K & 10K After Dark, a disco-drenched nighttime run through the Valley where polyester reigns, vibes are high, and everybody’s a star at the finish line.

Presented by Jed & Ted’s Excellent Races

Roller skates. Gold chains. Big dreams. Inspired by the unforgettable energy of Boogie Nights (yes, that Boogie Nights), this race is a tribute to the over-the-top sparkle and grit of 70s/80s California cool — with just enough late-night chaos to make it magic.

Choose your challenge:

  • Boogie Nights 5K – A funky little sprint with serious Dirk Diggler attitude
  • Boogie Nights 10K – Twice the disco, double the dazzle

Expect funk and soul on the speakers, throwback signage, and a crowd ready to dance their way to the finish. Costumes welcome. Big collars and roller flair encouraged.

This is a Jed & Ted’s Excellent Race — fun, fast, and full of heart.

Sign up now. You’ve got the touch. You’ve got the power.

 
🌀 Multiverse Option (Virtual Runners Welcome)
Can’t make it in person? No problem — we’re bringing the disco to your dimension.

Choose the Multiverse Option during registration and select your distance (5K or 10K).

Then:

  • Run anytime between June 27–30
  • Track it however you like (Strava, NRC, selfie — we’re chill)
  • Submit your proof and shipping info

We’ll send your medal straight from the Valley to your door

Same race. Same medal. Different timeline.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

🚨 Parody Disclaimer
This race is a fan-made parody event created with love by Jed & Ted’s Excellent Races. We are not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by any of the original creators, studios, or rights holders referenced in our race themes. All names, references, and characters are used for humorous and transformative purposes under fair use. We're just fans… who like to run in costume.

name: Bowman Run with the Bulls presented by Hotel Vista Sierra
description:
Join us for the annual Bowman Run with the Bulls 5K Run/Walk presented by Hotel Vista Sierra!
Lace up your shoes and be part of this fun community tradition that welcomes runners and walkers of all ages. The course winds through the heart of Auburn, The Endurance Capital of the World.

The race starts and finishes at Overlook Park, with all proceeds supporting Bowman Charter School programs, facilities and activities through Bowman PTO. 

🏅 Registration Details

  • $25 for kids (13 and under)
  • General registration is $30 through 10/16 and $35 10/17-11/14
  • $45 same-day registration
  • Free littles' 1/4-mile fun run (5 and under) sponsored by Auburn Clay Arts
  • Register by 10/23 to guarantee your T-shirt

🌟 Special recognition for Bowman families: Register for the race by 10/23 and include a $50 or more donation at checkout, and your family name will be proudly featured on the race T-shirt.

🏃‍♂️ Race Highlights

  • New start and finish location at Overlook Park, same course!
  • Race bibs and timing made possible by Hotel Vista Sierra
  • Packet pickup Friday before at Auburn Running Company
  • Finisher's medals provided to all kids, sponsored by Reliable Auto Glass
  • Water aid station and finish line fuel courtesy of Robinson Sand & Gravel
  • Professional digital race photos sponsored by Sacfit Ultra
  • Age-group prizes will be presented for both kids and adults

Come out and celebrate fitness, community, and school spirit -- Run with the Bulls!

This is an annual event organized by Bowman Charter PTO.

name: Brassfield Estate Winery's Whine Now, Wine Later Run
description:
Get ready to run, roam, and raise a glass at Brassfield Estate Winery, perched high above Lake County in the stunning High Valley AVA.

Choose your adventure, whether that's the 5K, 10K, or 10-mile, and hit trails that wind through picturesque vineyards, volcanic soils, and rolling hills, with incredible views of Mount Konocti and Round Mountain along the way.

Whether you're chasing a PR, tackling a new distance, or simply enjoying a beautiful day outside with friends, there's a trail waiting for you.

Every Race Entry Includes

  • A custom race hat
  • A scenic trail adventure
  • A finish-line celebration you won't want to miss
  • A glass of Brassfield wine (21+ with valid ID)

 

Race Day Schedule

8:00–9:30 AM: Bib Pickup & Check-In

10:00 AM: 10-Mile Race Start

10:15 AM: 10K Race Start

10:30 AM: 5K Race Start

12:00 PM: Music and pizza!

 

Cross the Finish Line & Let the Fun Begin!


The race ends at the finish line, but the party is just getting started.

Grab your wine, refuel with delicious food, and enjoy live music as you celebrate a day well spent on the trails. Bring your friends, soak in the views, and raise a glass to your accomplishment.

Fast feet, happy hearts, great wine. What more could you ask for?

Come for the run. Stay for the wine. Leave with a High Valley experience you won't forget.

 

A Quick Note

Please leave your pups at home, as no dogs are permitted at the event.

Course Maps

Course maps are below and may be subject to slight changes. The overall distance and difficulty of each course will stay the same.

name: Brazen New Year's Day
description:
The sun is rising on Friday morning, January 1st, the first day of 2027. Where should you be? Pounding the trails of Lake Chabot, of course!

Join us at Lake Chabot in Castro Valley for the scenic and invigorating 5K, 10K or half marathon.

Better yet, make sure you run at the Brazen New Year's Eve race and then you can start 2026 with the highly coveted New Year Mega Medal! Learn about our Brazen New Year's Eve race here.

Take it even one step higher by running both half marathons (one on 12/31 and one on 1/1) and then brag to your friends: "It took me two years to finish that marathon"!

name: Brian Waterbury Memorial Rock to Pier Run
description:
Run the Coast. Honor a Legacy. Experience the Central Coast at its Best!

Join us on Saturday, July 17, 2027, for the 57th annual Brian Waterbury Memorial Rock to Pier Fun Run and the 13th annual Rock’n Around the Pier Half Marathon, starting at 8:00 AM.

Set against the stunning backdrop of the Central Coast, both events begin at Morro Rock and take runners along the shoreline for an unforgettable beach-running experience.

Event Options
Rock to Pier Fun Run (6 miles)
Run from Morro Rock to the iconic Cayucos Pier, finishing right at the pier. This beach run is open to all ages and abilities—perfect for seasoned runners and first-timers alike.

Rock’n Around the Pier Half Marathon
A challenging and scenic out-and-back course starting at Morro Rock, heading to the Cayucos Pier, and returning south. At mile 10.5, runners will detour through Cloisters Park before finishing back at Morro Rock.
Course closes at 12:00 PM.

 

Rock to Pier Pre-Packet Pickup

Join us on Friday, July 16, from 3:00 PM to 7:00 PM at the Morro Bay Community Center for pre-packet pickup for the Rock to Pier Run & Half Marathon.

Participants are encouraged to pick up their race packet the day before the event to avoid race-day lines. Your packet will include your race bib, timing chip (if applicable), event information, and any participant giveaways.

Staff will be available throughout the afternoon and evening to assist with packet pickup and answer any last-minute questions. We look forward to seeing you and getting you ready for race day!

Race Day Details

Both events start at 8:00 AM

Water/Aid Stations throughout course!

Expect wet shoes—this is a true beach run!
Post-race breakfast and awards at Morro Rock
Bus transportation provided from Cayucos Pier back to Morro Rock for Rock to Pier participants
Parking is limited in Cayucos; ample parking available at Morro Rock (arrive early!)

Extras & Notes
Limited shirt sizes available (some sizes sold out)
Dogs are not allowed on the course due to Snowy Plover nesting season

Come celebrate tradition, community, and coastal beauty in one of California’s most unique running events. Whether you’re racing for a personal best or soaking in the scenery, this is a run you won’t forget!

name: Californian Dreamin 5K, 10K, & Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
Californian Dreamin’ 5K, 10K & Half Marathon

🌴 Date: Sunday, August 22, 2026
🌊 Location: Long Beach, CA

Dream big, run free, and soak up the California sunshine at the Californian Dreamin’ Run in Long Beach! With ocean views, a laid-back vibe, and a scenic coastal course, this event captures the heart of the Golden State in every step.

 

Event Highlights
☀️ Iconic Coastal Views: Experience the beauty of Long Beach’s beaches, palm trees, and breezy ocean paths.
🏅 Finisher Medals: Finish strong and take home a medal inspired by the California lifestyle.
🎉 Positive Vibes: Run to the rhythm of good vibes, great music, and an encouraging community.
👟 Distances for All Levels: Choose from 5K, 10K, or Half Marathon—perfect for new runners and seasoned athletes alike.

name: CASA Superhero Run
description:
Get ready to unleash your inner superhero at the CASA Superhero Run on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the Park at Riverwalk! Whether you're a seasoned runner or just looking for a fun, family-friendly event, this race is for you.

Join fellow heroes and villains as we run, walk, and fly in support of children in foster care. Choose from a 2K, 5K, or 10K. The 5K and 10K races are officially timed, perfect for runners aiming for a personal best, while the 2K is an untimed fun run for those who want to enjoy the excitement at their own pace.

🗓 Race Day Schedule – Saturday, October 24th
📍 Location: The Park at River Walk

7:15 AM – Registration Opens
8:15 AM – 10K Race Start
8:30 AM – 5K Race Start 
8:45 AM – 2K Kids & Family Fun Run Begins
10:00 AM – Raffle Prize Winners & Awards Ceremony (time subject to change)

🎭 Costume Contest – Show off your best superhero or villain look!
🎟 Raffle Prizes – Enter for a chance to win exciting prizes!
🛍 Local Vendors & Food – Explore delicious eats and fun activities for the whole family.

Every participant receives (while supplies last):
🏅 A one-of-a-kind CASA Superhero Medal
👕 An exclusive race t-shirt
🎒 A swag bag full of goodies

✨ Capes are available for purchase, so suit up and get ready to save the day!

Why run? Because every child deserves a hero, but children in foster care need a SUPERHERO. Your participation supports CASA’s mission to advocate for children who need a voice.

Register today and be a hero for kids in Kern County! 🚀💥

name: Catalina Island Half-Marathon & 10K
description:
Experience the ultimate California trail half-marathon, an adventure that will test your limits while rewarding you with awe-inspiring beauty. Starting in the charming town of Avalon, the race kicks off with a scenic run past the historic Wrigley Mansion. From there, you’ll journey into Catalina Island’s rugged Interior, tackling challenging climbs that lead to breathtaking peaks.

At the summit, take in sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean, where, on a clear day, you might catch a glimpse of two other Channel Islands. The journey continues with a thrilling descent through the serene Wrigley Memorial, winding your way back into the heart of Avalon.

For runners looking for a shorter, yet equally stunning course, the 10K route offers a picturesque tour through Avalon’s scenic hillsides, capturing the island’s unique charm and natural beauty. Whether you’re taking on the half-marathon or the 10K, this race is a perfect blend of challenge, adventure, and unforgettable views.

name: Cerro Gordo Silver Run 2027
description:
Saturday, May 29, 2027 | Start: 7:00 AM | Check-in by 6:00 AM
8 miles | 4,600 ft of vertical gain | Keeler, CA → Cerro Gordo

(Camping & lodging info at the bottom)

Watch the 2026 recap video for a feel of what you're signing up for.

----

OUR 5TH ANNUAL RUN — COME CELEBRATE WITH US

Are you tough enough to race up a mountain road built for mule trains and silver barons?

Join us for a legendary race in the Eastern Sierra — an 8-mile uphill battle climbing 4,600 vertical feet to the historic ghost town of Cerro Gordo, once the richest silver mine in California.

This is not your average run. This is a gut-check. A pilgrimage. A challenge against time, gravity, and yourself.

The infamous Cerro Gordo Road was carved out in 1865 to shuttle silver down from the mountains. Now, once a year, runners race back up — chasing glory, chasing ghosts, and chasing history.

What happens at the top

When you summit the town, the day's just beginning. Cross the finish line and celebrate with:

— A giant mountaintop BBQ with mains, sides, and drinks
— Live music and games
— Self-guided exploration of the abandoned town
— A well-earned sense of triumph

What's included with your entry

— Aid stations every mile, stocked with fuel and encouragement
— A limited-edition Silver Run 2027 shirt and finisher's medal
— Mountaintop BBQ (mains, sides, drinks)
— Shuttle vans for the ride back down
— Eternal bragging rights — the winner's name is engraved in silver and enshrined in Cerro Gordo's history

The bar to beat

2026 winning time: 1:18:26 by Garrett Patrick. Think you've got what it takes?

See the full 2026 results: https://my.raceresult.com/401628/

For everyone, not just the fastest

There's no time limit. Whether you finish in 1 hour or 5, this mountain has room for all. We've had teenagers run alongside their parents. We've had two 82-year-olds cross the finish line in the same year. All are welcome — as long as you're willing to dig deep and climb.

----

Camping & Lodging

Keeler camping (closest & cheapest): Our neighbor offers camping spots in Keeler, CA, less than a quarter mile from the starting line, for $20/spot. Restrooms available on site.

Lone Pine, CA (15 miles away): A wide range of hotels, motels, and RV parks.

BLM land (free): Plenty of BLM land in the area allows free camping for up to 14 days. Google "BLM camping Owens Valley" for options.

Parking: Multiple lots in Keeler will be available the morning of the race. Volunteers will direct you on arrival. After the race, shuttle buses will bring you back down to your car.

Spectators

Bring your family and friends. For 2027, spectators ride up the mountain in our shuttle vans before the race begins to cheer runners across the finish line. Spectator passes are $30 and include the shuttle ride up and the mountaintop BBQ.

name: Champion Mine Trail Race
description:
Challenge Yourself and Enjoy the Great Outdoors

Join the Sierra TrailBlazers Running Club and Bear Yuba Land Trust for the 2nd annual Champion Mine Trail Race! Money raised through the races, besides supporting a great race, will be used to support more trails in Nevada County and the Mines to Pines trail work.

Get ready to travel to a must-see destination race in Northern California. Explore some of Nevada City’s most exciting trails with this challenging half-marathon (13.1 miles) event. The course winds through towering pines, crosses a historic swinging bridge, and challenges runners with a series of rewarding climbs. With multiple aid stations, historical landmarks, and a newly constructed trail section offering varied terrain, this course rivals some of the best trail races in Northern California.

Runners will enjoy breathtaking views along the Tribute Trail and Deer Creek, combined with a beautiful variety of landscapes throughout the race. Best of all, the adventure begins right on Nevada City’s historic Broad Street — a truly unforgettable starting line!

The Champion Mine Trail Run offers a dynamic mix of pavement, gravel, and single-track trails, making it a must-do event for any trail enthusiast.

There will also be a 5K and new this year, a 10K! A 5K too short for you and a 1/2 marathon just sounds painful, then please consider the 10K. You won't be disappointed. 

Money raised with the race will be donated towards the Mines to Pines Trail development so everyone in Nevada County can enjoy the trail from Nevada City to Truckee. Please help us raise even more towards the trail's development. 

Sierra TrailBlazer's also sponsor a scholarship to a graduating senior in the Nevada Joint Union District that desires to continue to college and pursue their studies and running.

Runners will enjoy breathtaking views along the Tribute Trail and Deer Creek, combined with a beautiful variety of landscapes throughout the race. Best of all, the adventure begins right on Nevada City’s historic Broad Street — a truly unforgettable starting line!

The Champion Mine Trail Run offers a dynamic mix of pavement, gravel, and single-track trails, making it a must-do event for any trail enthusiast.

There will also be a 5K and new this year, a 10K! A 5K too short for you and a 1/2 marathon just sounds painful, then please consider the 10K. You won't be disappointed. 

Money raised with the race will be donated towards the Mines to Pines Trail development so everyone in Nevada County can enjoy the trail from Nevada City to Truckee. Please help us raise even more towards the trail's development. 

Sierra TrailBlazer's also sponsor a scholarship to a graduating senior in the Nevada Joint Union District that desires to continue to college and pursue their studies and running.

name: CHAOS-  HYBRID 5K CHALLENGE
description:
🔥 BEAST MODE — HYBRID 5K CHALLENGE


Saturday, November 6, 2027 | Long Beach, CA

 Challenge combines a 5K run with four fitness challenges designed to test your strength, endurance, and determination. Run your 5K, enter the Hybrid Zone, complete all four challenges, then earn your way across the finish line.

 

📍 Location: 5400 E. Ocean Blvd., Long Beach, CA 90803
⏰ Event Start: 8:00 AM

🏃 THE CHALLENGE
Complete the 5K run first, then enter the Hybrid Zone:

JUMP — 80m Burpee Broad Jumps
Chest to the ground. Get up. Broad jump forward. Repeat for 80 meters.

LUNGE — 100m Walking Lunges
Keep moving forward through the entire marked 100-meter zone.

CARRY — 100m Sandbag Carry
Pick it up and carry it through the complete 100-meter course.

SQUAT — 100 Bodyweight Squats
No equipment. Just you and 100 squats between you and the finish.

Then you're released to the FINISH LINE. 🏁

5K. FOUR CHALLENGES. ONE FINISH.
You don't have to be an elite athlete. You don't have to be the fastest runner. You just have to be willing to work.

Run. Jump. Lunge. Carry. Squat. Finish.

 🔥

name: Chasing Santa – 5K, 10K, 10-Miler, Half Marathon
description:
Santa’s on the move and it’s your turn to chase him down the Long Beach coast. Chasing Santa is all about festive miles, holiday spirit, and a little seasonal mischief by the sea. Whether you’re jogging, walking, or just soaking up the holiday cheer, this run is the perfect way to start the season with miles, smiles, and a touch of Santa magic.

Details

Start Location: Alamitos Beach, 780 E Shoreline Dr Long Beach, CA
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

Saturday
1:00-3:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event & post-race)

Sunday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens at the start
7:00am – Half marathon and 10-miler start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half)
Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged in advance for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out & Back Course

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More About the Course

This is an out and back course, meaning you will begin and finish in the same location.

Our courses are not closed, which means that there are often runners, walkers, and others enjoying the day along with you. Safety is must and all runners must stay on the right side (pedestrian side) of the beach path. The course never goes off the beach path.

On-course support: Courses are well marked with two water stations and restrooms along the way. Turns will be clearly marked with chalk, a sign that says runner turn, and a flag.

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Medals: All finishers earn a race medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

description:
It's that time of year to run down shaded Christmas Tree Lane… in JULY! 
Experience one of Fresno’s most iconic routes in a whole new way. This festive 5K follows the same beloved course as the Jingle Bell Run, starting and finishing near Palm & Van Ness... only this time, we’re bringing the holiday magic to summer!

👟 Special Rate: Children 9 and under automatically receive discounted entry during registration, making this a perfect family event!
