name: Long Beach Labor Day Run - Labor of Love 5K, 10K,  Kids Dash
description:
💛 Labor of Love – Merging Forces 5K, 10K & Kids Dash


📅 Labor Day — Monday, September 6, 2026
📍 Shoreline Aquatic Park / Shoreline Village
200 Aquarium Way, Long Beach, CA 90802

Celebrate Labor Day on the Long Beach waterfront with a morning of running, walking, music, community, and purpose!

The inaugural Labor of Love – Merging Forces Run starts near the iconic lighthouse at Shoreline Village and takes participants through one of the most beautiful areas of Long Beach before heading onto the scenic beach path.

With waterfront views, professional chip timing, custom race swag, free photos, music, vendors, awards, and plenty of CaliFlow energy at the finish line, this is more than just a run — it's a Labor Day morning you'll remember.

Participant Parking in Parking Structure

⏰ RACE DAY SCHEDULE

Same Day Registration- Bib Pick Up Opens 6:30 AM
5K & 10K Start — 8:00 AM

Age Group Medal Pickup — Beginning at 9:00 AM

Kids Dash — 9:15 AM

Overall Awards Ceremony — 9:30 AM

 

✨ WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT
✔️ Professional ChronoTrack Chip Timing
✔️ Instant Race Results available within minutes of finishing
✔️ Custom Finisher Medal
✔️ Custom Race Shirt
✔️ Winner Trophies - Top 3 Male and Female Each Distance ( Gun Time)
✔️ Age Group Awards- Based on Chip Time
✔️ FREE Race Day Photos
✔️ Multiple On-Course Water Stations
✔️ Flat, Fast & Scenic Course
✔️ Beautiful Long Beach Waterfront Views
✔️ DJ, Music & Finish-Line Energy
✔️ Vendors & Community Partners
✔️ Kids Dash
✔️ Walkers Welcome
✔️ Stroller Friendly
✔️ Dog Friendly
✔️ Beginner Friendly
✔️ PR Chasers Welcome

Whether you're racing for a new PR, walking your first 5K, bringing the whole family, or simply looking for a fun way to kick off Labor Day, there's a place for you at our Start Line.

🌊 A BEAUTIFUL LONG BEACH COURSE
Enjoy a scenic waterfront course featuring the energy of Shoreline Village and the Long Beach waterfront before heading onto the paved beach running and walking path.

The course is designed to be flat, fast, and approachable for all abilities.

This is an open course, meaning the beach path remains open to the public during the event. Please be courteous and aware of other runners, walkers, cyclists, and beach-path users.

Course markings, turnaround signs, flags, and race staff will be positioned along the route to help keep you on course.

📸 FREE RACE PHOTOS
Yes — FREE!

Our photographers will be out capturing the morning, and race photos are included with your registration. We want you to leave with more than a finish time.

A race experience designed to give you memories and photos — not just a finish time.

Smile when you see the camera. 😎📸

🎉 STAY FOR THE FINISH-LINE FUN
Don't disappear the second you cross the finish line!

Celebrate your finish, take photos, cheer on other runners, visit our vendors and community partners, enjoy the music, and soak up the waterfront atmosphere.

Friends and family are welcome to come cheer you on and be part of the morning.

👟 RUN WITH PURPOSE
This special event is proudly hosted in partnership with Merge Opportunities, a nonprofit dedicated to creating pathways for underserved youth, system-impacted individuals, and transitioning foster youth.

Through job training, mentorship, and essential support services, Merge empowers individuals to rebuild, reconnect, and move forward with purpose.

Your miles are helping us bring people together while supporting meaningful work in our community.

💛 Run with meaning.
💛 Move with purpose.
💛 Be part of something bigger.

Come help us launch a brand-new Long Beach Labor Day tradition where community, impact, movement, and good energy come together.

Come for the run. Stay for the vibe. Run for a reason.

 

🏆 IMPORTANT AWARDS INFORMATION
Overall Awards
Trophies are awarded to the Top 3 Overall Male and Top 3 Overall Female finishers in the 5K and 10K. Overall placement is determined by gun time.


Age Group Awards
Age Group medals are awarded in 10-year age divisions and are determined by chip time. Age Group winners do not need to wait for the Overall Awards Ceremony. Beginning at 9:00 AM, check your results and pick up your medal at the Results Kiosk.

The awards ceremony is for Overall Winners only.


You must be present to receive an award.
Awards must be picked up during the event. No awards will be distributed or mailed after the event. No exceptions. Please check your results before leaving if you believe you may have placed Overall or in your Age Group.

name: Long Beach Mother's Day Bloom & Zoom 5K, 10K, Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🌸 Bloom & Zoom
Long Beach Mother’s Day Run
5K • 10K • Half Marathon
📅 Sunday, May 9, 2027
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA

 
💐 Event Description
This Mother's Day, trade the brunch table for the finish line and celebrate with miles that bloom!
The Long Beach Mother's Day Run – Bloom & Zoom honors moms, caregivers, and all who uplift us—with ocean views, finish-line flowers, and CaliFlow’s signature energy. Whether you’re running hard or walking easy, this day is about movement, memories, and love.

🌸 Flower Bar at the Finish
Create your own mini bouquet—a little something beautiful to take home 💐

Perfect for:

💖 First-time walkers
👟 Runners chasing PRs
👩‍👧 Stroller moms & multi-gen families
🌼 Anyone who wants to show up with heart
 
🌺 Race Highlights
⏱ Professionally chip-timed
📸 Free downloadable race photos
🏅 Finisher medals for everyone
🏆 Overall & age group awards
🎭 Mother’s Day outfit contest (prizes for best florals, matching duo, and family group!) Details Below
🌊 Scenic, flat out-and-back course along the beach path - Stroller Friendly, Dog Friendly
🥤 Water stations & restrooms on course
🎶 Finish-line celebration with music, snacks & photo ops
 
💞 Beginner- & Walker-Friendly!
Whether you're walking your first 5K or strolling with your little one, you're welcome here.
There’s no pressure, no judgment—just good vibes and plenty of encouragement.
We’ll cheer you across that finish line like a hero, no matter your pace.

 
🧡 Why CaliFlow Runs?
We believe races should be inclusive, affordable, and fun. With over 50 events a year, we create high-vibe spaces where everyone feels like they belong. No outrageous prices, no boring courses—just real community and real finish-line joy. 🌊

 
👟 Who Can Participate?
Everyone!
🏃 Runners | 🚶 Walkers | 👶 Strollers | 🐾 Supportive friends
All ages. All paces. All love.

 
⏰ Bib Pick-Up & Start Times
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803
🕕 Bib Pick-Up: 6:15 AM – 8:00 AM
🏃‍♀️ Half Marathon Start: 7:00 AM
🏃 5K & 10K Start: 8:00 AM

🏃‍♀️ 1 Miler Start: 8:15 AM

🏃‍♀️. Kids 400 Yard Dash: 9:00 AM - (Kids Medals and Goodie Bags for Kiddos Ages 2 to 7)

 
🚗 Parking Info
Street parking available (check signs!).
Beach lot parking is $2.00/hr (via app or kiosk). Plenty of parking steps from the finish/start Line
Arrive early for best spots near the start.

 
🏅 Medals & Awards
🌼 Custom Bloom & Zoom Mother’s Day Finisher Medal for all
🏆 Overall & Age Group Awards

💡 If it’s not CaliFlow… it’s just another average race.

name: Long Beach Race for Rare 5K Run & Walk Event
description:
Join the National MPS Society at the 5th Annual Long Beach Race for Rare 5K Run & Walk Event hosted by Long Beach locals, Lynn and Scott Hopkins!

This event is to raise money and awareness to help change the lives of those living with a rare disease.  10% of Americans suffer from a rare disease and less than 5% have an FDA-approved treatment.  3 out of 10 children with a rare condition do not live to see their 5th birthday, and we work to change this.  Proceeds benefit the National MPS Society.

Race Details

7:30 AM: Onsite registration, packet pick-up, and pre-race entertainment
9:00 AM: 5K Run/Walk
10:00 AM: Awards/Raffle
10:30 AM: Beachside Picnic

Lunch is included in registration costs. Come out and enjoy a fun day to help raise awareness and funds for our MPS and ML families!

Start your Team Fundraiser!

At the top, hover over "Donate"
Select "become a fundraiser"
Create your team page - Choose your photo, team name, bio and fundraising goal!
Share the link for people to donate directly to your fundraiser!
You can do this before or after you register

Not able to join in person? Participate virtually!

It is just like any other 5K, except there is no official race location.  You get to choose where, with whom, and even how you want to complete the 5K.  by participating virtually, you can run the 5K at any time leading up to October 10th.  It can even be done in increments, keep track of your distance until you hit the 5K!

Contact Bethany Greene at bethany@mpssociety.org for sponsorship details.

In-person and virtual runners: Shirts are available on a first-come, first-served basis when you register!

Your Gift Makes a Difference

The National MPS Society is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization (FEIN: 11-2734849). Donations made in addition to race registration are tax-deductible to the extent permitted by law. Race registration fees are not considered tax-deductible charitable contributions.

All proceeds from the Long Beach Race for Rare support the mission of the National MPS Society.

name: Lookin' for a Cure Palo Alto
description:
Description

Join Us in the Pursuit of a Cure at the Lookin' For A Cure Palo Alto 5K!


Every year, Lookin' For A Cure 5k events light up cities across the United States. These events are not just about running, they are about igniting awareness, and unity in the fight against Ocular Melanoma. By participating, you're not only support groundbreaking research but also bringing together individuals affected by Ocular Melanoma.We are Lookin' For a Cure" in Palo Alto. Join A Cure in Sight on Saturday July 10th, 7AM-11AM at: 2452 Watson Ct. Palo Alto, CA US 94020. Help raise awareness and support the fight against Ocular Melanoma, the most common eye cancer in adults in the United States.  

A Partnership for Progress


A Cure In Sight collaborates with leading research facilities and dedicated physicians that specialize in Ocular Melanoma treatment. Together, we channel the net proceeds from these events into ongoing research projects and patient support programs. Your involvement directly contributes to advancing the quest for a cure. Walk shoulder-to-shoulder with Ocular Melanoma survivors, their families, and the medical professionals who care for them at the Byers Eye Institute at Stanford University School of Medicine. 

All ages are welcome to attend. Come run, walk, or stay in one place and play games at the Fourth Annual Lookin' for a Cure 5K at Stanford, hosted by A Cure in Sight and the Byers Eye Institute at Stanford.  Set up your team, invite your friends and family, start your fundraiser and you are off to the finish line. Proceeds from this event will support the Stanford Ocular Oncology Program. Stanford is a national leader in providing state-of-the-art care for ocular melanoma patients of all ages and has pioneered groundbreaking research advances. Prithvi Mruthyunjaya, MD, MHS, professor of ophthalmology who anchors the ocular tumor service at Stanford is also working hard at Stanford to bring this event to fruition.

The race also aims to spread the word about the importance of early detection by getting regular dilated eye exams. Ocular melanoma makes up approximately 5 percent of melanomas in the United States. It is estimated that between 6-8 people per million will be diagnosed annually in the Western world. 

Read more about the work Stanford is doing around ocular melanoma here.

Event Details

Packet pick up will be held at Road Runner Sports San Carlos located at: 1125 Industrial Rd, San Carlos, CA 94070 on July 9, 2026 from 4-6pm. 

Race Swag

  • Guaranteed T-shirt, If Registered by June 27th.
  • Finisher Medal
  • Food & Drink
  • Course Aid Station
  • Commemorative Race Bib
  • Free Downloadable Photos
  • Official Finishers Time With Age Group Placements

Race day schedule

  • Registration 7 AM
  • Race start 8 AM
  • Announcements Awards 9:30 am

Free parking is available in the Byers Eye Institute parking lot on the corner of Embarcadero Rd. and Bayshore Rd.

Description

Join Us in the Pursuit of a Cure at the Lookin' For A Cure Palo Alto 5K!


Every year, Lookin' For A Cure 5k events light up cities across the United States. These events are not just about running, they are about igniting awareness, and unity in the fight against Ocular Melanoma. By participating, you're not only support groundbreaking research but also bringing together individuals affected by Ocular Melanoma.We are Lookin' For a Cure" in Palo Alto. Join A Cure in Sight on Saturday July 10th, 7AM-11AM at: 2452 Watson Ct. Palo Alto, CA US 94020. Help raise awareness and support the fight against Ocular Melanoma, the most common eye cancer in adults in the United States.  

A Partnership for Progress


A Cure In Sight collaborates with leading research facilities and dedicated physicians that specialize in Ocular Melanoma treatment. Together, we channel the net proceeds from these events into ongoing research projects and patient support programs. Your involvement directly contributes to advancing the quest for a cure. Walk shoulder-to-shoulder with Ocular Melanoma survivors, their families, and the medical professionals who care for them at the Byers Eye Institute at Stanford University School of Medicine. 

All ages are welcome to attend. Come run, walk, or stay in one place and play games at the Fourth Annual Lookin' for a Cure 5K at Stanford, hosted by A Cure in Sight and the Byers Eye Institute at Stanford.  Set up your team, invite your friends and family, start your fundraiser and you are off to the finish line. Proceeds from this event will support the Stanford Ocular Oncology Program. Stanford is a national leader in providing state-of-the-art care for ocular melanoma patients of all ages and has pioneered groundbreaking research advances. Prithvi Mruthyunjaya, MD, MHS, professor of ophthalmology who anchors the ocular tumor service at Stanford is also working hard at Stanford to bring this event to fruition.

The race also aims to spread the word about the importance of early detection by getting regular dilated eye exams. Ocular melanoma makes up approximately 5 percent of melanomas in the United States. It is estimated that between 6-8 people per million will be diagnosed annually in the Western world. 

Read more about the work Stanford is doing around ocular melanoma here.

Event Details

Packet pick up will be held at Road Runner Sports San Carlos located at: 1125 Industrial Rd, San Carlos, CA 94070 on July 9, 2026 from 4-6pm. 

Race Swag

  • Guaranteed T-shirt, If Registered by June 27th.
  • Finisher Medal
  • Food & Drink
  • Course Aid Station
  • Commemorative Race Bib
  • Free Downloadable Photos
  • Official Finishers Time With Age Group Placements

Race day schedule

  • Registration 7 AM
  • Race start 8 AM
  • Announcements Awards 9:30 am

Free parking is available in the Byers Eye Institute parking lot on the corner of Embarcadero Rd. and Bayshore Rd.

name: Louis Duarte's Breast Cancer Awareness 5k
description:
Join us for the Louis Duarte Breast Cancer Awareness 5K at Hart Park! Whether you’re an experienced runner, a casual jogger, or simply looking to support a meaningful cause, this event is for you.

What Your Registration Includes

Your registration includes an official Louis Duarte Breast Cancer Awareness 5K performance T-shirt, a custom finisher medal, a complimentary Bentley Bowl meal, refreshments, event swag and giveaways, a race bib, and access to all post-race festivities, sponsor booths, music, and community activities. Every participant will receive an unforgettable race-day experience while helping support an important cause.

The scenic 5K course begins at Hart Park and winds through the beautiful park grounds and trails, offering participants a fun, family-friendly, and memorable race experience. After crossing the finish line, stick around to enjoy delicious food, refreshments, sponsor booths, music, giveaways, and the opportunity to connect with fellow participants while celebrating a great morning together.

This event is dedicated to raising awareness and supporting the fight against breast cancer. Every registration helps make a difference while bringing our community together to honor survivors, remember loved ones, and support those currently battling breast cancer.

Whether you choose to run, walk, or cheer from the sidelines, all fitness levels are welcome. We can’t wait to see you on October 10 as we come together for an incredible cause. Thank you for supporting the Louis Duarte Breast Cancer Awareness 5K we look forward to seeing you at the starting line!

name: Love Your Park Run & Walk Fundraiser
description:
❤️ Join us for a community celebration that brings neighbors together for a great cause!

The Love Your Park Walk & Run Fundraiser supports the North of the River Recreation Foundation's Youth Scholarship Fund. Every step you take helps local children and families access recreation programs, sports, and camps that build confidence, connection, and lifelong memories.

Whether you're running the 5K or 10K, walking the Fun Run, or cheering from the sidelines, this event is all about loving our parks, loving our hearts, and investing in the community spaces that bring us together.

👟 Fun Run – Perfect for beginners, walkers, families, and children.

🏃 5K – A great challenge for runners and walkers looking to go the distance.

💪 10K – Take on an extended course and challenge yourself while supporting a great cause.

Please note: The Fun Run takes place entirely within Polo Community Park. The 5K and 10K routes extend beyond the park into the surrounding neighborhoods and through Almondale Park.

🔗  Learn more about the Foundation.

Get ready for the 3RD Annual Lucha Run—a lively, family-friendly event to finish the year with a bang! Bring your best "luchador/a" costume and join us for either a 6K run or a 3K (2-mile) walk. It’s a celebration of fitness, fun, and flavor for all ages! NEW FOR 2025: OUR EVENT WILL TAKE PLACE AT FRESNO CITY COLLEGE AS WE'LL HAVE A REAL "LUCHA LIBRE" WRESTLING MATCH AT THE END OF THE EVENT! 

  • Fun and Festive Atmosphere: Show off your best lucha-inspired costumes, and bring your friends and family to cheer you on.
  • Post-Race Fiesta: Celebrate at the finish line with delicious tacos, hot chocolate, and "pan dulce" waiting to refuel you.
  • Support Local Fitness: As with all Reyes Racing events, this run brings the community together to stay active and celebrate the joy of movement.

WE HAVE ADDED A 2 MILE SPEED WALK! TOP 5 MALE/FEMALE GET AWARDS! 

A FEW REASONS TO JOIN OUR EVENT!

  • DRI FIT LONG SLEEVE SHIRTS!
  • Unique MEDAL
  • TACOS
  • HOT CHOCOLATE
  •  "PAN DULCE"
  • REAL LUCHA EVENT AFTER THE EVENT!! NEW FOR 2025!
  • $100 CASH to top male/female!
  • $200 CASH to team with most participants!
  • $200 CASH to the fastest team (top 5 runners in your team count for scoring)
  • UNIQUE COFFEE MUGS FOR TOP 10 MALE/FEMALE OVERALL!
  • Unique AGE GROUP AWARDS
  • ATHENA/CLYDESDALE age group divisions
  • BEST COSTUME competition
  • GREAT RUNNING COURSE, FLAT AT FRESNO CITY COLLEGE CAMPUS!
  • KIDS RACES
  • FUN, MUSIC!

SAT, DEC 5TH, 3:00-5:00PM @ FLEET FEET STORE

SUN, DEC 6TH, 7:45-8:45AM @ FRESNO CITY COLLEGE (Veterans Peace Memorial Area)

RACE DAY SCHEDULE:

8:45AM- KIDS RACES

9:00AM- 6K/2 MILE

10:30AM- AWARDS

11:00AM- LIVE LUCHA LIBRE!!! (FREE EVENT FOR ALL PARTICIPANTS. NON PARTICIPANTS/PUBLIC CAN BUY A TICKET FOR THE LUCHA LIBRE EVENT. $20 ADULTS, $10 KIDS. TICKEST CAN BE BOUGHT ONLINE OR AT THE DOOR AT THE EVENT)

name: Martha's Village & Kitchen 20th Annual Thanksgiving Day 5K
description:
The Martha’s Village & Kitchen Thanksgiving Day 5K is an annual, family friendly run and walk held in Palm Desert, California and this year we are celebrating 20 years of giving back!

This beloved Thanksgiving tradition brings more than 5,000 participants, spectators, and volunteers together to raise awareness and critical funds in support of Martha’s Village & Kitchen and our mission to end hunger and homelessness in the Coachella Valley.

Race day is a full celebration featuring a live DJ and stage, trophy presentations, and a high energy finish line experience. Register as an individual, start a team, or join an existing team and get ready to run or walk for a cause!

Do not forget to capture the moment! Share your race day photos and videos and tag @MarthasVillage or use #MVK5K on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok!

name: Mash + Dash – 5K, 10K, 10-Miler, Half Marathon
description:
Still full? Perfect. Mash & Dash is here to help you run off that mountain of mashed potatoes with a morning of coastal miles and post-feast fun. It’s the perfect way to keep the holiday vibes rolling while giving those leftovers a little competition. Whether you’re out to burn off pie slices or just want an easy cruise by the water, this run is all about laughter, movement, and shaking off that Thanksgiving food coma.

Race Details

Start Location: Alamitos Beach, 780 E Shoreline Dr. Long Beach, CA
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

Friday
1:00-4:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event & post-race)

Saturday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens at the start
7:00am – Half marathon and 10-miler start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged in advance for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Course

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More About the Course

This is an out and back course, meaning you will begin and finish in the same location.

Our courses are not closed, which means that there are often runners, walkers, and others enjoying the day along with you. Safety is must and all runners must stay on the right side (pedestrian side) of the beach path. The course never goes off the beach path.

On-course support: Courses are well marked with two water stations and restrooms along the way. Turns will be clearly marked with chalk, a sign that says runner turn, and a flag.

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Medals: All runners earn a finishing medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance.
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, the San Fernando Valley, Orange County, and San Diego. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

name: Matcha for Miles
description:
Spring energy. Good movement. Matcha magic! This is your feel-good run to start the season right.

Matcha for Miles is our newest Spring wellness event— a blend of community-powered energy and feel-good miles. Think: your favorite Saturday morning routine, but leveled up with DJ beats, friends, and a whole community moving together.

Whether you’re an elite runner, not-so-elite runner, stroller-pushing hero, or maybe you're in need of a hot-girl walk (yes diva!)… this morning is for you!

name: MAYEM -  HYBRID 5K CHALLENGE
description:
🔥 BEAST MODE — HYBRID 5K CHALLENGE

 

Sunday, August 1
 | Long Beach, CA

 

MAYEM Hybrid 5K Challenge combines a 5K run with four fitness challenges designed to test your strength, endurance, and determination. Run your 5K, enter the Hybrid Zone, complete all four challenges, then earn your way across the finish line.

📍 Location: 5400 E. Ocean Blvd., Long Beach, CA 90803
⏰ Event Start: 8:00 AM

🏃 THE CHALLENGE
Complete the 5K run first, then enter the Hybrid Zone:

JUMP — 80m Burpee Broad Jumps
Chest to the ground. Get up. Broad jump forward. Repeat for 80 meters.

LUNGE — 100m Walking Lunges
Keep moving forward through the entire marked 100-meter zone.

CARRY — 100m Sandbag Carry
Pick it up and carry it through the complete 100-meter course.

SQUAT — 100 Bodyweight Squats
No equipment. Just you and 100 squats between you and the finish.

Then you're released to the FINISH LINE. 🏁

5K. FOUR CHALLENGES. ONE FINISH.
You don't have to be an elite athlete. You don't have to be the fastest runner. You just have to be willing to work.

Run. Jump. Lunge. Carry. Squat. Finish.

 🔥

description:

Celebrate Memorial Day the right way — by running! The Memorial Day 5K, 10K & Kids 1 Mile Run is one of Hemet, CA's most beloved annual running events, held near the stunning Diamond Valley Lake. Whether you're chasing a new personal record or lacing up for the first time, this flat, fast, out-and-back course is designed for every runner and walker.

👕 Premium race experience — custom finisher's medals, well-designed race bibs, and technical fabric shirts for men and women
🍷 Scenic location — just 10 minutes from Southern California's top wineries
🛍️ Prime area — close to Old Town Temecula and the region's premier shopping mall
❤️ Locally owned & locally produced — a true community race built by and for the Hemet/Temecula Valley

Every registered participant receives:

name: Menlo Park Back-to-School Kids Triathlon
description:
The Menlo Park Back to School Kids Triathlon is the perfect way for kids ages 4–17 to kick off the new school year with confidence, energy, and fun!

Whether it’s their first triathlon or they’re returning to set a new personal best, participants will enjoy an exciting race featuring swimming, biking, and running in a safe, supportive, and family-friendly environment at Burgess Park.

name: Menlo Park Kids Triathlon
description: The Menlo Park Kids Triathlon (“MPKT”) is a triathlon specifically for kids ages from 4 to 17 years old. A triathlon is a race that consists of a combination of three sports: swimming, cycling, and running. The kids start the race with swimming at the Burgess Pool in waves (triathlon speak for groups) of 20 to 25  kids. From the swim, they run to the transition area to put on their helmets, shoes, and anything else they need. They then mount their bikes and head out to the bike course. When the kids are done with the bike, they head back to transition to put their bike away, and head to run round Burgess Park. They finish the race in the park by crossing through the finishing chute!

name: Merry Miles-  5K, 10K,  and Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🎅 Merry Miles 5K. 10K. Half Marathon
📅 Saturday, December 6, 2026
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd Long Beach, CA 90803

 

This festive coastal run is all about holiday spirit, good vibes, and giving back — plus, we’re collecting donations for the Long Beach Animal Shelter to help local pets in need. 🐾
Bring a toy, treat, blanket, or bag of food from their wish list (posted at check-in) and help spread pawsitive cheer to our four-legged friends waiting for their forever homes.

 
🏃‍♀️ Event Highlights
✨ Professional chip timing on a flat, fast course
📸 Elfie Stations & finish-line photo ops galore
🏅  Finsher Medals for All - Overall and Age Group Awards
🎅 Costumes encouraged! Dress festive, funny, or fabulously extra 

🎅 Costume Contest with Prizes
🍪 Holiday treats & hot cocoa at the finish-line festival
🎶 DJ Claus spinning holiday remixes all morning

 
🕒 Schedule of Events
Bib Pick-Up: 6:00 AM – 8:00 AM at the Race Ready Athletics Tent
Half Marathon Start: 7:00 AM
5K & 10K Start: 8:00 AM
🏆 Awards: 9:30 AM

All finishers receive a medal, free race-day photos, and yummy holiday snacks — whether you’ve been naughty, nice, or somewhere in between.

 
💝 Why We Run
Because giving back feels even better than crossing the finish line.
Your donations to the Long Beach Animal Shelter help keep rescue pets warm, fed, and full of holiday hope. Every mile = a tail wag of gratitude. 🐾

 
💬 Why CaliFlow Runs
CaliFlow Runs creates inclusive, affordable, and high-vibe races that bring runners and walkers of all paces together. We keep it low-key, coastal, and full of good energy — because fitness and fun should always go hand in hand.

 
🚗 Parking
$2.00 per hour in the beach lot or Street Parking is FREE

description:

Join us for a fun and interacting class in which you are able to create your own sterling silver ring. This is a 2~2.5hr hands-on experience with expert guidance. The Liberty Program is thrilled to provide a 40% discount for Active Duty E1-E6 service members (original price $120 per person).

Sign Up Today!

name: Michael Bazan Jimenez & Noah Lichwa Memorial Fun Run/Walk
description:
The 4th Annual Michael Bazan Jimenez & Noah Lichwa Memorial Fun Run will be a fundraiser taking place on Winters Youth Day, April 24th, 2027 to help raise money for the Noah Lichwa & Michael Bazan Jimenez Memorial Scholarships. On June 9th 2022, we tragically lost two young men which effected our community deeply. We are bringing back this Youth Day Fun Run not only to raise money to benefit students at the local high school, but also to remember and honor the boys we lost that day. This will be a 5K fun run/walk, on April 24th, 2027 and starting at 7:00 AM. All funds raised will be given to the Scholarship and awarded at the Winters High School Senior Night. If you can't register on line, in person registration will take place on Friday April 23th from 5:00 to 7:00 PM at Hooby's Brewery at 9 E Main St. All participants that register by Thursday April 1st will be guaranteed a commemorative Noah Lichwa and Michael Bazan Jimenez Memorial Fun Run t-shirt. Participants who register after that will only receive t-shirts as supplies last, on a first come first serve basis. 

 

Race Day Schedule:

7:00-Shirt Pick Up and Late Registration

7:30 Announcements

8:00- Race Starts

name: Midway Shelter Winter Run / Walk ~ 5k, 10k and Kids Run
description:
General Info - December 5th, 2026


Join us for the annual Midway Shelter winter run. Event takes place at the Harbor Bay Ferry Terminal in Alameda on Bay Farm Island and supports a great cause. 


The run will take you along the beautiful shoreline of Bay Farm Island and is a flat out and back with views of San Francisco and the Alameda Main Island. the first half is on the Harbor Bay Road with closed lanes for runners and the return is on the trails


The Kids run for 12 and under will be a 1/2 mile course. Kids run will start at 9:45am and will follow a circular loop out and back on the shoreline trail. There is plenty of parking at the Ferry terminal and we will have snacks and drinks when the race is over. 


Packet Pick up and Race Schedule:

  • December 3rd and 4th, 2026: 10:00am - 5:00pm Lauren's Closet 1420 Park St / Alameda, Ca. 94501
  • December 5th: 
    • 7:30am ~ raceday registration opens
      8:30am ~ 10k starts
      8:45am ~ 5k starts
      9:45am ~ kids 1/2 mile run starts
      10:00am ~ 5k and 10k awards
       

Midway Shelter provides emergency shelter to homeless women and children and is operated through a partnership with Alameda Homeless Network and Building Futures – learn more about our work by checking out our two websites, below!

Founded in 1989, Midway Shelter of Alameda provides a safe and supportive environment for women and children experiencing  homelessness. By pledging any dollar amount, in addition to your registration, you can support the Midway Shelter provide a safe place for women and their children. Your donation is tax deductible as the Alameda Homeless Network operates as a 501(c)3 Tax ID number 94-3078153)

 

http://midwayshelter.org/donate.htm
www.bfwc.org

name: Mile Madness Endurance Run
description:
Join the Ultimate Loop Adventure in the Heart of Trail Country!

Mile Madness is more than a race—it's a vibrant celebration of endurance, community, and personal triumph. Set against the stunning backdrop of Auburn, California, this looped trail event invites runners of all paces to push their limits (or simply enjoy the journey) on a meticulously designed 0.75-mile course and paved bike path, featuring a beautiful pond, shaded paths, and much more for an unforgettable experience.

Event Details:

Dates: September 24-27, 2027

Friday:

9:00 am 72 Hour Run

6:00 pm: 48 Hour Run

Saturday:

9:00 am: 3-Hour Run/Walk, 12-Hour Run/Walk, and 100 Mile Race 

Noon: 24 Hour Run/Walk

3:00 pm: 6 Hour Run/Walk

Location: Auburn Recreation District Regional Park, 3770 Richardson Dr, Auburn, CA 95602

Race Options: Choose your challenge from 7 timed events, ranging from a beginner-friendly 3-hour run to the epic 72-hour ultra. With exceptionally long cutoffs and no strict time pressures, whether you're walking, running, or crawling, there's space for everyone to shine and even earn one of the coveted Mile Madness Buckles.

Course Highlights: A compact 0.75-mile loop means continuous laps with easy access to aid stations, festive decorations, and upbeat music to keep your spirits high. Aim for that first ultra milestone or chase elite goals—many of our runners discover untapped potential here. The course will be professionally measured prior to the race.

Why Mile Madness?

Inclusivity for All: We had runners from under age 10 to runners and walkers in their 80's, with a balanced mix of 52.8% male and 47.2% female participants. In 2024, we welcomed 115 runners with a remarkable 72% buckle completion rate (applies to 48- and 72-hour runners); in 2025, we were 140 strong, and in 2026, 181. Beginners who've never run an ultramarathon often surprise themselves with distances they never imagined.

Top-Notch Support: Fully stocked aid stations featuring a rotating menu of hearty meals, electrolytes, all the typical aid station food, and endless encouragement from what might be the best trail-running volunteers. Other amenities include on-site massage therapists, family cheer zones, glow run, food trucks, and more...

Bling & Bragging Rights: Earn the coveted Silver 100-Mile Buckle (many trying an ultra for the first time) or challenge yourself for the stunning Gold 150-Mile Buckle or the 200-Mile Buckle. Plus, a 100% rollover policy up to 24 hours before race start means zero risk if life throws a curveball.

SWAG: Every registered runner will receive amazing SWAG. In 2026, every registered runner received MudGear/Mile Madness co-branded socks, a long-sleeve hooded tech shirt, and a waterproof picnic blanket... We cannot guarantee sizes for registrations after 8/1/27, but we will do our best to accommodate requests. 

Bib Raffle: We will hold a bib raffle at regular intervals during the race. Registered runners will be entered into the raffle. It's a bonus: you might walk away with fantastic prizes, including shoes, handheld bottles, an antichafe stick, and more. Why should podium winners get all the bling?

Family & Community Focus: Bring your crew! Our expansive UltraLounge, which offers shaded comfort, music, free snacks and water, games, festive decorations, S’mores, and a DIY sign-making station to fuel the fun. Come solo or with friends—you'll leave with new bonds, shared stories, and memories that last a lifetime. Runners rave: "The highlight of my year!" (Summer W.) and "My favorite race ever!" (Shawnee).

Worry-Free Guarantee: We will roll over your race entry to next year if you can't run because of injury, training challenges, or any other reason. We want you to enjoy the race you pay for, and we understand that life happens.

Extra Perks: Plenty of clean restrooms with showers, spots to "rest" in tents when you need a break (we can't call it camping), and a commitment to giving back through the Run Free Foundation, whose mission is to empower at-risk youth and runners facing financial barriers by providing access to quality running gear and race registration scholarships, enabling them to pursue their athletic dreams and enhance their well-being. 

Mile Madness isn't just about the miles—it's about the madness of joy, grit, and connection that turns strangers into trail family. Whether you're chasing a PR, your first buckle, or the thrill of the loop, we're here to support you every step of the way. We may have the best volunteers in the business.

Ultra Lounge: The family cheer zone is getting a more fitting name. We are borrowing the Ultra Lounge name and will have our 13x26 wedding tent with fun activities that will keep your crew going so they can keep cheering you on.  We will have food and water, a poster-making station, a glow party, cornhole, and more... Don't forget the running movies, fire pit with s'mores, and games for your crew and family while you crush miles.

Referral Rewards: We want to reward you for referring other runners to Mile Madness.  When you register, you will get a referral code to share.  Have your family, friends, or social circle use that code, and you will receive a refund for every referral.

Earn $10 for any 6-Hour or 12-Hour referral.  Earn $20 for each referral to the 24-Hour or longer races.  The refund will happen automatically, and the referral code must be used by the person registering. 

Questions? Email Race Director Brian Goldman at brian@everydayenduranceraces.com. Let's make 2027 your most memorable madness yet! We had an amazing 2026, our best year yet, and 2027 is going to blow it out of the water.  We hope to see you at the starting line and the monthly training runs on course, starting in January.

name: Miles For Meals Virtual Triathlon and Virtual Marathon
description:
Miles for Meals 
A Pneuma Impact Project in partnership with Support the Cuban People Org
Go the distance for a neighbor you'll never meet.

A 30-day virtual endurance challenge uniting athletes around one goal: keeping a community fed in Cuba, where food, medicine, and power have all but run out.

11/01/2026 – 12/01/26 · 30 days
Choose: 70.3 Triathlon or Marathon
Track every mile on Strava

We connect a global community of athletes around one goal: bringing sustained aid to those the world has forgotten. Because every neighbor deserves to be seen and served — and loving your neighbor isn't optional. Miles for Meals turns the miles you'd train anyway into action where it matters most.

Why Cuba, why now
Cuba is living through one of its worst crises in decades. The economy has collapsed, and ordinary families are carrying an almost unbearable weight. 20 hrs — Some areas lose power for up to 20 hours a day, crippling hospitals, businesses, and homes.
Shortages — Severe nationwide shortages of the essentials: food, medicine, and fuel.
Daily — Basic groceries are increasingly out of reach for everyday families.

Our partner on the ground: Pan de Vida
Every weekend, Pan de Vida opens its doors to anyone in the community who needs a meal — no requirements, no barriers, just food for whoever shows up. In a country where basic groceries are slipping out of reach, a warm weekend meal can make all the difference.

Pick your challenge

name: Miles for Migraine Los Angeles
description:
Miles for Migraine will host its 9th annual 2-mile Walk, 5K Run and Relax Los Angeles event on Saturday November 21st at Woodley Park. This event is a fundraiser for Migraine & Headache Awareness, Treatment & Research. It's more than a walk/run - come connect with your local migraine & headache community, listen to our speakers & visit sponsors in the festival area.

The 5K run is professionally timed. The Walk and the Relax events are FREE, and donations are encouraged. All walk and run finishers receive a finisher medal. Dress up in your best purple flair for a chance at a fun prize!

Funds raised will benefit Miles for Migraine free programs & services as well as the Keck Medicine of USC Headache Center to support local migraine research and fellowship training programs.

name: Miles Together
description:
A little movement, a little ocean air, and a whole lot of community.

Join MeiMei and Jacob in partnership with Skechers for Miles Together, a community run and walk hosted by McAve Media in partnership with Skechers in Manhattan Beach.

We’ll meet at the Skechers store for a warm-up, photos, and time to connect before heading out along the coast together. Whether you’re running or walking, come enjoy the morning at your own pace.

Afterward, head back to Base Camp for refreshments, personalized photo keychains, and a relaxed post-run hangout with MeiMei and Jacob.

Spaces are limited, and advance registration is required. All participants must complete the participant waiver and photo/video release before joining.

Let’s make some memories, one mile at a time.

name: Millerton Lake Crows Nest Triathlon, 5k & 10k
description:
What will you find at the "Crows Nest" Triathlon?

+ Finisher's Medal 
+ Event T-Shirt
+ Prizes and Giveaways
+ Finisher's Meal
+ Free Race Photos 

The Millerton Lake Sprint Triathlon has long been known as a great "first lake swim" triathlon, and a warm up for the upcoming season. But don't let the bike and run distances fool you, there are a few steep hills on the ride, and the trail portion of run is a challenge.

More of a good thing... The Olympic Distance has a more challenging swim, two loops of the bike course, and two loops of the run course with a trail run heading out, a paved road coming back and beautiful Millerton Lake as the backdrop.

Note:

A USAT membership is required for the Triathlon, (but not the 5k/10k). If you do not have one, you can purchase one during the registration process.  Per USAT rules, multisport participants must present ID and USAT membership card at packet pickup.

Total participation at this event is capped at 200.  Register before it is sold out.

There is a $10 vehicle entrance fee.

description:

+ Finisher's Medal 
+ Event T-Shirt
+ Prizes and Giveaways

name: Millerton Madness Triathlon
description:
USAT Sanctioned Super Sprint Triathlon.  

Perfect for beginners, or a tune-up before your next big race.

400 yd swim | 5.4 mile bike | 2.2 mile run

Swim: Starting in the water at Millerton, athletes will utilize Millerton Lake Boat Launch. Athletes will swim 400 yards around buoys, back to the boat ramp, exit the water and proceed to the Transition Area.

Bike: Starting at the Transition Area, athletes will make their way north towards the Millerton park entrance, to the turnaround at the top Millerton Lake SRA sign. The bike is out and back with rolling hills. Returning to the transition area.

Run: Run is all asphalt road. Starting at the Transition Area, athletes head north from the parking lot along the street for approximately 1.1 miles towards the Millerton park entrance to the turn around, (at the crosswalk), and back to the finish line.

name: Mind Over Miles
description:
Mind Over Miles is a community endurance event unlike a traditional race.

Beginning at the top of each hour, participants have the opportunity to complete a 4.2-mile loop. When you finish, you'll have the remainder of the hour to rest, refuel, connect with others, or cheer on fellow participants before the next loop begins.

You choose your challenge:

Complete one loop (4.2 miles)
Run several loops throughout the day
Or take on the ultimate challenge by completing 12 loops for approximately 50 miles
There are no expectations—only an invitation to show up, challenge yourself, and encourage those around you. Whether you're an experienced ultrarunner, training for your next race, walking with family, supporting a friend, or simply looking for a reason to get outside, there's a place for you at Mind Over Miles.

Our mission is simple:

Helping people find hope, purpose, and the strength to keep moving forward—one step at a time.

This event exists to bring people together through movement while raising awareness for mental wellness, recovery, and the power of community. Every mile is a reminder that difficult roads are easier when we don't walk them alone.

Come for one lap. Stay for twelve. However many miles you choose, you'll be part of something bigger than yourself.

One community. One hour at a time. One step at a time.

name: MISSION INN FOUNDATION RUN
description:
The 49th Annual Mission Inn Foundation Run returns to downtown Riverside on October 18, 2026! 

The Mission Inn Foundation Run, a signature Riverside event and key fundraiser for the Mission Inn Foundation, has been a Southern California Tradition for nearly 50 years. This historic race has traditionally launched in downtown Riverside, winding through the parks, landmarks and historic neighborhoods of our town. Proceeds support the nonprofit Mission Inn Foundation and Museum.

Races include the 5K, 10K and ½ Marathon with dedicated 5K Walk (perfect for the kids and pups!) Everyone from competitors to casual strollers are invited to join us!

•      All participants will receive the 2026 limited edition dry-tech Mission Inn Foundation Run T-shirt 
•      All participants will receive 2026 finisher medal 
•      All participants will receive limited edition non-woven reusable tote bag

The Mission Inn Foundation Run, a Riverside tradition since 1977, is the primary fundraiser for the Mission Inn Foundation, a 501c3 non-profit museum organization. The Mission Inn Foundation Run is the trademarked intellectual property of the Mission Inn Foundation.  There is no affiliation with the Historic Mission Inn Corporation, nor does the Historic Mission Inn Corporation benefit from or support this event.  All funds raised go to the Mission Inn Foundation, a 501c3 non-profit organization.  For more information about the Mission Inn Foundation, please visit www.missioninnmuseum.org

name: Miwok 100K Trail Race presented by The North Face
description:
The Miwok 100K presented by The North Face is one of the most beautiful and iconic trail ultramarathons in the world. We believe everyone deserves a shot at something extraordinary. The Miwok100K is about the everyday runner who shows up ready to dig deep on some of the most breathtaking trails around. Set in the Marin Headlands just north of San Francisco, The Miwok 100K offers 62 miles of gorgeous trails, over 11,000 feet of gain, and nonstop views, from redwoods to ridge lines to crashing coastal cliffs. 

The course features single-track trails and dirt roads with about a mile of paved road. The race is competitive at the front, and a rewarding challenge for all. Less than an hour from San Francisco, the Start/Finish is in the town of beautiful Stinson Beach, nestled against Mount Tamalpais, with its excellent cafés, a small market, lodging, and more.

Course marking is excellent, and you’ll be supported by some of the best volunteers on a race course anywhere. We hire professional medical for all aid stations for those occasional skinned knees and such. Our 2027 runners will receive a custom Miwok 100K finisher’s medal and a Miwok 100K sweatshirt.

We have 3 options for you to participate in our event:

1. Miwok 100K on May 1, 2027 (When the race is full, you will be placed on a Waitlist. Your card will not be charged until you are offered a spot, and accept it. Registered runners who drop prior to February 1 will receive a $124 (40%) refund. 

2. Miwok 100K on May 1, 2027, PLUS a 16 week training plan from coach & Race Director Magda Boulet (no refund)

3. Miwok 100K 4 person Team Relay on May 1, 2027 (must have 4 participants per relay)

Please make sure you sign up for the correct event!

name: MJC Turkey Trot 5k Run and Gobbler Walk
description:
***PARK IS ON THE CORNER OF TIOGA DRIVE AND LEIGION PARK

 

WALK-IN REGISTRATIONS ONLY STARTING ON WEDNESDAY 11/25
***RACE DAY REGISTRATION RATES INCREASE ONCE PRE-REGISTRATION CLOSES, SO SIGN UP TODAY!!!

***PLEASE REMEMBER TO BRING IN CASH FOR RACE DAY SIGN UPS. VENMO IS ALSO AVAILABLE

 

Packet Pickup:

  When: Wednesday (11/25) from 2-6pm 
                

  Location: Fleet Feet Modesto - 1427 Standiford Avenue, Suite A

  AND/OR

  Race day morning up to 30 minutes before the start of the first kid's race

 

***All Proceeds Benefit MJC's Track and Field and Cross Country Programs

 

Exercise with friends and family before indulging on your Thanksgiving meal!

 

Course: The 3.1 mile course is on a paved path with some grass and dirt. Please no strollers, headphones, or dogs in the 5K run.

name: MLK Jr. Freedom Run 5K/10K/13.1 LOS ANGELES
description:
Join in our annual Martin Luther King Jr. Day Run! Today, we gather to honor the legacy of Dr. King and his enduring commitment to justice, equality, and peace. Together, we can honor Dr. King’s dream and inspire one another to continue striving for a better world.  

Forget the massive, impersonal race-day crowds. We keep things small, personal, and local, so every run feels less like a number and more like a memory. Whether it's a 5K, 10K, half-marathon, or virtual run, you'll get the warmth of a hometown event.
 

Overview:
Spots sell out FAST! We close each wave the moment it fills. Once a wave sells out, you can grab the virtual run option or join the waitlist.

This is a smaller, private group run with a capped field per wave so it never feels crowded and you're never just a bib number.
All paces and ages welcome (under 18 with a guardian) - run it, walk it, however you like!
There's no gear, no setup, no fuss - just you, the course, and our coordinators cheering you on in a relaxed, stress-free setting.
When you sign up, you're not just registering for a race - you're getting real support toward your fitness goals, plus an invite to join one of our local run clubs to keep the momentum going.
 
Timing:
Optional! Track your own time via Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, or similar, then submit it through our easy online form to get posted.  Or just ask a coordinator to help time you.
No timing chips - this is about progress, not pressure.
 
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-shirt (shipped to your address - U.S. only)
- Finisher's medal
- Virtual Training Run (emailed to you a month before your run)
- Online results & certificate of completion
- Invitation to join a local running club
- NEW: Upgrade to a lightweight, moisture-wicking technical shirt for just $5 more
 
Packet Pickup?
Skip It. No lines, no hassle - your swag ships straight to your door. (Double check your full U.S. mailing address, including apartment number, when you register as your shirt is sent to this address!) Race bibs are simply handed out on race day.
 
When Will My Swag Arrive?
Your shirt will arrive at your mailing address the week of your race.
 
Signing Up Last Minute? (Within 2 Weeks of the Race)
No problem - just note that shipping may not catch up in time, so your shirt could arrive after race day. No worries, though: wear whatever you like and come run with us anyway!
 
When Will I Receive the Course Map and Details?
We'll send final participant info by the Wednesday before race day with all the details and course maps.
 
Wave Times  (Once you've registered, use your confirmation number to reserve a wave here)
Wave A: 7:30 AM
Wave B: 8:00 AM
Wave C: 8:30 AM
 
Running Late?
Jump in when you arrive - our coordinators stay on-site for 3 hours after the first wave. Times may be subject to change depending on seasons, please check your participant info email!
Got more questions? Check our FAQ.
 
Virtual Run Option
Prefer to run on your own time? Our Virtual Run includes a digital training pack to keep you on track. Run it whenever, wherever, with any tracking device you like (optional) — then send your results to info@thebestraces.com to claim your medal.

name: MLK Jr. Freedom Run 5K/10K/13.1 SAN FRANCISCO
description:
Join in our annual Martin Luther King Jr. Day Run! Today, we gather to honor the legacy of Dr. King and his enduring commitment to justice, equality, and peace. Together, we can honor Dr. King’s dream and inspire one another to continue striving for a better world.  

Forget the massive, impersonal race-day crowds. We keep things small, personal, and local, so every run feels less like a number and more like a memory. Whether it's a 5K, 10K, half-marathon, or virtual run, you'll get the warmth of a hometown event.
 

Overview:
Spots sell out FAST! We close each wave the moment it fills. Once a wave sells out, you can grab the virtual run option or join the waitlist.

This is a smaller, private group run with a capped field per wave so it never feels crowded and you're never just a bib number.
All paces and ages welcome (under 18 with a guardian) - run it, walk it, however you like!
There's no gear, no setup, no fuss - just you, the course, and our coordinators cheering you on in a relaxed, stress-free setting.
When you sign up, you're not just registering for a race - you're getting real support toward your fitness goals, plus an invite to join one of our local run clubs to keep the momentum going.
 
Timing:
Optional! Track your own time via Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, or similar, then submit it through our easy online form to get posted.  Or just ask a coordinator to help time you.
No timing chips - this is about progress, not pressure.
 
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-shirt (shipped to your address - U.S. only)
- Finisher's medal
- Virtual Training Run (emailed to you a month before your run)
- Online results & certificate of completion
- Invitation to join a local running club
- NEW: Upgrade to a lightweight, moisture-wicking technical shirt for just $5 more
 
Packet Pickup?
Skip It. No lines, no hassle - your swag ships straight to your door. (Double check your full U.S. mailing address, including apartment number, when you register as your shirt is sent to this address!) Race bibs are simply handed out on race day.
 
When Will My Swag Arrive?
Your shirt will arrive at your mailing address the week of your race.
 
Signing Up Last Minute? (Within 2 Weeks of the Race)
No problem - just note that shipping may not catch up in time, so your shirt could arrive after race day. No worries, though: wear whatever you like and come run with us anyway!
 
When Will I Receive the Course Map and Details?
We'll send final participant info by the Wednesday before race day with all the details and course maps.
 
Wave Times  (Once you've registered, use your confirmation number to reserve a wave here)
Wave A: 7:30 AM
Wave B: 8:00 AM
Wave C: 8:30 AM
 
Running Late?
Jump in when you arrive - our coordinators stay on-site for 3 hours after the first wave. Times may be subject to change depending on seasons, please check your participant info email!

name: Mojave Half Marathon & 10K
description:
Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is proud to announce the 2027 Mojave Half Marathon & 10K, taking place on Saturday, 13 March 2027 aboard the Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center.  Military Installation access is required.  

The Half Marathon will challenge runners to test their stamina, determination, and grit. Whether you are a seasoned distance runner or preparing for your next major fitness goal, now is the time to start training!

The 10K is challenging yet accessible for beginners and intermediate runners, providing a good introduction to long-distance running without the intensity of a half marathon.

Registration Opens:  Monday, September 7, 2026

PLESAE NOTE:  Registration after Thursday, February 11, 2027 are not guaranteed participant t-shirts or finisher medals.

Registration Fees: 

Half Marathon Early Bird (ends 31 December) - $60

Half Marathon after 31 December - $75

10K Early Bird (ends 31 December) - $25

10K after 31 December- $30

ATTENTION:  Please be aware.  There is a cut off time for this event for half-marathon participants.  Runners must accomplish the 7-mile mark within 2 hours, or they will be removed from participating.  The overall limit for the half marathon is 4 hours.  Runners who do not meet these cut off times will be pulled from the event.  This is standard and due to the requirement to reopen closed roads to the MCAGCC community.

REMINDER:  This is an event aboard MCAGCC Twentynine Palms and Military Installation access is a requirement.

For questions or additional information, please contact MCCS Athletics at 760.830.6857 or email 29athletics@usmc-mccs.org.

name: Monster Dash 5k - Hosted by PCS MVP Club - Quincy Site
description:
Plumas Charter School Quincy Site is holding its annual Monster Dash 5k on Saturday, October 24th, at Feather River College to raise $10,000 for K-12th grade students and teachers.

The race starts at the FRC sand volleyball courts located by the FRC baseball fields. Racers will traverse along the walking trail and across the Gansner Park bridge continuing down spanish creek road to the midway point at the end of the road. Racers will turn around and head back the way they came! Folks that prefer a short route can turn around before the bridge if they choose.

DAY OF REGISTRATION AVAILABLE STARTING AT 3:00pm ON RACE DAY! CASH, CHECK AND CREDIT CARD WILL BE ACCEPTED.

name: Monster Mash Dash and Zombie Zoom
description:
Lace up your running shoes and join us on on October 31st for a frightfully fun day of racing!

The little monsters (ages 10 and under) kick things off at 12:00 PM with the 400 m Zombie Zoom, a quick run perfect for our youngest ghouls.

Then at 12:15 PM, the Monster Dash takes off with your choice of a timed 5K or 10K. Whether you're chasing a personal record or just out for a haunted good time, there's a distance for every runner.

Costumes are encouraged, so come dressed to scare!

Run fast! The first 100 finishers will take home a custom race medal, so don't get caught dead at the back of the pack.

Note: High schoolers in full monster costumes will be chasing and scaring during the 5K and 10K race. Options to not be chased.

name: Monterey's Breast Cancer Awareness Run
description:
In the journey to end cancer as we know it, every step makes a difference. On October 10th, Fleet Feet Monterey, is hosting their 4th Annual Breast Cancer Awareness 5K Walk and Run. Lace up those shoes and show up with like-hearted people who care as we take steps together to support cancer research, increase awareness about and access to screening and treatment, and honor the legacies of those who have courageously lived with breast cancer and other estrogen-related cancers. 

Join us in making a difference step by step! All proceeds from our race will go to the Monterey County Breast Cancer Assistance Group. Our goal is to raise $3000, join us to make a difference in our local community. 

The event kicks off at 8:15 am with doors opening at 8:00 am at Fleet Feet Monterey. The 5K will be an untimed community walk and run, promoting solidarity and support. The course will begin and end at Fleet Feet Monterey, taking participants on an out-and-back route.

Let's lace up our sneakers and come together for a great cause!

Schedule:
8:00 am - Doors open
8:15 am - Event officially Begins 
8:30 am - 5K begins
9:00 am - Post-Run breakfast, giveaways, photo booth

name: Moorpark Groundhog Day 5k/1M
description:
Benefiting Moorpark High School’s cross country and track programs, the Groundhog Day event consists of two events. Starting at the high school, the 5k is a fast, chip timed road race with an exciting finish at the beautiful Moorpark High School stadium. All ages and abilities are welcome.  All participants age 11 and under who complete the 5k will received a finisher medal.  There will also be a “Catch the Groundhog” 1 mile fun run for kids 11 and under which will be held on the track with finisher medals for all. Registration fees include a t-shirt for all runners (shirts are only guaranteed if you register by Sunday 1/24/27).

Post-race festivities include the awards ceremony with age group medals plus refreshments, vendors, and a raffle of wonderful prizes donated by local businesses.

name: Moraga Turkey Trot-2026
description:
Please join the Moraga Chamber of Commerce on Thanksgiving morning for the annual Moraga Turkey Trot! Gobble-Wobble your way out to the cart path at Moraga Country Club wearing your favorite zany costume, activewear or even PJs! You can push a pram, set up a run squad or saunter solo, but just be sure to bring your community spirit!

The morning will include “unofficial” timed 5K and 1.5m races, awards for best Thanksgiving-themed costume, each race's speediest turkey, as well as random bib number draws to earn prizes from local businesses. (Be sure to check your bib number on the board on race day to see if you're a prize winner!)  

Runners, walkers and lollygaggers of all ages are welcome, but advance registration is required. Unfortunately, we cannot take registrations on-site. Registrants receive a T-shirt (sizes & tees not guaranteed - see registration details), a numbered running bib and goodies, while they last! Participants will check the digital timer at START/FINISH for self-timing. Come enjoy this wholesome tradition and celebrate Thanksgiving morning together! You do not need to be a member of the Chamber or the Country Club to participate. 

 

START TIMES

  • 5K - START TIME (8:05a) – Participants line up by 8am
  • 1.5m - START TIME (8:15a) – Participants line up following the departure of 5K (8:10am)

 

IMPORTANT NOTES 

  • DAY-OF Registration is **Not Available**
  • Anyone on the course must be registered, "Bib'd" and have signed the waiver (Including any free participants)
  • Kids 4y and under are free, but must be registered
  • New packet pickup days & longer times - See pickup details
  • New Starting location - Further North on the cart path
  • Parking will be limited and traffic laws enforced. Arrange for carpool, drop-offs and walking over, whenever possible
  • Take Care and remember to be kind to one another!

name: Morgan Hill AAUW Wildflower Run
description:
The AAUW Wildflower Run raises money for scholarships and leadership programs for women & girls and community grants. (For information about our organization, go to www.aauwmh.org.) 10K Run, 5K Run, and 5K Walk are all on country roads with chip timing. The Kids' 2K Run (ages 5-11) and our "all inclusive, non-competitive" 2K Fun Run/Walk (for ages 2-102) are both on a school track.  
Our new 5K and 10K routes are in a country setting surrounding Morgan Hill with flat terrain on paved roads. Flat and fast for runners wanting to improve their personal record times. Water available at start and finish of race, with multiple water stops along the routes. Strollers are welcome everywhere except on the school's track. No pets permitted on school grounds.
NOTE: The event is an "open course", so you will need to stay to the side of the road as some vehicular traffic is expected.
Register early to be guaranteed a unique, 2027 T-shirt in your size.  
New this year, you can join (or form) a team during signup to enter our fun "Flower Power Team Challenge". You will be asked during registration "Do you want to join a team?" Teams must have at least 6 members and can compete in one of 2 overall categories: Biggest or Fastest. Please see wildflowerrun.org/teamchallenge for more details.
  •

name: Morgan Hill Veterans Day  Run
description: The Morgan Hill Freedom Fest is proud to host the Veterans Day 5k & 10k and 1 mile children's Run to honor the men and women who have served or are currently serving in the armed forces of the United States.  You will have the opportunity to walk and run with these honorable men and women during the race and express your appreciation for their service as you finish the course with them. We encourage participants to take a moment and say, “Thank you for what you’ve done!” Small gestures mean a lot to those who have sacrificed so much. All proceeds from the  race will go to the Veteran organizations listed on our Partners page.  We hope to see you there!

name: Mountains 2 Beach Marathon and Half
description: Uniquely situated and completely surrounded by beautiful mountains, the city of Ojai holds the start of the Mountains 2 Beach Marathon while the half starts closer to the beach. This point to point race winds through the Ventura River Valley as it makes its way to the pristine beaches of the last great surf town in California, Ventura. Runners will love the gradual downhill nature of the race, which is prime to make you faster but not hurt the knees, and the amazing weather of the area. After a final tour of beach front Ventura, runners and their families are treated to a finish line party only steps away from the surf and the shops and restaurants of Historic Downtown Ventura. As a certified Boston Qualifier, the courses, the race and the surrounding communities make for the perfect destination marathon and half.

name: MPSF Open Water Championships - Masters/Open 5 Kilometer and 1 Kilometer Open Water Swim
description:
The 4th MPSF Open Water Swimming Championships will be contested Saturday, October 17, 2026 at Marine Stadium in Long Beach, Calif.  Be a part of the third intercollegiate conference championship in open water swimming.  

The MPSF Championships in OWS could potentially lead to an NCAA Championship in the sport.  Open water swimming has been in the Olympics since 2008.  Alumni from institutions eligible for MPSF membership in OWS have participated in every one of these Olympic competitions and have medaled in both the men’s and women’s events.  The Marine Stadium will host Rowing and Canoeing during the 2028 Olympic Games.  Long Beach will also host the Open Water Swimming and eight other sports events for the 2028 Olympic Games.  

The Open 5 Kilometer and 1 Kilometer Open Water Swim participants are encouraged to affiliate with the MPSF member institution that they swam collegiately for, currently attend or graduated from.  Don't forget to wear your team colors.

Additional race information can be found at https://mpsports.org/tournaments/?id=69

name: Mt. Tam Trail Run
description:
Mt. Tamalpais is the dominating feature in Marin County.  Any true trail runner who sees it wants to run up it.  Here’s your chance.  Our Mt. Tam Trail Run begins at Stinson Beach and climbs (and climbs!) to perched views from Tam before returning via some of the best trails the Headlands have to offer until reaching the beach and bountiful post race food.  Bring the family and enjoy an afternoon with friends in the sand and surf.

Park Information: Mt. Tam State Park, Muir Woods National Monument

name: Mutt Run
description:
*Please note this 5K is just for fun and raising money for a non-profit—it won't count as a qualifying event for other races.

Get ready to run, walk, wag, and HOWL with us on Saturday, October 24 at the 13th Annual Howl-O-Ween Mutt Run 5K Run/Walk!

Whether you’re a serious runner, a casual walker, a dedicated dog person, or just looking for a fun Halloween morning with your favorite four-legged friend, there’s a place for you in our pack!

And this year, we’re running for a BIG reason: our goal is to raise $120,000 to help provide the food, shelter, medical care, and second chances our rescue dogs need while they wait for their forever homes.

🎃 Dress up with your dog (or on your own! No dog needed to join in the fun!), bring your friends, run or walk the 5K, enjoy the beer garden, fundraise for rescue and help save lives!

Registration is OPEN, so grab your spot and get ready to make this the best Howl-O-Ween yet!

--

The Howl-O-Ween Mutt Run isn’t just an event on our calendar – it’s a mission in motion. Every step we take, every dollar we raise, provides the lifesaving care for the 900 dogs we rescue each year.

This year, we reached an incredible milestone: our 16,000th dog rescued. These dogs faced an empty future and now have loving homes, warm beds, and a second chance. But for thousands more in Southern California, the fight is far from over. Many dogs are still trapped in overcrowded, heartbreaking shelter conditions, where the only way out is euthanasia.

We house the dogs we save at our Rescue Ranch Care Center where hope begins the moment they arrive. Each dog receives medical treatment, nourishing food, exercise, training, and most of all—love. Every day, over 150 dogs who once had nowhere to turn are safe because of Your Generosity!

When you run, you’re not just crossing a finish line—you’re crossing a lifeline.
You’re giving a dog the one thing they want most: A Future To Howl About!

Help us reach our goal of raising $115,000 so we can continue this life saving mission.

name: Nail the Rail Half Marathon, 10K & 5K
description:
Join us for a stroll along the Sacramento Rail Trail.  A converted Southern Pacific Railroad track that starts at the base of Shasta Dam and runs for over 11 miles.

Enjoy a the view along the Sacramento River/Keswick Lake in the cool of the morning.  Trail is very flat and fast.

Field is limited to 500.

Races include a half marathon, 10K and 5K.

Finisher awards to Half marathoners.  Awards 3 deep in age groups, plus overall awards.

Start/Finish will be from the Chappie OHV area at the base of Shasta Dam.  Once you cross Shasta Dam you will follow the road down to the OHV area.

Race day registration and packet pickup opens at 7am at OHV area.

Packet pickup and registration on Friday the 23rd from 11am to 3pm at Redding Fleet Feet Store at 1376 Hilltop Dr.

Start times:

Half Marathon - 8am

5K & 10K - 8:15am

Cutoff time of 3hrs 15 minutes for half-marathon.

name: Napa Valley Turkey Chase
description:
Welcome to the Turkey Chase, Napa's only Thanksgiving Day 5K/10K! 

The Napa Valley Turkey Chase is a fun family event! Race, jog or walk this fast, paved course around the Napa Valley College and the Napa River Trail and work up your Thanksgiving appetite!

The start & finish line are located in lot J behind the Napa Valley College track. Lot J will also be the staging area for packet pick-up, day of race registration, booths and toilets. There is NO PARKING in lot J .

The 10K course runs a counterclockwise loop through the college and then meets the Napa River Trail. Runners will go north to a turn around under the Imola bridge near mile 2. Then they will run south to Kennedy Park where the course makes a small counterclockwise loop near the skate park and then retraces the route back up the river trail. The 10K course then meets back up with the 5K by the baseball field and finishes back in lot J.

The 5K course runs the same counterclockwise loop through the college and then connects to the Napa River Trail. Runners will immediately proceed south past mile 2 and turn at the baseball field to head to the finish back in lot J. Both courses have been measured by wheel and GPS, but it is not a USATF certified course.

name: Napa Valley Turkey Chase
description:
Welcome to the Turkey Chase, Napa's only Thanksgiving Day 5K/10K! 

The Napa Valley Turkey Chase is a fun family event! Race, jog or walk this fast, paved course around the Napa Valley College and the Napa River Trail and work up your Thanksgiving appetite!

The start & finish line are located in lot J behind the Napa Valley College track. Lot J will also be the staging area for packet pick-up, day of race registration, booths and toilets. There is NO PARKING in lot J .

The 10K course runs a counterclockwise loop through the college and then meets the Napa River Trail. Runners will go north to a turn around under the Imola bridge near mile 2. Then they will run south to Kennedy Park where the course makes a small counterclockwise loop near the skate park and then retraces the route back up the river trail. The 10K course then meets back up with the 5K by the baseball field and finishes back in lot J.

The 5K course runs the same counterclockwise loop through the college and then connects to the Napa River Trail. Runners will immediately proceed south past mile 2 and turn at the baseball field to head to the finish back in lot J. Both courses have been measured by wheel and GPS, but it is not a USATF certified course.

name: Navy Ten-Miler
description:
Run with Honor. Endure with Courage. Finish with Commitment.

The Navy Ten-Miler brings together athletes, service members, veterans, and civilians to honor the Navy’s core values of Honor, Courage, and Commitment. Whether you're a seasoned runner or searching for your next challenge, this is your call to RUN NAVY.

Navy Races are more than a finish line. They celebrate the strength, resilience, and unity of our community. Proceeds benefit Navy Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) programs that enhance the lives of Sailors and their families.

Key Benefits:

  • Support Navy personnel and families
  • Run along San Diego’s iconic waterfront
  • Experience naval history and patriotism
  • Connect with the veteran and civilian running community
  • Be part of a race with purpose and impact

Who Can Participate?

Everyone is welcome. Whether you are active duty, a veteran, a military family member, or a civilian who wants to support a meaningful cause, Navy Race events are open to all fitness levels.

Join a race with purpose.

name: Nelson Family Vineyards Wine Run 5k
description:
Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Saturday, April 17, 2027 at 10:00am for a super fun annual event that features the amazing hospitality and scenery of Nelson Family Vineyards! For 70 years the Nelson family has farmed the land they live on, with the traditions of farming passed on to four generations. Through many seasons of tending and harvest, Nelson Family Vineyards has embraced the truth that great wines are born in the vineyard. So, whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wine this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience! This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing.  Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: 
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!

name: New Year's Day Dash – 5K, 10K, 10-Miler, Half Marathon
description:
Start your year on the right foot with the New Year’s Day Dash on January 1, 2027 in Long Beach. Whether you’re starting a new training goal, kicking off a resolution, or just looking for a fun way to welcome the year, this race is the perfect blend of fresh energy and festive spirit. Enjoy a beautiful course along the shoreline, the camaraderie of fellow runners, and the satisfaction of logging your first miles of 2027 before most people have finished their coffee. Make this your tradition and dash into the new year with us

Race Details

Start Location: Alamitos Beach, 380 E Shoreline Dr, Long Beach, CA 90802
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

Thursday
3:00-5:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event)
2100 N Bellflower Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90815

Friday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Courses
5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More about the Course
The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support
A fully stocked water station is located at the Belmont Pier. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, gatorade, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
