name: Race The Flame
description:
Are you ready? If you had to escape a wildfire in Santa Cruz how long would it take you to run or walk to reach safety?  Would you know which way to go? Here’s your chance to test yourself and gain knowledge about wildfires and their impact on our community. 

Join the second award-winning emergency preparedness run/walk in Santa Cruz - hosted by the City of Santa Cruz and The University of California at Santa Cruz. 

Adults are only $20 and kids 12 and under are $15.  This will automatically be calculated at check-out. 

Each participant will receive a bib with a timing chip regardless of which category you select. Competitive runners should pick the run option.  Walkers and strollers will start after competitive runners.

Because this event takes place on the UCSC campus there is a strict "no dogs" policy, so please plan on leaving your pooch at home. 

Background 

Race the Flame combines a community fun run, and an wildfire and emergency preparedness fair hosted by the City of Santa Cruz at the finish line. 

This event reinforces the community commitment to emergency preparedness and hazard mitigation. It highlights the shared responsibility to protect our community. 

The race begins on the UCSC campus at the East Field and follows a route down Coolidge Drive with an ending at the Bay Tree Campus Bookstore and High Street. The total distance is 2.3 miles from start to finish. 

At the finish line, an emergency preparedness fair will celebrate community resilience. Community-based organizations will share emergency preparedness information with the community. The fair will focus community attention on the need for 72 hours of personal and household preparedness.

During the registration process you will be asked if you would like to opt into Cruz Aware, the local emergency notification service. Find more information by clicking tab above. 

Parking will be available at the East Remote Parking Lot on Hagar Drive. Shuttle busses will be available to take you from the finish line up to your car or bike.

name: Race Thru the Redwoods
description:
*Sign up and take advantage of early bird pricing from Mother's Day through Father's Day only! 

The Race Thru The Redwoods starts and finishes at Roaring Camp Railroads in Felton, California.  The majority of the 10K race occurs under the majestic redwoods of Henry Cowell Redwoods State Park.  The Felton Business and Community Association and many local volunteers help manage and administer the race.

We are very excited to continue this race back for another year; with all that has gone on over this year and last, it is nice to do something that brings back fond memories and reminds us how lucky we are to be able to race, run, walk, or jog in such a lovely place. My wife and I fell in love under these trees at this race in 2013.

The race is open to anyone: runners, walkers, strollers, and joggers.

The 10k will take place on August 16th at 8:30 am.  Before the 10k, we will start the Kids Race at 8 am.  After the race, we are also delighted to host the PANCAKE breakfast sponsored by the Zayante Fire Department. Pancake Breakfast is included in your race fee. Non-participants can still enjoy a late brunch for a $10.00 fee.

If you'd like to share a picture or video of your run/walk with us.  We will create an album of all race pictures and share it via the RttRW website.

https://www.facebook.com/racethrutheredwoods 

This year has all the traditional course features that make the RttRW a local favorite and destination race.

10k Route: https://www.strava.com/routes/3257857005510265448

Kids 1 Mile: https://www.strava.com/routes/3260069223760673672 (2 laps)

Race Thru the Redwoods is more than a run through one of the most beautiful places in the Santa Cruz Mountains — it is also the Felton Business & Community Association’s biggest annual fundraiser. Proceeds from the race help support the many free community events and traditions we are proud to bring to Felton throughout the year. Every registration helps keep these events alive, welcoming, and accessible to our neighbors, families, and visitors. Thank you for running with us, supporting our town, and helping us continue to create moments that bring the Felton community together.

name: Race to the Flagpole
description:
The Race to the Flagpole is a community oriented race through beautiful wine country in Livermore California. The event is organized by the Livermore Granada Boosters, a local organization that has been celebrating the excellence of scholar athletes in Livermore since 1949. 

We accomplish our mission by promoting scholar athletic events with thousands of photos/video posted on our website, social media, and newsletter. Throughout the year, we recognize top individual and team achievements with Wall of Fame photos, posted throughout the community. At the end of each school year we host our Olympian Banquet for all varsity athletes and coaches. At this event, we recognize high character athletes of Livermore and Granada High Schools in 70 Varsity Sports. We induct past athletes into the Livermore Hall of Fame and award $20,000 in Scholarships to the top boy and girl student athletes from each high school.

All proceeds from the Race to the Flagpole supports these activities.

name: Ramona Wine Country 5K
description:
Be sure to grab your family, friends, coworkers and come join us for one of the most fun filled events in Southern California, the Ramona Wine Country 5k. It takes place at the breathtaking Backcountry Gardens and is part trails with a splash of mud run plus a healthy dose of Mother Nature’s obstacles mixed in for fun. You’ll also find some hills, streams, boulders and much more. Not your average 5K! Everyone can do it as long as you have the drive and determination to keep going, not quit and in the words of Joe Dirt, “keep on keepin’ on." 

It’s a 1.5 mile two loop course. If two loops are too many, feel free to enjoy the single loop option. You can walk, hike, run...your pick!

Oh, and don’t miss out on the Charity Solo & Team Beer Mile after the 5K is finished. All you gotta do is drink 4 beers and run 4 x400 meters Fastest individual or 2-4 person team earns the bragging rights.  

Once the fitness is over, you’ve gotta then join us across the road at the award winning Ramona Ranch Winery for a FREE wine tasting, share stores and food for purchase. If you didn’t know, Ramona Ranch is also San Diego’s only Certified Sustainable Vineyard and Winery.  

REGISTRATION INCLUDES;
- FREE Ramona Ranch wine tasting
- Finisher’s medal
- Race swag
- Ramona Radio playing tunes
- Food for purchase
- FREE Parking 

*Packet pick-up will be onsite the day of the event from 8AM-8:45AM. The charity beer mile will follow after everyone finishes the 5K. 

A portion of the proceeds help support the life changing OPERATION REBOUND – FRONTLINE TO FINISH LINE: CAF’s Operation Rebound® program strengthens the mental and physical well-being of veterans, military personnel and first responders with permanent physical injuries by providing them opportunities to use sports and fitness to re-integrate into our communities and by empowering them through sports.

name: RANCHO SAN PASQUAL TURKEY TROT 2026
description:
Run. Walk. Gobble. Then go eat!

Start your Thanksgiving morning with your neighbors at the Rancho San Pasqual Turkey Trot!

Thanksgiving Morning • November 26, 2026 • 8:00 AM

Whether you're a serious runner, a casual walker, bringing the kids, or just looking for a fun way to earn your Thanksgiving feast, this event is for everyone. Gather your family, bring your friends, wear your best Thanksgiving spirit, and join us for a festive morning right here in our community.

🏃 THE 5K TURKEY TROT
Our 5K run/walk will wind through the community, giving you a chance to get moving, enjoy the morning, and celebrate with your neighbors. Run it, walk it, jog it, or do a little of all three. No expectations, no pressure. Just come have fun!

🦃 KIDS' GOBBLER
Our youngest turkeys can join in the fun with a short, kid-friendly run designed especially for them. Every little gobbler gets to be part of the Thanksgiving morning celebration!

🏅 REGISTER TO GET A MEDAL!
Registration helps us make sure we have enough medals and refreshments for everyone. Register before November 6th to receive a Turkey Trot medal.

❤️ A COMMUNITY TRADITION
We've been doing an informal Turkey Trot since COVID to bring neighbors together, get us moving, and start the holiday on a high note. 

Registration is FREE!

Come run. Come walk. Come gobble.

Thanksgiving Morning • November 26, 2026

We'll see you at the starting line! 🦃

description:
The REACH Foundation’s favorite tradition continues! The Shamrock ’n Run 5K & 2K is once again bringing the Placentia-Yorba Linda community together for a festive, fun-filled day in support of our students.

Since 2012, thousands of families have participated in this beloved community event—running, walking, and celebrating together—while helping raise critical funds that directly support enrichment programs and events for PYLUSD students. It’s more than a race; it’s a celebration of community, school spirit, and giving back.

Performance Medals

Medals are awarded for 1st, 2nd and 3rd for both genders in Overall and by Age Divisions.

  • Overall
  • Ages 1-8, 9-10, 11-12, 13-15, 16-18, 19-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39- 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80-84, 85-89, 90-94, 95-99

We’re excited to welcome our four-legged friends, too! 🐾 For participants planning to run or walk the 5K or 2K with their dogs, please review the Yorba Regional Park guidelines below to help ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone:

  • Dogs must be on a leash at all times while in the park
  • Leashes must be no longer than 6 feet
  • Leashes must be physical leashes (no e-collars)
  • Participants must carry doggie bags and clean up after their pets
  • Dogs should be well-socialized and comfortable in a busy race environment with runners, walkers, and spectators


Thank you for helping us keep Shamrock ’n Run safe, welcoming, and fun for all—two-legged and four-legged alike. We can’t wait to celebrate with you! 🍀

The REACH Foundation Team

name: Red, White & Blue Race
description:
Welcome to the second Red, White & Blue Race! This event benefits Code 3 Mind Health, Inc.  We are a local non-profit that provides mind health services for first responders.  

This course is along the scenic coastal trail in Fort Bragg California.  The event begins at the south coastal trail (Noyo Headlands Park) and continues north with the 5k turnaround being near the compass rose.  If you participate in the 10k run, you will continue north past historic Glass Beach, and across the Pudding Creek Trestle onto the historic Mackerricher Haul Road with the turn around being near the "silver gate" entrance.  For the half-marathon participants, the course continues along the Haul Road, through Mackerricher State Park and turning around just before the entrance to Ten Mile State Preserve.  This course is ocean front, with epic views every step of the way!  For those of you that have participated in races in this area before, it will look very much like the Whale Run course!

All runners will get a tee shirt - choice of long sleeve or short sleeve
End of race will have fruit/water and coffee.


Coffee will be available for entire event.


Finisher medals will be given to all who complete the 1/2 marathon
Medals for 1, 2, and 3 place for all age categories (copy age categories from Whale Run)
Award baskets for 1st male and female finisher in each race (1/2, 10k, 5K), filled with local goodies!


All kiddie competitors get a finisher price, but awards will be given to the first three to finish.

name: Redlands Turkey Trot
description:
Thanksgiving Day 5K run and Kids 1K run in beautiful Redlands, CA.

The race course will start at the intersection of University St. and Brockton Ave. (near University of Redlands Ted Runner Stadium) and weave through the streets in and around the University of Redlands. 

ALL PARTICIPANTS THAT REGISTER ON OR AFTER WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 25 ARE NOT GUARANTEED A T-SHIRT. 

All proceeds benefit worldwide and local charities including Phoenix Hope International and Redlands Educational Partnership Foundation. 

*NOTE ON REGISTRATION FEES: All add-ons and registration processing fees are now included in amounts shown instead of those fees showing up at the end at checkout. Price you see is the price you pay.

name: Redondo Beach Super Bowl Sunday 10k/5k
description:
For 49 years, Southern California has kicked off Super Bowl Sunday on the Redondo Beach waterfront. The course takes you past the Historic Redondo Beach Pier, the marina at King Harbor and the Wyland whale mural, with ocean breezes and perfect SoCal winter weather the whole way.

Pick your distance: 10K Run, 5K Run/Walk, 5K Stroller Walk, Big Game Challenge, Kids 1K, or the Baby Buggy 10K. Run it, walk it, or stroll it.

Then stick around for the two-day Health & Fitness Expo — food, drinks and running gear for participants and spectators alike.

Start your Super Bowl Sunday on a healthy, festive note, and still be home well before kickoff.

name: Reggie's Run 2026
description:
5K Run/Walk

(Run starting at 9am sharp. Please be there at least 30 minutes early to pick up bib)

If you knew Reggie Heard, you knew that he loved his shoes and he loved the sports he played in them. Reggie also had a soft spot for younger kids and he often took the time to make each one feel special.

The Boghosian family found a way to honor Reggie's memory by combining the things that he loved most and by creating a local nonprofit called REGGIE'S KICKS FOR KIDS. This program works to provide athletic shoes for boys and girls, of all ages, that share Reggie's passion for sports.

The program will raise funds to provide athletic shoes for youth and will be working with local sports teams and leagues to ensure kids have what they need to play their respective sports. With the funds raised through the runs of past years, Reggie's Kicks for Kids has purchased hundreds of shoes for kids.

Hope to see you again this year! Together we will continue to spread Reggie's spirit!

name: Reindeer Run 5k Fun Run
description:
Date: Sunday, December 6, 2026
Location: Civic Center/City Hall | 34009 Alvarado-Niles Road, Union City, CA
Check-In: 8:00 AM | Race Begins: 9:00 AM

The reindeer are ready to run! Grab your friends, family, and favorite holiday gear and join us this December for the Reindeer Run 5K Fun Run & Walk. This festive community event is a great way to get active, celebrate the holiday season, and race your way to the finish line!

Award medals will be presented to the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place finishers in each registration category, broken down by age group and gender: Youth Ages 12 & Under, Ages 13–17, 18–29, 30–39, 40–49, 50–59, 60–69, and 70+.

We’ll also have holiday-themed prize raffles for participants after the race!

Race shirts are not included in the registration fee and will be available as an optional add-on during registration. A limited number of shirts may be available for purchase on race day while supplies last.

Registration
Pre-registration will close prior to race weekend. Walk-up registration will be available beginning at 8:00 AM on Sunday, December 6. Please arrive early to allow enough time to check in before the 9:00 AM start.

Rain or Shine 
The Reindeer Run will take place rain or shine, so dress for the weather—and holiday attire is encouraged! Ugly sweaters, reindeer antlers, Santa hats, and other festive gear are welcome. Prizes will be given out on best dressed in holiday attire!

name: Release the Kraken 5K. 10K. 18 Miler & 50K
description:
RELEASE THE KRAKEN
April 3, 2027 | Long Beach, California
5K • 10K • 18 Mile • 50K

The Kraken has been released—and it’s calling you to the coast.

Take on a fast, scenic beachfront course at Release the Kraken, featuring distances for everyone from casual 5K runners to athletes ready to conquer 30 miles.

The 18-mile and 50K races begin at 6:30 AM and follow a six-mile loop from the start, down the beach path to Gaucho Beach at Alamitos Beach, and back.

18 Mile: Three 6-mile loops
50K: Five 6-mile loops plus One 1.07 out and back
Time limit: Six hours
Course closes: 12:30 PM
All 18-mile and 50K participants must complete their distance within the six-hour course limit.

The 5K and 10K begin at 8:00 AM, bringing even more runners—and more energy—to the beachfront course.

Race-Day Schedule

Bib Pick Up Opens: 6:00 AM
6:30 AM: 18 Mile and 30 Mile start
8:00 AM: 5K and 10K start
12:30 PM: Course closes
Your Registration Includes
Custom Release the Kraken finisher medal
Professional chip timing
Live race results
Free race photos
Course support and water stations
Finish-line celebration with DJ and MC
Overall and age-group awards
Runners, walkers, and friendly dogs are welcome in the 5K and 10K. Participants in the 18-mile and 30-mile distances should be prepared to maintain the pace required to finish by noon.

Will you escape the creature—or conquer it?

RELEASE THE KRAKEN. CHOOSE YOUR DISTANCE. CLAIM YOUR MEDAL.

name: Reservoir Dogs
description:
The Reservoir Dogs Trail Race is the first trail-running event allowed to completely circumnavigate the Briones Reservoir on the serene–and usually “permit-only”–East Bay Municipal Utility District (EBMUD) trails.Most trail runs are inherently beautiful, but this course offers more rolling open fire roads and boasts a nice progression of quintessentially East Bay environments, along with tree covered single-track and sweeping views of the watershed lands. Briones Reservoir is also one of the few EBMUD properties that has a substantial length of single-track trail. The 10K, Half Marathon and 35K courses are faster than other Inside Trail races because they have less elevation but they are consistent in a design intended to push each runner.

The Start and Finish for all races will be in the San Pablo Reservoir Visitor Center, which has a plethora of outdoor activities for all ages, including: hiking, fishing, kayaking/canoeing and picnicking.

name: Resolution Run for Coffee 5K/10K/13.1 - Roseville
description:
Resolution Run for Coffee — Roseville

New year, new goal! Start yours off right in Roseville! Choose a 5k, a 10k, or a half marathon (13.1). Whether it's your first race or your fiftieth, there's a distance for you.

The course is supported by aid stations along the way, and a DJ will keep the energy up from the start line to the finish. When you cross the line, coffee, donuts, and snacks are waiting! plus a custom wood plaque to commemorate your finish!

Race Day Schedule

7:15 AM: Arrival
7:30 AM: Check-in
8:00 AM: Race start

What to Know

  • Choose your distance: 5k, 10k, or 13.1
  • Aid stations are available along the course
  • Coffee, donuts, and snacks provided for all finishers
  • Custom wood plaque finisher award
  • A waiver and course maps for each distance will be sent to registered participants before race day

name: Resolve2Run
description:
We would like to take this opportunity to introduce you to Resolve2Run, a 5K/10K Run/Walk. Our event will be on January 1, 2027 beginning at Chicago Park School and winding through beautiful country backroads.  Resolve2Run has become the second largest 5K/10K in the Nevada County running community. This will be the 15th year of this popular event. 

 


Our goal in this run is multi-faceted. We want to encourage the community toward better health and lifestyle habits that will last all year. The funds raised benefit the Peardale-Chicago Park Firefighters Association, Chicago Park 4-H Club, and Chicago Park School PTA. We would like you to join us in meeting these important goals! 

 


Sponsorship can be at various levels. Please see the attached chart detailing the

advantages of each level. We thank you in advance for your generosity! You are the foundation on which we are building this annual event for our community. We look forward to hearing from you!

name: Ride Santa Barbara 100
description:
Ride Santa Barbara returns for its 15th year!

RideSB100 offers four distinct courses to suit a range of cycling abilities – each course offering a world-class Santa Barbara cycling experience! 🚵🏻‍♂️

All courses start along the beach and follow the beautiful Santa Barbara beachfront before turning inland to experience all Santa Barbara has to offer. Cyclists will wind through some of the most exclusive neighborhoods in the country; experience the rolling foothills lined with citrus and avocado orchards and climb some of the most famous mountains in the country, all while experiencing some of the most beautiful views in southern California.

 

All cyclists will receive:

  • Official 2026 RideSB100 t-shirt
  • Official 2026 RideSB100 water bottle
  • Official RideSB100 drawstring bag with sponsor goodies
  • Fully supported aid stations
  • Mechanical support
  • Finish Line Festival with lots of food and beer
  • All Gibraltar Challenge finishers will receive a coin at the top of the hill.
  • Age group medals for Gibraltar Challenge
  • Option to buy event Jersey
  • And more!

All riders will receive an overall chip time and riders who participate in the Gibraltar Challenge will be ranked for the King and Queen of the Mountain (KOM/QOM) Jersey awards! 

 

RIDES*

 

100 mile

  • Over 9,700′ of climbing | Start Time: 7:00 AM
  • Recommended for experienced cyclists only 
  • Tackle a challenging ride that begins at Chase Palm Park, rolls through Carpinteria, and continues into the scenic Lake Casitas region. Climb Toro Canyon and Ladera Lane before testing your legs on the Gibraltar Climb Challenge, a timed 6.1-mile ascent with an 8% grade and over 2,500 ft of elevation gain. Descend, then join the 100KM Coastal Route along Cathedral Oaks through Isla Vista and past UCSB, finishing back at Chase Palm Park.

name: Ride the Point
description:
Ride the hidden, unridden, and forbidden San Diego to support pancreatic cancer research! 

Cycle through scenic areas of San Diego on November 7th to support pancreatic cancer research in the 13th Annual Jim Krause Memorial Charity Cycling Ride the Point. The ride starts and ends at Liberty Station and includes exclusive routes through Point Loma, Ocean Beach, Mission Bay La Jolla, Torrey Pines, and Sorrento Valley. This ride takes participants through historic neighborhoods and past some of the most scenic areas of San Diego, some that are only open once a year for this event. The event has volunteers along the route, SAG, and five fully stocked rest stops to support the riders.   

Ride the Point has three distances to accommodate diverse levels of cycling experience. The 5-mile Family Fun Ride is a relatively flat course on bike paths along beautiful San Diego Bay and is perfect for cruisers, beginning riders, challenged athletes, and families. The 25 and Metric Century are street rides with exclusive routes and challenging climbs around scenic San Diego. This is a boutique ride limited to 600 riders to ensure an unforgettable experience. The public is invited to the free healthy lifestyle expo at Oggi’s in Liberty Station from 9 am until 2 pm with local vendors, music, and refreshments.

name: Ridge Creek Run Club 12 Hour Ultra
description:
Challenge yourself on one of the most unique ultra-running courses in the Central Valley! The Ridge Creek 12-Hour Ultra takes place at the beautiful Ridge Creek Dinuba Golf Club, featuring a scenic 3-mile loop winding through rolling fairways, cart paths, lakes, and picturesque golf course views. Surrounded by the Sierra foothills and orchards of the Valley, Ridge Creek offers a peaceful yet challenging setting for runners of all abilities.

Whether you're chasing your first ultra distance, aiming for a personal best, or seeing just how many miles you can accumulate in 12 hours, this event is designed for you. Complete as many 3-mile loops as you can before time expires. A fully stocked aid station located near the start/finish area will keep you fueled and hydrated throughout the day, while friends and family enjoy easy access to cheer you on lap after lap.

The course combines gentle rolling terrain with beautiful scenery, creating an enjoyable loop that remains engaging from the first mile to the last. Every lap brings you back through the event hub where you'll find aid, encouragement, and the camaraderie that makes ultra running special.

Whether your goal is 15 miles, 30 miles, 50K, 50 miles, or beyond, the Ridge Creek 12-Hour Ultra is your opportunity to test your limits in a welcoming atmosphere and unforgettable venue.

Event Highlights

  • 12-hour timed ultra
  • Scenic 3-mile loop course
  • Individual ultra-running challenge
  • Fully stocked aid station
  • Real-time lap and mileage tracking
  • Finisher award for all participants
  • Special awards for top male and female mileage totals
  • Beautiful golf course setting with rolling terrain and lake views

Come experience the beauty of Ridge Creek, the support of the ultra-running community, and the satisfaction of seeing just how far you can go in 12 hours.

name: Ring Out the Old – 5K, 10K, Half Marathon
description:
Join us for the celebratory Ring out the Old race and let's kick 2026 to the curb together!

Race Details

Location: Woodley Park, 6076 Woodley Ave, Encino, CA
Parking: Free parking in the lot; more is available on Woodley Ave

Event Schedule

6:20am – Bib pick-up opens
7:00am – Half marathon & 10k start
7:30am – 5k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10k)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Courses (rain routes)

5k route: Runners do one loops around the lake – route here
10k route: Runners do two loops around the lake with a little extra – route here
Half Marathon: Route is around the park, done twice and then one of the 10k route loops – route here

More about the Course
The race routes go across the grass, under the road through a tunnel, and enter the Lake Balboa Park area. Route will be finalized week of race, rain-pending

Our courses are on open paths so please be considerate of other park users!

On-Course Support
Multiple water stations are located along the routes. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, and other snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk and runner turn signs

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Medals: All runners receive a finishing medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, Santa Monica, San Diego, the San Fernando Valley, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

name: Rise Up and Run 5K
description:
Valley Health Foundation, in partnership with the County of Santa Clara Reentry Resource Center, is hosting a 5K run/walk to raise money to support the immediate needs of justice-involved people (clothing, food, hygiene, transportation, etc.). The in-person 5K will take place on Saturday, October 17th at Hellyer County Park with a race start time of 9:00AM. Participants who choose the virtual option can run or walk the race on the day and time of their choice between October 17, 2026, and October 31, 2026. Runners will receive a Rise Up and Run race shirt and medal. 

Packet pickup information will be coming soon.  

Help support this effort by registering for the race, sponsoring other participants to run or donating to buy new clothes for those reentering our community from jail or prison. Many of these individuals have no clean clothes in which to start their reentry journey.  

Here are some ways you can help:

  • Register and run the race!
  • Sponsor a race registration for an individual or a family.
  • Donate monetarily to buy new clothes for individuals released from custody.
  • Buy or donate new clothes for reentry clients leaving custody.

Every day at the County of Santa Clara Reentry Resource Center we see clients ready to make dramatic changes in their lives. But having a felony record can be almost as restrictive as being incarcerated. Access to jobs, housing, and other opportunities becomes incredibly limited due to employment and housing restrictions and social stigma. 

Yet despite these challenges, we see clients determined to clear those hurdles. name: Rise Up and Run 5K
description:
Valley Health Foundation, in partnership with the County of Santa Clara Reentry Resource Center, is hosting a 5K run/walk to raise money to support the immediate needs of justice-involved people (clothing, food, hygiene, transportation, etc.). The in-person 5K will take place on Saturday, October 17th at Hellyer County Park with a race start time of 9:00AM. Participants who choose the virtual option can run or walk the race on the day and time of their choice between October 17, 2026, and October 31, 2026. Runners will receive a Rise Up and Run race shirt and medal. 

Packet pickup information will be coming soon.  

Help support this effort by registering for the race, sponsoring other participants to run or donating to buy new clothes for those reentering our community from jail or prison. Many of these individuals have no clean clothes in which to start their reentry journey.  

Here are some ways you can help:

  • Register and run the race!
  • Sponsor a race registration for an individual or a family.
  • Donate monetarily to buy new clothes for individuals released from custody.
  • Buy or donate new clothes for reentry clients leaving custody.

Every day at the County of Santa Clara Reentry Resource Center we see clients ready to make dramatic changes in their lives. But having a felony record can be almost as restrictive as being incarcerated. Access to jobs, housing, and other opportunities becomes incredibly limited due to employment and housing restrictions and social stigma. 

Yet despite these challenges, we see clients determined to clear those hurdles. They are taking college credit classes, working their way up from minimum wage jobs to management positions and union apprenticeships and some are entering peer mentoring and counseling professions to help those who are following in their footsteps. 

You can help support individuals who are just starting this journey to change their lives and share their talents with our community. Each person you help to rise up makes our community stronger.

name: Riverpark 5k Summer Run
description:
THE RIVERPARK 5K SUMMER RUN IS BACK!

One day. One course. One fast, fun 5K.

For the last few years, the Riverpark 5K Summer Series has brought runners together for summer racing, competition, and fun. For 2027, we’re switching things up!

Introducing the Riverpark 5K Summer Run — one big race day on Saturday, June 26, 2027!

We’re bringing back the same great course, the same competitive-but-fun atmosphere, and the same community spirit that has made the Riverpark 5K Summer Series a summer tradition — just packed into one awesome morning.

Whether you’re chasing a PR, racing your friends, getting ready for your next season, or simply looking for a fun summer 5K, there’s a place for you at the starting line.

 

WHAT YOU GET:

🏃 5K Run/Walk on our fast, familiar course
👕 Race T-shirt included with every ADULT 5K registration
⏱️ Professional live chip timing
📺 Immediate post-race results displayed digitally at the finish and online 📱 
🏆 Awards for the top 3 finishers in every age group
👟 Kids K for our youngest runners with finisher medals
🍎 Post-race refreshments and snacks
🛍️ Local vendors & community partners
🎉 A fun, family-friendly race-day atmosphere

 

REGISTRATION:

  • $25 Super Early (Oct 1- Dec 31)
  • $30 Early Bird (Jan 1- Mar 31)
  • $35 Regular Registration (Apr 1-Jun 19)
  • $40 Race Week (Jun 20- Jun 25)
  • $45 Race Day (Jun 26)

  • $10 Super Early (Oct 1- Dec 31)
  • $12 Early Bird (Jan 1- Mar 31)
  • $15 Regular Registration (Apr 1-Jun 26)

Registration prices will increase as race day gets closer, so register early and save!

Come run, have fun, and celebrate summer with us! Same course. Same energy. Get ready for the Riverpark 5K Summer Run!

name: Roasted Run 5K
description:
Roasted Run 5K ☕🔥
Get Roasted. Then Get Running.

This is not your typical 5K.

Roasted Run is where running meets coffee culture - a high-energy, feel-good morning designed for runners, walkers, first-timers, and anyone who just wants to have a great time.

Start your day with a scenic 5K, then cross the finish line into a coffee-fueled celebration with music, good vibes, and a community that doesn’t take itself too seriously.

✨ What makes Roasted Run different:

A fun, approachable 5K - run it, jog it, or walk it
Fresh coffee waiting for you at the finish ☕
Live music + post-run hangout vibes
High-energy atmosphere without the pressure
Perfect for friends, couples, and groups
Whether you’re chasing a PR or just showing up for the coffee, Roasted Run is built to be memorable, social, and something you’ll want to come back to.

So grab your crew, lace up your shoes, and get ready to start your morning the right way.

☕ Run first. Coffee after. Vibes always.

name: Robin Ames Foundation 100 Mile Solo Run
description:
Steven Epifano will be running 100 Miles Solo around San Clementer to raise money for the Robin Ames Foundation. https://www.ramesfoundation.org/

This is not a race, this page is to collect donations. You are more than welcome to join Steve on December 5th as he takes on the 100 mile challenge. Come out for any amount of miles along the beach path in San Clemente, CA.

On February 17th, 2020, Robin Ames was struck and killed by a distracted driver while returning home from a cycling ride less than a mile from his home. He was a beloved husband, father, son, brother and cherished friend to so many and missed immensely.

All funds raise will go directly to the Robin Ames Foundation.

The fundraising goal is $5000.

name: Rock & Run
description:
Lace up your running shoes and join us for one of the most unique 5K events in California.

For one day each year, Graniterock's historic Wilson Quarry opens its gates to the community, giving runners and walkers exclusive access to a working hard rock quarry that has helped build California for more than 126 years.

As you make your way through the quarry, you'll travel past towering quarry walls, ancient granite deposits formed millions of years ago and some of the largest and most impressive construction equipment on the Central Coast.

The Rock & Run 5K offers a rare behind-the-scenes look at a place few people ever get to experience.

Along the route, you'll see firsthand how Graniterock combines modern mining, environmental stewardship and responsible land management to produce the materials that build and maintain our roads, homes, schools and infrastructure.

Whether you're chasing a personal best, walking with friends and family or simply looking for a memorable outdoor adventure, Rock & Run is an experience unlike any other.

Supporting Local Schools
All proceeds from the event benefit Aromas School and San Juan Elementary School.

Event Schedule
7 a.m. – Race number pickup opens
8 a.m. – Rock & Run 5K begins
Please arrive early to pick up your race number and be ready for the start of the event.

name: Rock It in Chino Hills 5K & 10K
description:
Run it, hike it, and conquer the trails of the stunning and expansive Chino Hills State Park! Choose the 5K or 10K to challenge yourself with the beauty of trail running or hiking, all while soaking in the tranquility and scenic views, with trails stretching as far as the eye can see on most of the course. Your experience will be captured in race photos included with registration, the shirt you’ll wear with pride, and your finisher patch. Age group awards for first place finisher in age these nine age groups <9, 10-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80+. Course maps are here.  

Please note, this event may be subject to weather conditions and could be rescheduled due to rain or other event and venue restrictions. Participants will be automatically transferred to the new date, and no refunds will be provided.

Parking at California State Parks is $10 per vehicle (cashless payment only), or you can park at the nearby Carbon Canyon Park for $5. Carpooling is encouraged!

Parking at Chino Hills State Park - Discovery Center lot opens at 6:30am. Packet pick-up starts at 7:00am. The address is 4500 Carbon Canyon Road, Brea, CA 92823 - Discovery Center location.

name: Rose Bowl Turkey Trot
description:
We are back for the 9th annual Rose Bowl Turkey Trot, a family favorite tradition 5k race on Thanksgiving morning around the Rose Bowl Stadium. All are invited whether you have two legs or four! All entry fees for 2026 will be 100% tax-deductible and will go directly to the Rose Bowl Legacy Foundation. Trot before you gobble and help preserve, protect, and enhance the Rose Bowl Stadium! To learn more about the Rose Bowl Legacy Foundation and its ongoing efforts surrounding the Lasting Legacy campaign, visit https://www.rosebowllastinglegacy.org.

Each participant will have an opportunity to donate after checkout. This year, the Rose Bowl Stadium is partnering with the Pasadena Unified School District through the Pasadena Educational Foundation to provide critical financial support for athletics programs across PUSD. These funds will help expand opportunities for student-athletes and strengthen sports programming throughout the district.

The race is on Thanksgiving morning at the Rose Bowl Stadium! A timed race will go through a 3.1-mile course. All participants will receive a race bib and medal. The race will start and finish at the top of Lot K. The course itself will run around the Rose Bowl Loop. On race day bib pickup will begin at 6:30 AM. We highly encourage you to pick up your bib in advance on Wednesday, November 25th from 12:00 PM - 5:00 PM in Lot K at the Rose Bowl Stadium.  

Reminder: This race is all ages and children under the age of 12 must be accompanied by a registered parent/legal guardian at all times. 

Don’t forget to post photos of your trot and tag @rosebowlstadium and @rosebowllegacy and use hashtag #RoseBowlTurkeyTrot

name: Rotary Mission Ten - Half Marathon, 10 Mile and 5K
description:
Race Day Registration and Packet/Bib pickup begins at 7:15am on January 30th, 2027

 

This event is in its 43rd year. It is sponsored by the Rotary Club of Hollister and all proceeds go to benefit local scholarships and charities. San Juan Bautista is a small California Mission town just off Hwy 101 approximately 50 miles south of San Jose. The four races: 1/2 marathon, 10 miles, 5k and 1 Mile kids fun run, all start and finish in front of the historic and beautiful San Juan Mission. The area is rural and the course takes runners through farm land and up the Anzar hills. Medals are awarded three deep in standard age categories. The 1/2 marathon (USATF cerfitied)  and 10 mile races  are particularly good training for upcoming spring marathons. Theme teams encouraged and trophies will be awarded to top teams. (Please keep costumes family friendly)

Fees include Long sleeve dri-tech t-shirt and finisher medal. Great training for marathon base. All races except fun run timed w/awards.

name: RPV's Run For Myles
description:
Experience an unforgettable adventure along a picturesque road course with breathtaking views of the majestic Pacific Ocean. This nonprofit event starts and finishes at the Point Vicente Interpretive Center in Rancho Palos Verdes, CA, and directly benefits the preservation of the city's beautiful trails.

Participants are invited to enhance their impact by becoming individual fundraisers or by creating fundraising teams.

Bib pick up will be on Friday, January 29th, time and location TBD. Also available on race day starting at 7am. Pick up your bib on Friday to avoid lines.

If you are having someone else pick up your bib, shirt and bag, they will need two things:

1. A copy of your ID (printed on paper or on their phone)
2. A printed signed copy of the waiver. You can download and print the waiver from this link

If you are picking up your own bib, you only need to bring your ID, you can sign the waiver in person.

No bibs will be given out without ID and a signed waiver. The lawyers and our insurance company require us to be strict on this, sorry for the inconvenience.

Parking is available at two locations:

Point Vicente Interpretive Center (Until 7AM ONLY)

31501 Palos Verdes Dr W
Rancho Palos Verdes, CA 90275

Rancho Palos Verdes City Hall

30940 Hawthorne Boulevard
Rancho Palos Verdes, CA 90275
(*Shuttles will transport participants from City Hall to and from the Point Vicente Interpretive Center.)

The event kicks off at 7 AM with registration open to the public for check-in. At 7:45 AM, announcements are made, and a warm-up session takes place to prepare participants. The 10K race begins promptly at 8 AM, followed by the 5K race at 8:15 AM. At 9:45 AM, the Kids’ Fun Run race takes place. Afterward, at 10:15 AM, there are announcements and awards to recognize outstanding participants.

name: Ruff Run California
description:
Join Us here for our annual obstacle run designed for people and their pups! Over 20 obstacles and growing every year- this course will test your training, your bond and your willingness to just let loose and have great time! This 20 acre course is more than just getting dirty!!! Our obstacles range from mud and water to thinking and strategy to test your bond with your pup!! Are you a team??Every year we add more challenges!  After party with music, games and vendors! Come spend the day in the beautiful high desert at 4200 ft above sea level! 

Follow our Facebook page Ruff Run California for all the info and details as well as pics from the last event!

description:
Get ready, Colusa County, we are bringing a new community-run event to town!

RUN Colusa is Peyton Miller’s senior project, created in collaboration with the City of Colusa. This event is designed to bring our community together through miles, movement, and memories.

Whether you are a seasoned runner, a first-time 5K participant, or someone looking for a fun community experience, there will be a distance for everyone: Half Marathon, 10K, and 5K. Registration includes a t-shirt and medal! 

Start training, grab your friends and family, and get ready to be part of something special!
We are looking to make RUN Colusa more than just a race. We want it to be a full community event with runners, walkers, volunteers, supporters, and local organizations all coming together.

If you would like to sponsor a corporate team of 6 people, reach out to us through the contact button, and we will send the necessary information! 

Interested in sponsoring, volunteering, or helping make this event happen?
Reach out to us, we would LOVE to have you involved!

name: Run for a Claus presented by Optima Tax Relief
description:
The OC Marathon Presents the 13th Annual Run For a Claus 5K and Kids 1 Mile Run/Walk benefiting various charity partners as well as our own Kids Run the OC Foundation. All runners will receive a commemorative 2026 giveaway, Santa Hat, a finisher's medal and free race photos. With cookies, costumes, holiday music and decorations, this will be fun for the whole family.

When you Run for a Claus, you can Run for a Cause!

name: Run for Austin's Lungs
description:
Run for Austin’s Lungs is a family-friendly 5K walk/run held in honor of baby Austin, who is bravely battling chronic lung disease. Join us to celebrate his second birthday, raise awareness of his Chronic Lung disease, and support his ongoing medical care. Every step taken helps give Austin the breath of a brighter future.

The entire registration fee (minus the $4 processing fee) goes directly to Austin’s care. After you register, the site will ask if you’d like to make an additional donation—this can simply be left at $0, meaning your total charge will be $54 for race registration.

**Children under 15 can participate for free**

If you’d prefer to support Austin without registering for the race, you can do so by selecting the Donate button instead of Sign Up.

name: Run for Breast Cancer 5K/10K/13.1 LOS ANGELES
description:
🎀 Join the Fight: Breast Cancer Run! 🎀
Together, we can raise awareness and funds to support those affected by breast cancer. 
Enjoy a spirited day filled with community, inspiration, and hope. Let’s unite for a cause that touches us all and run for a future without breast cancer! Sign up now and help us make a lasting impact!

Forget the massive, impersonal race-day crowds. We keep things small, personal, and local, so every run feels less like a number and more like a memory. Whether it's a 5K, 10K, half-marathon, or virtual run, you'll get the warmth of a hometown event.
 

Overview:
Spots sell out FAST! We close each wave the moment it fills. Once a wave sells out, you can grab the virtual run option or join the waitlist.

This is a smaller, private group run with a capped field per wave so it never feels crowded and you're never just a bib number.
All paces and ages welcome (under 18 with a guardian) - run it, walk it, however you like!
There's no gear, no setup, no fuss - just you, the course, and our coordinators cheering you on in a relaxed, stress-free setting.
When you sign up, you're not just registering for a race - you're getting real support toward your fitness goals, plus an invite to join one of our local run clubs to keep the momentum going.
 
Timing:
Optional! Track your own time via Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, or similar, then submit it through our easy online form to get posted.  Or just ask a coordinator to help time you.
No timing chips - this is about progress, not pressure.
 
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-shirt (shipped to your address - U.S. only)
- Finisher's medal
- Virtual Training Run (emailed to you a month before your run)
- Online results & certificate of completion
- Invitation to join a local running club
- NEW: Upgrade to a lightweight, moisture-wicking technical shirt for just $5 more
 
Packet Pickup?
Skip It. No lines, no hassle - your swag ships straight to your door. (Double check your full U.S. mailing address, including apartment number, when you register as your shirt is sent to this address!) Race bibs are simply handed out on race day.
 
When Will My Swag Arrive?
Your shirt will arrive at your mailing address the week of your race.
 
Signing Up Last Minute? (Within 2 Weeks of the Race)
No problem - just note that shipping may not catch up in time, so your shirt could arrive after race day. No worries, though: wear whatever you like and come run with us anyway!
 
When Will I Receive the Course Map and Details?
We'll send final participant info by the Wednesday before race day with all the details and course maps.
 
Wave Times  (Once you've registered, use your confirmation number to reserve a wave here)
Wave A: 7:30 AM
Wave B: 8:00 AM
Wave C: 8:30 AM
 
Running Late?
Jump in when you arrive - our coordinators stay on-site for 3 hours after the first wave. Times may be subject to change depending on seasons, please check your participant info email!
Got more questions? Check our FAQ.
 
Virtual Run Option
Prefer to run on your own time? Our Virtual Run includes a digital training pack to keep you on track. Run it whenever, wherever, with any tracking device you like (optional) — then send your results to info@thebestraces.com to claim your medal.
 
Race Bundle
Sign up for multiple races and save with a bundle discount.
 
Sponsorships & Promoting Your Business
Want to put your business in front of our community? We'd love to feature you as a sponsor. Learn more.
 
Team Glo Volunteers
Love helping people cross finish lines? Join our volunteer team and help bring these community runs to life. Sign up here.
 
Be Part of the Journey
Discover our charity initiatives at https://www.thebestraces.com/runforothers/.
Got a mission that helps people around the world? Let us help you fundraise at no cost to you.
 

Your Race | Your Journey | Your Story

Who says you can't have your chocolate—and run it too? The 2027 Run for Chocolate is coming, and it’s sweeter than ever! 🎉
Rally your friends, set your pace for our 5K/10K/13.1 Half-Marathon, and let the craving guide you to the finish line. It’s not just a race; it’s a chocolate lover's paradise in motion! 🍫❤️🏃‍♀️

 
Forget the massive, impersonal race-day crowds. We keep things small, personal, and local, so every run feels less like a number and more like a memory. Whether it's a 5K, 10K, half-marathon, or virtual run, you'll get the warmth of a hometown event.
Overview:
Spots sell out FAST! We close each wave the moment it fills. Once a wave sells out, you can grab the virtual run option or join the waitlist.
This is a smaller, private group run with a capped field per wave - so it never feels crowded, and you're never just a bib number.
All paces and ages welcome (under 18 with a guardian) - run it, walk it, however you like!
There's no gear, no setup, no fuss - just you, the course, and our coordinators cheering you on in a relaxed, stress-free setting.
When you sign up, you're not just registering for a race - you're getting real support toward your fitness goals, plus an invite to join one of our local run clubs to keep the momentum going.
 
Timing:
Optional! Track your own time via Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, or similar, then submit it through our easy online form to get posted.
Or just ask a coordinator to help time you.
No timing chips - this is about progress, not pressure.
 
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-shirt (shipped to your address - US only)
- Finisher's medal
- Virtual Training Run (emailed to you a month before your run)
- Online results & certificate of completion
- Invitation to join a local running club
- NEW: Upgrade to a lightweight, moisture-wicking technical shirt for just $5 more
 
Packet Pickup?
Skip It. No lines, no hassle - your swag ships straight to your door. (Double-check your full US mailing address, including apartment number, when you register as your shirt is sent to this address!) Race bibs are simply handed out on race day.
 
When Will My Swag Arrive?
Your shirt will land at your mailing address the week of your race.
 
Signing Up Last Minute? (Within 2 Weeks of the Race)
No problem - just know shipping may not catch up in time, so your shirt could arrive after race day. No worries, though: wear whatever you like and come run with us anyway!
 
When Will I Receive get the Course Map and Details?
We'll send a final participant info by the Wednesday before race day with all the details and course maps.
 
Wave Times (Once you've registered, use your confirmation number to reserve a wave here.)
Wave A: 7:30 AM
Wave B: 8:00 AM
Wave C: 8:30 AM
Running late? Jump in when you arrive - our coordinators stay on-site for 3 hours after the first wave. Times may be subject to change depending on seasons, please check your participant info email!
Got more questions? Check our FAQ.
 
Virtual Run Option
Prefer to run on your own time? Our Virtual Run includes a digital training pack to keep you on track. Run it whenever, wherever, with any tracking device you like (optional) — then send your results to info@thebestraces.com to claim your medal.
 
Race Bundle
Sign up for multiple races and save with a bundle discount.
 
Sponsorships & Promoting Your Business
Want to put your business in front of our community? We'd love to feature you as a sponsor. Learn more
 
Team Glo Volunteers
Love helping people cross finish lines? Join our volunteer team and help bring these community runs to life. Sign up here
 
Be Part of the Journey
Discover our charity initiatives at https://www.thebestraces.com/runforothers/
Got a mission that helps people around the world? Let us help you fundraise at no cost to you.
 
Smaller Races, Warm Memories, Always Ready for You

name: RUN FOR FREEDOM
description:
Join the Movement and break some chains. This is more than just a race—it's a chance to make a lasting impact in the fight against human trafficking.

Lace up for something bigger than a finish line.
Whether you're running, walking, or cheering from the sidelines, the EDEN 5K/10K is more than a race—it's a movement. The Run for Freedom helps raise funds and awareness to support anti-trafficking organizations. Your participation fuels change, provides resources, and empowers those on the frontlines to continue to bring hope to survivors.

Tentative schedule of the day

6:00-7:00 a.m. Vendor set-up

7:00-8:30 a.m. Registration/packet pick up

8:15 a.m. Warm Up

8:30 a.m. Speakers

9:00 am 5K/10k Run/Walk

11:00-11:30 Post race speaker program

7 a.m.-12.30 p.m. Vendor Expo & Entertainment

Scenic Lakeside 5k Course

Our 5K course takes you along a beautiful lakeside road at Bonelli Regional Park, with views of sparkling Puddingstone Lake and rolling hills all around. The route features a mix of flat stretches and a few gentle inclines to keep things fun and challenging.

As you run, you’ll be surrounded by mountain backdrops, lush greenery, and open skies—perfect for an energizing morning on the move. Bonelli Park is a favorite spot for local runners, cyclists, and nature lovers, and you’ll see why: the course combines scenic beauty with a welcoming, race-day atmosphere.

Whether you’re walking, jogging, or aiming for a personal record, this course offers a little bit of everything—lake views, shady sections, rolling terrain, and plenty of inspiration.

Scenic Lakeside 10k Course

Our 10K course begins on the same scenic lakeside road as the 5K, letting you take in the sparkling waters of Puddingstone Lake and the mountain views that make Bonelli Park so special.

At the halfway point, the course branches off to bring you onto park trails and rolling hills, adding a little more adventure and challenge. You’ll experience a blend of paved paths, natural terrain, and inclines that keep things exciting while still being very runnable.

With the combination of lake views, shaded sections, open trails, and mountain backdrops, the 10K is a rewarding course for both seasoned runners and those looking to push themselves a bit further.

Come ready for a mix of beauty and challenge—the 10K at Bonelli Park offers an unforgettable run surrounded by nature.

VIRTUAL 5K/10K—RUN FROM ANYWHERE

Can’t join us in San Dimas? You can still be part of the movement through the Run for Freedom Virtual Race.

Complete a 5K or 10K wherever you are—around your neighborhood, on a favorite trail, at a local park, or on a treadmill. Want to make a bigger impact? Invite your running club, church, company, real estate office, gym, friends, or family to participate together and lead a Run for Freedom group from wherever you live.

Your participation supports EDEN’s work creating sustainable funding for organizations fighting human trafficking.

       How the virtual race works:

  • Register for the Run for Freedom Virtual Race.
  • Choose your own 5K or 10K route.
  • Complete your distance between now and November 7, 2026.
  • Share your experience and submit your results on social by using #RunForFreedomVIRTUAL and tagging @restoringedentogether
  • Race items will be mailed starting 10/31/26 / mailed after the event / and available for pickup. Please confirm your mailing address during registration.

All Registrations Includes:
Race bib
Event shirt
Finisher’s medal

 

RAIN OR SHINE and NO REFUNDS

name: Run for Hope
description:
The Sierra Cascades Run for Hope is a meaningful community event created to bring people together in support, remembrance, and hope. This run represents every stage of the cancer journey-those currently in treatment, showing extraordinary courage each day; the survivors whose strength inspires others; the loved ones who remain forever part of our lives; and the families and caregivers who stand beside them through it all.

On this day participants don’t just show up to run or walk. They show up for someone.…for a Friend…for a Parent…for a Child…for Themselves. Each step becomes more than movement-it becomes a symbol of support, strength, and unity. 

Run for Hope creates a space where the community comes together to lift one another, share encouragement, and stand side by side in a way that reminds every person they are not alone in their journey.

With distances welcoming both runners and walkers of all ages and abilities, this event is open to everyone who wants to be a part of something meaningful. Because Run for Hope is not defined by finish times, but by the people, stories, and hearts that move together.

This is Sierra Cascades Run for Hope. A Run with purpose, a community united, a day that reminds us all what Hope looks like in motion.

name: Run for Mental Health 5K/10K/13.1 LOS ANGELES
description:
Join the Movement for Mental Health!
Introducing the "Run for Mental Health" - an empowering journey towards well-being! Run with purpose, run with heart for someone you know who is on that difficult journey like all of us. 
Let's break the stigma and stride towards a healthier mind! Your run can make a difference! 💙

 

Forget the massive, impersonal race-day crowds. We keep things small, personal, and local, so every run feels less like a number and more like a memory. Whether it's a 5K, 10K, half-marathon, or virtual run, you'll get the warmth of a hometown event.
 

Overview:
Spots sell out FAST! We close each wave the moment it fills. Once a wave sells out, you can grab the virtual run option or join the waitlist.

This is a smaller, private group run with a capped field per wave so it never feels crowded and you're never just a bib number.
All paces and ages welcome (under 18 with a guardian) - run it, walk it, however you like!
There's no gear, no setup, no fuss - just you, the course, and our coordinators cheering you on in a relaxed, stress-free setting.
When you sign up, you're not just registering for a race - you're getting real support toward your fitness goals, plus an invite to join one of our local run clubs to keep the momentum going.
 
Timing:
Optional! Track your own time via Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, or similar, then submit it through our easy online form to get posted.  Or just ask a coordinator to help time you.
No timing chips - this is about progress, not pressure.
 
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-shirt (shipped to your address - U.S. only)
- Finisher's medal
- Virtual Training Run (emailed to you a month before your run)
- Online results & certificate of completion
- Invitation to join a local running club
- NEW: Upgrade to a lightweight, moisture-wicking technical shirt for just $5 more
 
Packet Pickup?
Skip It. No lines, no hassle - your swag ships straight to your door. (Double check your full U.S. mailing address, including apartment number, when you register as your shirt is sent to this address!) Race bibs are simply handed out on race day.
 
When Will My Swag Arrive?
Your shirt will arrive at your mailing address the week of your race.
 
Signing Up Last Minute? (Within 2 Weeks of the Race)
No problem - just note that shipping may not catch up in time, so your shirt could arrive after race day. No worries, though: wear whatever you like and come run with us anyway!
 
When Will I Receive the Course Map and Details?
We'll send final participant info by the Wednesday before race day with all the details and course maps.
 
Wave Times  (Once you've registered, use your confirmation number to reserve a wave here)
Wave A: 7:30 AM
Wave B: 8:00 AM
Wave C: 8:30 AM
 
Running Late?
Jump in when you arrive - our coordinators stay on-site for 3 hours after the first wave. Times may be subject to change depending on seasons, please check your participant info email!
Got more questions? Check our FAQ.
 
Virtual Run Option
Prefer to run on your own time? Our Virtual Run includes a digital training pack to keep you on track. Run it whenever, wherever, with any tracking device you like (optional) — then send your results to info@thebestraces.com to claim your medal.
 
Race Bundle
Sign up for multiple races and save with a bundle discount.
 
Sponsorships & Promoting Your Business
Want to put your business in front of our community? We'd love to feature you as a sponsor. Learn more.
 
Team Glo Volunteers
Love helping people cross finish lines? Join our volunteer team and help bring these community runs to life. Sign up here.
 
Be Part of the Journey
Discover our charity initiatives at https://www.thebestraces.com/runforothers/.
Got a mission that helps people around the world? Let us help you fundraise at no cost to you.
 

Your Race | Your Journey | Your Story

name: RUN FOR PIE 2026
description:
NOVEMBER 26th, 2026

Sponsored by: Brooks Running & Beckmann's

Come join us on Thanksgiving morning for our 13th annual Thanksgiving Day race! Run For Pie has become one of Santa Cruz County's favorite holiday traditions. Bring the whole family (or your pet turkey) out to run or walk a 5K. Run for Pie also includes a 1/2 mile Turkey Chase Race for kids. All participants get a slice of pumpkin pie at the finish. This event will benefit the Second Harvest Food Bank and the Soquel High School Track Team. With the high demand for this race every year, we have decided to cap registrations, so be sure to register your friends and family before our race sells out! 

Kids 1/2 Mile: All proceeds from this race will go to Second Harvest Food Bank. We are hoping to donate over 12,000 meals this year!

How to register for the Pie Mile Relay: The relay will consist of 4 individuals and each individual will need to register. When you are registering for this specific race, place your first name and next to your last name place your team name. This way we can keep track of full teams. 

Race Start Times: 

Kids 1/2 Mile: 8:35 am 

5k Start Time: 9:05 am 

Pie Mile Relay Start Time: 10:15 am 

Pricing Update:

Why the random price? Due to the new California Price Transparency Act, we are required to show the price with processing fees added. The price that it is displaying is the $45 + processing fee. We are sorry for any confusion. If you have any questions, please reach out to the race director, amber.melville@fleetfeet.com.

Race Shirt Details: 

You can purchase a t-shirt during registration for $5. 

Volunteer Form:

Want to be part of the Thanksgiving morning fun? Join our amazing Run For Pie volunteer team! From cheering on runners to serving up slices of pie at the finish line, our volunteers make this community tradition possible. Volunteer Form Coming Soon! 

Questions: 

If you have any questions regarding Fleet Feet Aptos 13th Annual Run For Pie race, please reach out to the Race Director, Amber Melville (amber.melville@fleetfeet.com).

name: Run for Roots: Heard It Through the Grapevine
description:
Building Community Together

🍇 Heard It Through the Grapevine… Fresno Is Running Like a Raisin! 🍇

Highway City Community Development (HCCD) invites you to the 2nd Annual Run for Roots 5K – “Heard It Through the Grapevine” Edition, where runners, walkers, families, and costumed raisins come together to celebrate West Fresno’s community, culture, and agricultural legacy.

This year’s race honors our area’s deep roots in agriculture—and a fun piece of Fresno history. Participants are encouraged to dress as raisins or “Raisin Eaters,” inspired by Fresno’s first professional baseball team from 1906. Set against the iconic vineyards of Kearney Park, this run is playful, meaningful, and uniquely Fresno.

Whether you’re chasing a personal best, walking with friends, or racing in full raisin costume, Run for Roots is about more than the finish line—it’s about celebrating who we are and where we come from.

Why We Run (It’s Bigger Than the Finish Line)

Since 1998, HCCD has been planting seeds of opportunity and cultivating resident leadership right here in West Fresno and the West of 99 / Central Unified area.

In 2025 alone, HCCD:

  • Served 10,000+ community members through classes, workshops, outreach and community events
  • Supported nearly 1,000 families during moments of crisis
  • Expanded access to food assistance, care navigation, education, housing advocacy, health resources, arts & culture, and community development

Your participation helps sustain a place where community, culture, agriculture, and families can grow—together.

*Note the race will occur rain or shine.

name: Run For The Brains!
description:
Come One, Come All to the Halloween Spooktacular!

Formerly known as the Brain Health to Beat Stroke, this event is a fang-tastic 5K, 10K, and 1K that raises funds and awareness for strokes. Don't let your loved ones become zombies—join us for a monstrously good time!

Why Participate?

Healings in Motion provides local educational programs and services supporting brain health, stroke awareness, and prevention. Your participation and donations will increase stroke awareness in our community, help reduce the number of strokes, and directly support those with stroke recovery. It's a grave cause we're passionate about! For more information, visit https://www.healingsinmotion.org

The Courses

5K - A Closed Course (No Ghouls Allowed!)

All runners will start on Ben Holt Drive in the heart of the Lincoln Center. We'll head West toward Lincoln High School, then make our way back to the finish line where you'll be greeted by a ghoulishly good time! Expect themed music, trick-or-treating, thriller dance competitions, and tons of great goodies from the community. It's going to be un-boo-lievable!

5K Virtual - Run, Walk, or Roll Your Way!

Participate where you want, when you want between October 30th–November 1st! Send us a screenshot of your path from Strava, Nike Run Club, Garmin, or any other fitness tracker via Instagram or email us at brainhealth5K@gmail.com. While your results won't appear with our in-person participants, we'd love to see your spooky selfies and post them on our socials. No coffin required!

1-Mile Survivor Champion Walk or Roll

We'll make our way around the North side of Lincoln Center! For stroke survivors and others recovering from a brain injury, this is your chance to participate at any level of ability. We all know someone affected by stroke—honor them by joining us or donating in their honor. Because when it comes to supporting survivors, we don't ghost anyone!

Fees

  • 5K & 10K: May 1st - $35 | August 1st - $40 | September 1st - $45 | October 1st - $50 | October 30th - $55
  • 5K Virtual: $5.00 if you'd like your Goodie Bag mailed (no boo-gies for staying home!)
  • Champion Walk - Individual: May 1st - $35 | June 1st - $40 | July 1st - $45 | Free to all Survivors

All fees include a finisher medal, brain freeze ice cream, a timed race bib, and an event t-shirt. Talk about a sweet deal—it's not just a treat, it's a trick-or-treat!

Packet Pickup

Early Pickup: Fleet Feet Stockton, 265 Lincoln Center, Friday, October 30th from 10am to 5pm. Don't be a skeleton crew—pick up early!

Race Day Pickup: 6am at the Skedaddle Registration tent. We promise not to boo you if you're running late!

Awards

5K & 10K In-Person: Overall male/female winners in age group categories: 12 & under, 13-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80+

name: Run for the Fallen 10K-5K at Merced College
description:
SUNDAY, NOVEMBER 8th at MERCED COLLEGE

                                      400m Kids Race is back this year!  Starts at 8:20am.

Opening Ceremonies begin at 8:30am. 5K/10K starts at 9:00am... RAIN or SHINE.      

On Flag Day, June 14, 2008, a dedicated team of runners participated in the first Run for the Fallen and ran 4100 miles across America from Fort Irwin, CA to Arlington National Cemetery, one mile for every Soldier, Sailor, Airmen, and Marine killed since the War on Terror began. In 2018 on its tenth anniversary Honor and Remember expanded the initial run by creating America’s Run for the Fallen, the most comprehensive fallen veteran tribute to date. April 7th - August 5th, covering 6,000 miles over 120 days through 19 states honoring over 20,000 service members.

Each year since the first run across America, runners from around the world have joined Run for the Fallen in remembering our fallen. Over 50,000+ participants and over 200,000+ miles have been collectively run in remembrance of those heroes, organized in over 26 states.  Help us keep the memory of our local fallen heroes alive by joining us at Merced College on Sunday, November 8th.

The Merced Sunrise Rotary Club would like to invite you, your family, and your friends to this year’s Run for the Fallen and Field of Honor events.  On Sunday, November 8th, the running events start at 8:20am with the Kids 400m Fun Run.  All kids get a finisher's medal!  The 5K Run/Walk & 10K Run will start at 9am.  The start and finish will take place near the main lawn where the Field of Honor is located at Merced College near M St./Yosemite Ave.  All participants will be chip-timed and eligible to receive a 1st, 2nd, or 3rd Place medal in all male and female Age-groups.  Those Age-groups are: 10 & under, 11-13, 14-18, 19-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, and 70+.  Commemorative t-shirts will be sold for $25 on race day and only while supplies last, with all proceeds donated to the Merced Field of Honor.  We thank you for your support, in advance.

All participants are invited to attend a short ceremony at 8:45am where our local fallen heroes will be honored.  That will be followed by the 5K/10K at 9am.  You may register on race day from 7:00am to 8:30am.  All those that pre-register must pick up their bibs between 7:00am-8:30am. To view the course map, click on the link below.   

Stay safe and we hope you will join us.  See you at the race!

name: Run for the Planet – 5K, 10K, 10M, and Half Marathon
description:
The annual High Tide Runs Earth Day celebration is here! Join us for a thrilling celebration of loving our planet, environmental stewardship, and movement!

Details
Start Location: Long Beach
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free. See map at the bottom of this email.

Event Schedule

Friday
4:00-6:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email race week)

Saturday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners and 10-milers only, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Course
Courses will be run along the beach path in Long Beach

More about the Course
The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support: A fully stocked water station is located along the course. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Awards: All finishers earn a race medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance.
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, San Diego, the San Fernando Valley, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule.

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

name: Run In The New Year 5k/10K/Half Marathon
description:
It's SoCal's HEALTHIEST LIVE PARTY!  LIVE BAND at  the START/FINISH and  the course! It's YOUR NEW YEAR'S CELEBRATION. WITH New Year's BLING!

Friday, Jan. 1, 2027

  • 8:30 am Half Marathon Start

  • 8:40 am Kid's Dash

  • 9:00 am 5k/10K Mass Start

Early Packet Pick-Up: We encourage you to pick up the day prior

    • TBD

    • Packet pick-up is optional, so if you cannot make it- don't worry. Packets can be picked up on race day starting at 7 am in LOT 25. The gates to the STATE PARK open at 7am.

Write a New Year resolution on the back of your bib and RUN, JOG, or WALK it into the new year. 

The course is the flat and fast, paved, wide State Park path, watching and listening to the surf.! Whether an avid runner, jogger, first-timer, or walker, we are the something for every BODY & EVERYBODY best-themed race! Bring family and friends, or just yourself and shoes! Let's get 2024 off and  RUNNING. 

  Entry comes with a Run In The New Year CUSTOM 5K/10K T-Shirt

  Special LONG SLEEVE DESIGN T-shirt for Half Marathon Finishers

  And, a huge CUSTOM CAST finisher medal to all! HUGE!!

Make it a Post-race 5K/10K resolution party ( New Year's Beanies will be for sale at the t-shirt table.)

GEAR CHECK is available, if needed, at the Caren Ware Events BOOTH.  Put your bib number on a tag and pin to your gear.  

Professionally CHIP timed event by ITZ ABOUT TIME. Age division awards galore!

Entrance to Bolsa Chica State Park.

The event is in the farthest western lot- Lot 25, closest to Warner & PCH, but to enter the park use the following address: 17851 Pacific Coast Hwy.

Race Day Schedule:

  • 6:00 am: Gates Open
  • 7:00 am: Race Day Packet Pick-Up Begins (Lot 25)
  • 8:00 am Half Marathon Start for those that will take more than 3 hours and 45 minutes to finish
  • 8:30 am: Half Marathon Start (Must cross the starting arch by 8:05 am)
  • 8:40 am: Kid’s Dash
  • 9:00am: 5K/10K Mass Start (Must cross the starting arch by 9:05 am)
  • 9:40am: 5K Awards Ceremony begins.
  • 10:00 am 10K awards
  • 10:30 announcing of overall Half marathon awards

8:30 am start for HALF MARATHON.  You have until 8:35 to pass under the arch.  9:00am start for 5k/10K.  You have until 9:05 am to pass under the arch.  All 5k/10K must start before the lead half marathoner finishes.   YOUR START TIME does not start until you cross under the arch. Fastest runners in the front, and those looking to place in their age group division. Wear your bib on the front.  Make sure you run the distance on your bib or exchange it for the correct one of your choice at the Solutions/Late registration table if you decide to change races.

SPECIAL PANCAKE BREAKFAST!!!! You can add pancakes to your registration on the last page...

Visit the Speciality Coffee Booth, Fresh baked cookies (GALLETINAS BOOTH),  fresh cut fruits,  and street tacos and tamales will be there.

Awards:

There are “In It To Win It” age categories 3 deep with 5 year age spans: 1-10, 11-14, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39 40-44, 45-49, 50-54,55-59 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80-84 and 85 & over.

Course

Flat and fast, or slow and easy, make it the pace you want it. This 5K/10K course runs along the beach bike path at Bolsa Chica, Huntington Beach State Beach. Families can bring strollers but agree to use at their own risk.  Half Marathon Course: Flat, fast, perfect for PRs or training for your next marathon.  It is (2)Two loops of the 10k so you get plenty of aid stations, entertainment, and spectator friendly!! Aid Station Every 1.5 Miles

  • Water/Gatorade
  • Chargel/ Bananas  

FLAT!!! Great for first-time Half Marathoners or those wanting to PR!
Half Marathon Spectators - you can be at the finish line to see runners start then walk about 50 ft towards the runners to see them go on their second loop.

Restrooms:

Restrooms on RACE DAY: are located at each end of the parking lot.  A set by Sea Legs (east) and a set near  Warner Blvd on the west end of the parking lot.
